  34class Clustering:
  35    """
  36    A class for performing dimensionality reduction, clustering, and visualization
  37    on high-dimensional data (e.g., single-cell gene expression).
  38
  39    The class provides methods for:
  40    - Normalizing and extracting subsets of data
  41    - Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and related clustering
  42    - Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) and clustering
  43    - Visualization of PCA and UMAP embeddings
  44    - Harmonization of batch effects
  45    - Accessing processed data and cluster labels
  46
  47    Methods
  48    -------
  49    add_data_frame(data, metadata)
  50        Class method to create a Clustering instance from a DataFrame and metadata.
  51
  52    harmonize_sets()
  53        Perform batch effect harmonization on PCA data.
  54
  55    perform_PCA(pc_num=100, width=8, height=6)
  56        Perform PCA on the dataset and visualize the first two PCs.
  57
  58    knee_plot_PCA(width=8, height=6)
  59        Plot the cumulative variance explained by PCs to determine optimal dimensionality.
  60
  61    find_clusters_PCA(pc_num=0, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6, harmonized=False)
  62        Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize results.
  63
  64    perform_UMAP(factorize=False, umap_num=100, pc_num=0, harmonized=False, ...)
  65        Compute UMAP embeddings with optional parameter tuning.
  66
  67    knee_plot_umap(eps=0.5, min_samples=10)
  68        Determine optimal UMAP dimensionality using silhouette scores.
  69
  70    find_clusters_UMAP(umap_n=5, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6)
  71        Apply DBSCAN clustering on UMAP embeddings and visualize clusters.
  72
  73    UMAP_vis(names_slot='cell_names', set_sep=True, point_size=0.6, ...)
  74        Visualize UMAP embeddings with labels and optional cluster numbering.
  75
  76    UMAP_feature(feature_name, features_data=None, point_size=0.6, ...)
  77        Plot a single feature over UMAP coordinates with customizable colormap.
  78
  79    get_umap_data()
  80        Return the UMAP embeddings along with cluster labels if available.
  81
  82    get_pca_data()
  83        Return the PCA results along with cluster labels if available.
  84
  85    return_clusters(clusters='umap')
  86        Return the cluster labels for UMAP or PCA embeddings.
  87
  88    Raises
  89    ------
  90    ValueError
  91        For invalid parameters, mismatched dimensions, or missing metadata.
  92    """

  94    def __init__(self, data, metadata):
  95        """
  96        Initialize the clustering class with data and optional metadata.
  97
  98        Parameters
  99        ----------
 100        data : pandas.DataFrame
 101            Input data for clustering. Columns are considered as samples.
 102
 103        metadata : pandas.DataFrame, optional
 104            Metadata for the samples. If None, a default DataFrame with column
 105            names as 'cell_names' is created.
 106
 107        Attributes
 108        ----------
 109        -clustering_data : pandas.DataFrame
 110        -clustering_metadata : pandas.DataFrame
 111        -subclusters : None or dict
 112        -explained_var : None or numpy.ndarray
 113        -cumulative_var : None or numpy.ndarray
 114        -pca : None or pandas.DataFrame
 115        -harmonized_pca : None or pandas.DataFrame
 116        -umap : None or pandas.DataFrame
 117        """
 118
 119        self.clustering_data = data
 120        """The input data used for clustering."""
 121
 122        if metadata is None:
 123            metadata = pd.DataFrame({"cell_names": list(data.columns)})
 124
 125        self.clustering_metadata = metadata
 126        """Metadata associated with the samples."""
 127
 128        self.subclusters = None
 129        """Placeholder for storing subcluster information."""
 130
 131        self.explained_var = None
 132        """Explained variance from PCA, initialized as None."""
 133
 134        self.cumulative_var = None
 135        """Cumulative explained variance from PCA, initialized as None."""
 136
 137        self.pca = None
 138        """PCA-transformed data, initialized as None."""
 139
 140        self.harmonized_pca = None
 141        """PCA data after batch effect harmonization, initialized as None."""
 142
 143        self.umap = None
 144        """UMAP embeddings, initialized as None."""

 147    def add_data_frame(cls, data: pd.DataFrame, metadata: pd.DataFrame | None):
 148        """
 149        Create a Clustering instance from a DataFrame and optional metadata.
 150
 151        Parameters
 152        ----------
 153        data : pandas.DataFrame
 154            Input data with features as rows and samples/cells as columns.
 155
 156        metadata : pandas.DataFrame or None
 157            Optional metadata for the samples.
 158            Each row corresponds to a sample/cell, and column names in this DataFrame
 159            should match the sample/cell names in `data`. Columns can contain additional
 160            information such as cell type, experimental condition, batch, sets, etc.
 161
 162        Returns
 163        -------
 164        Clustering
 165            A new instance of the Clustering class.
 166        """
 167
 168        return cls(data, metadata)

 170    def sort_data(
 171        self,
 172        value_to_sort: str,
 173        ascending: bool = True,
 174        sort_order: list | None = None,
 175    ):
 176        """
 177        Sort metadata and synchronize all associated data matrices and embeddings.
 178
 179        This method reorders sample metadata based on a specified column and
 180        propagates the new sample order across all initialized data slots
 181        (e.g., expression matrices, PCA, harmonized PCA, and UMAP embeddings).
 182
 183        Parameters
 184        ----------
 185        value_to_sort : str
 186            Name of the metadata column used as the sorting key.
 187
 188        ascending : bool, default=True
 189            Sort ascending vs. descending. Ignored if `sort_order` is provided
 190            unless reversed sorting of the custom order is intended.
 191
 192        sort_order : list or None, default=None
 193            Explicit list defining the exact custom order of unique categories
 194            in `value_to_sort`. Must contain the exact same unique values as
 195            the target column.
 196
 197        Raises
 198        ------
 199        ValueError
 200            If `value_to_sort` does not exist in the metadata columns, or if
 201            `sort_order` does not match the unique values present in the column.
 202        """
 203
 204        # methode part for COMPsc project
 205        if "input_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
 206            if value_to_sort not in self.input_metadata.columns:
 207                available_cols = list(self.input_metadata.columns)
 208                raise ValueError(
 209                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in input_metadata. "
 210                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
 211                )
 212
 213            # step 1
 214            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.input_metadata))
 215            self.input_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 216
 217            if self.normalized_data is not None:
 218                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
 219
 220            if self.input_data is not None:
 221                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
 222
 223            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 224                unique_vals = set(self.input_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 225                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 226                    unique_vals
 227                ):
 228                    self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 229                        self.input_metadata[value_to_sort],
 230                        categories=sort_order,
 231                        ordered=True,
 232                    )
 233                    self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
 234                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 235                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 236                else:
 237                    raise ValueError(
 238                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 239                    )
 240            else:
 241                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
 242                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 243                ).reset_index(drop=True)
 244
 245            new_order = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 246
 247            if self.normalized_data is not None:
 248                self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 249                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
 250
 251            if self.input_data is not None:
 252                self.input_data = self.input_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 253                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
 254
 255            self.input_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 256            self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.input_metadata[
 257                value_to_sort
 258            ].astype(str)
 259
 260            # step 2
 261            if self.agg_metadata is not None:
 262                sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.agg_metadata))
 263                self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 264
 265                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
 266                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"]
 267
 268                if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 269                    unique_vals = set(self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 270                    if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 271                        unique_vals
 272                    ):
 273                        self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 274                            self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort],
 275                            categories=sort_order,
 276                            ordered=True,
 277                        )
 278                        self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
 279                            value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 280                        ).reset_index(drop=True)
 281                    else:
 282                        raise ValueError(
 283                            "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 284                        )
 285                else:
 286                    self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
 287                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 288                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 289
 290                new_order = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 291
 292                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
 293                    self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.iloc[
 294                        :, new_order
 295                    ]
 296                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["cell_names"]
 297
 298                self.agg_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 299                self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.agg_metadata[
 300                    value_to_sort
 301                ].astype(str)
 302
 303        # method for Clustering
 304
 305        if "clustering_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
 306            if value_to_sort not in self.clustering_metadata.columns:
 307                available_cols = list(self.clustering_metadata.columns)
 308                raise ValueError(
 309                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in clustering_metadata. "
 310                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
 311                )
 312
 313            # step 1
 314            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.clustering_metadata))
 315            self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 316
 317            if (
 318                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
 319                and self.clustering_data is not None
 320            ):
 321                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 322
 323            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
 324                tmp_pca = self.pca
 325                tmp_pca.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 326
 327            if (
 328                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
 329                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
 330            ):
 331                tmp_pca_harmonize = self.harmonized_pca
 332                tmp_pca_harmonize.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 333
 334            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
 335                tmp_umap = self.umap
 336                tmp_umap.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 337
 338            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 339                unique_vals = set(self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 340                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 341                    unique_vals
 342                ):
 343                    self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 344                        self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort],
 345                        categories=sort_order,
 346                        ordered=True,
 347                    )
 348                    self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
 349                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 350                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 351                else:
 352                    raise ValueError(
 353                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 354                    )
 355            else:
 356                self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
 357                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 358                ).reset_index(drop=True)
 359
 360            new_order = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 361
 362            if (
 363                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
 364                and self.clustering_data is not None
 365            ):
 366                self.clustering_data = self.clustering_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 367                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["cell_names"]
 368
 369            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
 370                tmp_pca = tmp_pca.loc[new_order, :]
 371                self.pca = tmp_pca.reset_index(drop=True)
 372                del tmp_pca
 373
 374            if (
 375                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
 376                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
 377            ):
 378                tmp_pca_harmonize = tmp_pca_harmonize.loc[new_order, :]
 379                self.harmonized_pca = tmp_pca_harmonize.reset_index(drop=True)
 380                del tmp_pca_harmonize
 381
 382            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
 383                tmp_umap = tmp_umap.loc[new_order, :]
 384                self.umap = tmp_umap.reset_index(drop=True)
 385                del tmp_umap
 386
 387            self.clustering_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 388            self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.clustering_metadata[
 389                value_to_sort
 390            ].astype(str)

 392    def harmonize_sets(self, batch_col: str = "sets"):
 393        """
 394        Perform batch effect harmonization on PCA embeddings.
 395
 396        Parameters
 397        ----------
 398        batch_col : str, default 'sets'
 399            Name of the column in `metadata` that contains batch information for the samples/cells.
 400
 401        Returns
 402        -------
 403        None
 404            Updates the `harmonized_pca` attribute with harmonized data.
 405        """
 406
 407        data_mat = np.array(self.pca)
 408
 409        metadata = self.clustering_metadata
 410
 411        self.harmonized_pca = pd.DataFrame(
 412            harmonize.run_harmony(data_mat, metadata, vars_use=batch_col).Z_corr
 413        ).T
 414
 415        self.harmonized_pca.columns = self.pca.columns

 417    def perform_PCA(self, pc_num: int = 100, width=8, height=6):
 418        """
 419        Perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the dataset.
 420
 421        This method standardizes the data, applies PCA, stores results as attributes,
 422        and generates a scatter plot of the first two principal components.
 423
 424        Parameters
 425        ----------
 426        pc_num : int, default 100
 427            Number of principal components to compute.
 428            If 0, computes all available components.
 429
 430        width : int or float, default 8
 431            Width of the PCA figure.
 432
 433        height : int or float, default 6
 434            Height of the PCA figure.
 435
 436        Returns
 437        -------
 438        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 439            Scatter plot showing the first two principal components.
 440
 441        Updates
 442        -------
 443        self.pca : pandas.DataFrame
 444            DataFrame with principal component scores for each sample.
 445
 446        self.explained_var : numpy.ndarray
 447            Percentage of variance explained by each principal component.
 448
 449        self.cumulative_var : numpy.ndarray
 450            Cumulative explained variance.
 451        """
 452
 453        scaler = StandardScaler()
 454        data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
 455
 456        if pc_num == 0 or pc_num > data_scaled.shape[0]:
 457            pc_num = data_scaled.shape[0]
 458
 459        pca = PCA(n_components=pc_num, random_state=42)
 460
 461        principal_components = pca.fit_transform(data_scaled)
 462
 463        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(
 464            data=principal_components,
 465            columns=["PC" + str(x + 1) for x in range(pc_num)],
 466        )
 467
 468        self.explained_var = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
 469        self.cumulative_var = np.cumsum(self.explained_var)
 470
 471        self.pca = pca_df
 472
 473        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 474        plt.scatter(pca_df["PC1"], pca_df["PC2"], alpha=0.7)
 475        plt.xlabel("PC 1")
 476        plt.ylabel("PC 2")
 477        plt.grid(True)
 478        plt.show()
 479
 480        return fig
 481
 482    def knee_plot_PCA(self, width: int = 8, height: int = 6):
 483        """
 484        Plot cumulative explained variance to determine the optimal number of PCs.
 485
 486        Parameters
 487        ----------
 488        width : int, default 8
 489            Width of the figure.
 490
 491        height : int or, default 6
 492            Height of the figure.
 493
 494        Returns
 495        -------
 496        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 497            Line plot showing cumulative variance explained by each PC.
 498        """
 499
 500        fig_knee = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 501        plt.plot(range(1, len(self.explained_var) + 1), self.cumulative_var, marker="o")
 502        plt.xlabel("PC (n components)")
 503        plt.ylabel("Cumulative explained variance (%)")
 504        plt.grid(True)
 505
 506        xticks = [1] + list(range(5, len(self.explained_var) + 1, 5))
 507        plt.xticks(xticks, rotation=60)
 508
 509        plt.show()
 510
 511        return fig_knee

 513    def find_clusters_PCA(
 514        self,
 515        pc_num: int = 2,
 516        eps: float = 0.5,
 517        min_samples: int = 10,
 518        width: int = 8,
 519        height: int = 6,
 520        harmonized: bool = False,
 521    ):
 522        """
 523        Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize the results.
 524
 525        This method performs density-based clustering (DBSCAN) on the PCA-reduced
 526        dataset. Cluster labels are stored in the object's metadata, and a scatter
 527        plot of the first two principal components with cluster annotations is returned.
 528
 529        Parameters
 530        ----------
 531        pc_num : int, default 2
 532            Number of principal components to use for clustering.
 533            If 0, uses all available components.
 534
 535        eps : float, default 0.5
 536            Maximum distance between two points for them to be considered
 537            as neighbors (DBSCAN parameter).
 538
 539        min_samples : int, default 10
 540            Minimum number of samples required to form a cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 541
 542        width : int, default 8
 543            Width of the output scatter plot.
 544
 545        height : int, default 6
 546            Height of the output scatter plot.
 547
 548        harmonized : bool, default False
 549            If True, use harmonized PCA data (`self.harmonized_pca`).
 550            If False, use standard PCA results (`self.pca`).
 551
 552        Returns
 553        -------
 554        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 555            Scatter plot of the first two principal components colored by
 556            cluster assignments.
 557
 558        Updates
 559        -------
 560        self.clustering_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list
 561            Cluster labels assigned to each cell/sample.
 562
 563        self.input_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list, optional
 564            Cluster labels stored in input metadata (if available).
 565        """
 566
 567        dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 568
 569        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
 570            PCA = self.harmonized_pca
 571
 572        elif pc_num == 0:
 573            PCA = self.pca
 574
 575        else:
 576            if harmonized:
 577
 578                PCA = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 579            else:
 580
 581                PCA = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 582
 583        dbscan_labels = dbscan.fit_predict(PCA)
 584
 585        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(PCA)
 586        pca_df["Cluster"] = dbscan_labels
 587
 588        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 589
 590        clusters = sorted(pca_df["Cluster"].unique())
 591        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(clusters))
 592
 593        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
 594            cluster_data = pca_df[pca_df["Cluster"] == cluster_id]
 595            plt.scatter(
 596                cluster_data["PC1"],
 597                cluster_data["PC2"],
 598                label=f"Cluster {cluster_id}",
 599                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
 600                alpha=0.7,
 601            )
 602
 603        plt.xlabel("PC 1")
 604        plt.ylabel("PC 2")
 605        plt.legend(title="Clusters", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
 606
 607        plt.grid(True)
 608        plt.show()
 609
 610        self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 611
 612        try:
 613            self.input_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 614        except:
 615            pass
 616
 617        return fig

 619    def perform_UMAP(
 620        self,
 621        factorize: bool = False,
 622        umap_num: int = 100,
 623        pc_num: int = 0,
 624        harmonized: bool = False,
 625        n_neighbors: int = 5,
 626        min_dist: float | int = 0.1,
 627        spread: float | int = 1.0,
 628        set_op_mix_ratio: float | int = 1.0,
 629        local_connectivity: int = 1,
 630        repulsion_strength: float | int = 1.0,
 631        negative_sample_rate: int = 5,
 632        width: int = 8,
 633        height: int = 6,
 634    ):
 635        """
 636        Compute and visualize UMAP embeddings of the dataset.
 637
 638        This method applies Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)
 639        for dimensionality reduction on either raw, PCA, or harmonized PCA data.
 640        Results are stored as a DataFrame (`self.umap`) and a scatter plot figure
 641        (`self.UMAP_plot`).
 642
 643        Parameters
 644        ----------
 645        factorize : bool, default False
 646            If True, categorical sample labels (from column names) are factorized
 647            and used as supervision in UMAP fitting.
 648
 649        umap_num : int, default 100
 650            Number of UMAP dimensions to compute. If 0, matches the input dimension.
 651
 652        pc_num : int, default 0
 653            Number of principal components to use as UMAP input.
 654            If 0, use all available components or raw data.
 655
 656        harmonized : bool, default False
 657            If True, use harmonized PCA embeddings (`self.harmonized_pca`).
 658            If False, use standard PCA or raw scaled data.
 659
 660        n_neighbors : int, default 5
 661            UMAP parameter controlling the size of the local neighborhood.
 662
 663        min_dist : float, default 0.1
 664            UMAP parameter controlling minimum allowed distance between embedded points.
 665
 666        spread : int | float, default 1.0
 667            Effective scale of embedded space (UMAP parameter).
 668
 669        set_op_mix_ratio : int | float, default 1.0
 670            Interpolation parameter between union and intersection in fuzzy sets.
 671
 672        local_connectivity : int, default 1
 673            Number of nearest neighbors assumed for each point.
 674
 675        repulsion_strength : int | float, default 1.0
 676            Weighting applied to negative samples during optimization.
 677
 678        negative_sample_rate : int, default 5
 679            Number of negative samples per positive sample in optimization.
 680
 681        width : int, default 8
 682            Width of the output scatter plot.
 683
 684        height : int, default 6
 685            Height of the output scatter plot.
 686
 687        Updates
 688        -------
 689        self.umap : pandas.DataFrame
 690            Table of UMAP embeddings with columns `UMAP1 ... UMAPn`.
 691
 692        Notes
 693        -----
 694        For supervised UMAP (`factorize=True`), categorical codes from column
 695        names of the dataset are used as labels.
 696        """
 697
 698        scaler = StandardScaler()
 699
 700        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
 701            data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca
 702
 703        elif pc_num == 0:
 704            data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
 705
 706        else:
 707            if harmonized:
 708
 709                data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 710            else:
 711
 712                data_scaled = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 713
 714        if umap_num == 0 or umap_num > data_scaled.shape[1]:
 715
 716            umap_num = data_scaled.shape[1]
 717
 718            reducer = umap.UMAP(
 719                n_components=len(data_scaled.T),
 720                random_state=42,
 721                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
 722                min_dist=min_dist,
 723                spread=spread,
 724                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
 725                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
 726                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
 727                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
 728                n_jobs=1,
 729            )
 730
 731        else:
 732
 733            reducer = umap.UMAP(
 734                n_components=umap_num,
 735                random_state=42,
 736                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
 737                min_dist=min_dist,
 738                spread=spread,
 739                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
 740                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
 741                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
 742                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
 743                n_jobs=1,
 744            )
 745
 746        if factorize:
 747            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(
 748                X=data_scaled, y=pd.Categorical(self.clustering_data.columns).codes
 749            )
 750        else:
 751            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X=data_scaled)
 752
 753        umap_df = pd.DataFrame(
 754            embedding, columns=["UMAP" + str(x + 1) for x in range(umap_num)]
 755        )
 756
 757        plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 758        plt.scatter(umap_df["UMAP1"], umap_df["UMAP2"], alpha=0.7)
 759        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
 760        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
 761        plt.grid(True)
 762
 763        plt.show()
 764
 765        self.umap = umap_df
 766
 767    def knee_plot_umap(self, eps: int | float = 0.5, min_samples: int = 10):
 768        """
 769        Plot silhouette scores for different UMAP dimensions to determine optimal n_components.
 770
 771        Parameters
 772        ----------
 773        eps : float, default 0.5
 774            DBSCAN eps parameter for clustering each UMAP dimension.
 775
 776        min_samples : int, default 10
 777            Minimum number of samples to form a cluster in DBSCAN.
 778
 779        Returns
 780        -------
 781        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 782            Silhouette score plot across UMAP dimensions.
 783        """
 784
 785        umap_range = range(2, len(self.umap.T) + 1)
 786
 787        silhouette_scores = []
 788        component = []
 789        for n in umap_range:
 790
 791            db = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 792            labels = db.fit_predict(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n])
 793
 794            mask = labels != -1
 795            if len(set(labels[mask])) > 1:
 796                score = silhouette_score(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n][mask], labels[mask])
 797            else:
 798                score = -1
 799
 800            silhouette_scores.append(score)
 801            component.append(n)
 802
 803        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
 804        plt.plot(component, silhouette_scores, marker="o")
 805        plt.xlabel("UMAP (n_components)")
 806        plt.ylabel("Silhouette Score")
 807        plt.grid(True)
 808        plt.xticks(range(int(min(component)), int(max(component)) + 1, 1))
 809
 810        plt.show()
 811
 812        return fig
 813
 814    def find_clusters_UMAP(
 815        self,
 816        umap_n: int = 5,
 817        eps: float | float = 0.5,
 818        min_samples: int = 10,
 819        width: int = 8,
 820        height: int = 6,
 821    ):
 822        """
 823        Apply DBSCAN clustering on UMAP embeddings and visualize clusters.
 824
 825        This method performs density-based clustering (DBSCAN) on the UMAP-reduced
 826        dataset. Cluster labels are stored in the object's metadata, and a scatter
 827        plot of the first two UMAP components with cluster annotations is returned.
 828
 829        Parameters
 830        ----------
 831        umap_n : int, default 5
 832            Number of UMAP dimensions to use for DBSCAN clustering.
 833            Must be <= number of columns in `self.umap`.
 834
 835        eps : float | int, default 0.5
 836            Maximum neighborhood distance between two samples for them to be considered
 837            as in the same cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 838
 839        min_samples : int, default 10
 840            Minimum number of samples in a neighborhood to form a cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 841
 842        width : int, default 8
 843            Figure width.
 844
 845        height : int, default 6
 846            Figure height.
 847
 848        Returns
 849        -------
 850        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 851            Scatter plot of the first two UMAP components colored by
 852            cluster assignments.
 853
 854        Updates
 855        -------
 856        self.clustering_metadata['UMAP_clusters'] : list
 857            Cluster labels assigned to each cell/sample.
 858
 859        self.input_metadata['UMAP_clusters'] : list, optional
 860            Cluster labels stored in input metadata (if available).
 861        """
 862
 863        dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 864        dbscan_labels = dbscan.fit_predict(np.array(self.umap)[:, :umap_n])
 865
 866        umap_df = self.umap
 867        umap_df["Cluster"] = dbscan_labels
 868
 869        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 870
 871        colors_1 = plt.cm.tab20b(np.linspace(0, 1, 20))
 872        colors_2 = plt.cm.tab20c(np.linspace(0, 1, 20))
 873        color_palette = np.vstack((colors_1, colors_2))
 874
 875        clusters = sorted(umap_df["Cluster"].unique())
 876
 877        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
 878            cluster_data = umap_df[umap_df["Cluster"] == cluster_id]
 879
 880            plt.scatter(
 881                cluster_data["UMAP1"],
 882                cluster_data["UMAP2"],
 883                label=f"Cluster {cluster_id}",
 884                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
 885                alpha=0.7,
 886            )
 887
 888        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
 889        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
 890        plt.legend(title="Clusters", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
 891        plt.grid(True)
 892
 893        self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 894
 895        try:
 896            self.input_metadata["UMAP_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 897        except:
 898            pass
 899
 900        return fig

 902    def UMAP_vis(
 903        self,
 904        names_slot: str = "cell_names",
 905        set_sep: bool = True,
 906        point_size: int | float = 0.6,
 907        font_size: int | float = 6,
 908        legend_split_col: int = 2,
 909        width: int = 8,
 910        height: int = 6,
 911        inc_num: bool = True,
 912        inc_bbox: bool = True,
 913        size_sort: bool = True,
 914        grid: bool = False,
 915        rasterized: bool = True,
 916    ):
 917        """
 918        Visualize UMAP embeddings with sample labels based on specyfic metadata slot.
 919
 920        Parameters
 921        ----------
 922        names_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
 923            Column in metadata to use as sample labels.
 924
 925        set_sep : bool, default True
 926            If True, separate points by dataset.
 927
 928        point_size : float, default 0.6
 929            Size of scatter points.
 930
 931        font_size : int, default 6
 932            Font size for numbers on points.
 933
 934        legend_split_col : int, default 2
 935            Number of columns in legend.
 936
 937        width : int, default 8
 938            Figure width.
 939
 940        height : int, default 6
 941            Figure height.
 942
 943        inc_num : bool, default True
 944            If True, annotate points with numeric labels.
 945
 946        inc_bbox : bool, default True
 947            If True, annotate points with a background box (bbox).
 948
 949        size_sort : bool, default=True
 950            If True, cluster names are sorted in descending order by cluster size.
 951             If False, cluster names follow the order of their first appearance in `names_slot`.
 952
 953        grid : bool, default False
 954            If True, the plot grid will be visible.
 955
 956        rasterized : bool, default True
 957            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
 958            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
 959            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
 960
 961
 962        Returns
 963        -------
 964        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 965            UMAP scatter plot figure.
 966        """
 967
 968        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
 969        umap_df["names"] = list(self.clustering_metadata[names_slot])
 970
 971        if set_sep:
 972
 973            if "sets" in list(self.clustering_metadata.columns):
 974                umap_df["dataset"] = list(self.clustering_metadata["sets"])
 975            else:
 976                umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 977
 978        else:
 979            umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 980
 981        umap_df["tmp_nam"] = list(umap_df["names"] + umap_df["dataset"])
 982
 983        umap_df["count"] = umap_df["tmp_nam"].map(umap_df["tmp_nam"].value_counts())
 984
 985        queue = pd.unique(umap_df["names"])
 986
 987        umap_df["names"] = pd.Categorical(
 988            umap_df["names"], categories=queue, ordered=True
 989        )
 990
 991        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("names").reset_index(drop=True)
 992
 993        umap_df["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(umap_df["names"])[0]
 994
 995        numeric_df = (
 996            pd.DataFrame(umap_df[["count", "tmp_nam", "names", "id_vec"]].copy())
 997            .drop_duplicates()
 998            .sort_values("count", ascending=False)
 999        )
1000
1001        numeric_df["numeric_values"] = range(0, numeric_df.shape[0])
1002
1003        if size_sort:
1004            numeric_df["id_vec"] = numeric_df["numeric_values"]
1005
1006        umap_df = umap_df.merge(
1007            numeric_df[["tmp_nam", "numeric_values"]], on="tmp_nam", how="left"
1008        )
1009
1010        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1011
1012        markers = ["o", "s", "^", "D", "P", "*", "X"]
1013        marker_map = {
1014            ds: markers[i % len(markers)]
1015            for i, ds in enumerate(umap_df["dataset"].unique())
1016        }
1017
1018        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(numeric_df["tmp_nam"]))
1019
1020        cord_list = []
1021
1022        numeric_df = numeric_df.reset_index(drop=True)
1023
1024        id_counts = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec")["id_vec"].transform("count")
1025        id_cum = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec").cumcount() + 1
1026
1027        numeric_df["id_vec"] = np.where(
1028            id_counts > 1,
1029            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str) + "." + id_cum.astype(str),
1030            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str),
1031        )
1032
1033        for idx, (num, nam) in enumerate(
1034            zip(numeric_df["numeric_values"], numeric_df["names"])
1035        ):
1036
1037            cluster_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] == num]
1038
1039            rest_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] != num]
1040
1041            current_size = max(point_size, 0.25)
1042
1043            ax.scatter(
1044                cluster_data["UMAP1"],
1045                cluster_data["UMAP2"],
1046                label=f"{numeric_df['id_vec'][idx]} - {nam}",
1047                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
1048                marker=marker_map[cluster_data["dataset"].iloc[0]],
1049                alpha=0.6,
1050                s=current_size,
1051                rasterized=rasterized,
1052            )
1053
1054            coords = np.round(cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1055            rest_coords = np.round(rest_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1056
1057            coords_tuples = set(map(tuple, rest_coords))
1058            should_keep = [tuple(pt) not in coords_tuples for pt in coords]
1059
1060            coords = coords[should_keep]
1061
1062            if len(coords) == 0:
1063                coords = cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values
1064
1065            if len(coords) > 0:
1066                mean_x = np.mean(coords[:, 0])
1067                mean_y = np.mean(coords[:, 1])
1068
1069                q1 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1070                q2 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1071                q3 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1072                q4 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1073
1074                quadrants = [q for q in [q1, q2, q3, q4] if len(q) > 0]
1075
1076                if quadrants:
1077                    quadrants.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
1078
1079                    top1 = quadrants[0]
1080                    center1 = np.mean(top1, axis=0)
1081
1082                    if len(quadrants) > 1:
1083                        top2 = quadrants[1]
1084                        center2 = np.mean(top2, axis=0)
1085
1086                        dist_between_tops = np.linalg.norm(center1 - center2)
1087
1088                        cluster_spread = np.mean(
1089                            np.linalg.norm(coords - [mean_x, mean_y], axis=1)
1090                        )
1091                        threshold = cluster_spread * 0.6
1092
1093                        if dist_between_tops < threshold:
1094                            combined_tops = np.vstack([top1, top2])
1095                            center_point = np.mean(combined_tops, axis=0)
1096                        else:
1097                            center_point = center1
1098                    else:
1099                        center_point = center1
1100                else:
1101                    center_point = np.array([mean_x, mean_y])
1102
1103                cluster_median = np.median(coords, axis=0)
1104                alpha = 0.5
1105                center_point = (1 - alpha) * center_point + alpha * cluster_median
1106
1107            else:
1108                center_point = np.array([0, 0])
1109
1110            cord_list.append(center_point)
1111
1112        if inc_num:
1113
1114            bbox_props = (
1115                dict(
1116                    boxstyle="round,pad=0.1",
1117                    facecolor="white",
1118                    edgecolor="none",
1119                    alpha=0.7,
1120                )
1121                if inc_bbox
1122                else None
1123            )
1124
1125            texts = []
1126            repeat_lab = []
1127            for (x, y), num in zip(cord_list, numeric_df["id_vec"]):
1128                if num not in repeat_lab:
1129                    texts.append(
1130                        ax.text(
1131                            x,
1132                            y,
1133                            str(num),
1134                            ha="center",
1135                            va="center",
1136                            fontsize=font_size,
1137                            color="black",
1138                            bbox=bbox_props,
1139                        )
1140                    )
1141                    repeat_lab.append(num)
1142
1143            adjust_text(
1144                texts,
1145                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", lw=0.5),
1146                force_text=(1.2, 1.2),
1147                force_points=(1.0, 1.0),
1148                expand_text=(1.3, 1.3),
1149                expand_points=(1.3, 1.3),
1150                lim=500,
1151            )
1152
1153        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1154        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1155
1156        ax.grid(grid)
1157
1158        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1159
1160        def sort_key(item):
1161            num_str = item[1].split(" - ")[0]
1162            parts = num_str.split(".")
1163            main_num = int(parts[0])
1164            sub_num = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
1165            return (main_num, sub_num)
1166
1167        sorted_pairs = sorted(zip(handles, labels), key=sort_key)
1168        sorted_handles, sorted_labels = zip(*sorted_pairs)
1169
1170        if not inc_num:
1171            sorted_labels = [lbl.split(" - ", 1)[1] for lbl in sorted_labels]
1172
1173        unique_datasets = umap_df["dataset"].unique()
1174        dataset_handles = list(sorted_handles)
1175        dataset_labels = list(sorted_labels)
1176
1177        if len(unique_datasets) > 1:
1178            for ds in unique_datasets:
1179                proxy_marker = Line2D(
1180                    [0],
1181                    [0],
1182                    marker=marker_map[ds],
1183                    color="w",
1184                    markerfacecolor="gray",
1185                    markeredgecolor="black",
1186                    markersize=current_size * 2,
1187                    linestyle="None",
1188                    label=f"Set: {ds}",
1189                )
1190
1191                dataset_handles.append(proxy_marker)
1192                dataset_labels.append(f"Data: {ds}")
1193
1194        ax.legend(
1195            dataset_handles,
1196            dataset_labels,
1197            title="",
1198            loc="center left",
1199            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.5),
1200            ncol=legend_split_col,
1201            markerscale=15,
1202        )
1203
1204        ax.grid(grid, which="both")
1205
1206        plt.tight_layout()
1207
1208        return fig

1210    def UMAP_feature(
1211        self,
1212        feature_name: str,
1213        features_data: pd.DataFrame | None,
1214        point_size: int | float = 0.6,
1215        font_size: int | float = 6,
1216        width: int = 8,
1217        height: int = 6,
1218        palette="light",
1219        grid: bool = False,
1220        rasterized: bool = True,
1221    ):
1222        """
1223        Visualize UMAP embedding with expression levels of a selected feature.
1224
1225        Each point (cell) in the UMAP plot is colored according to the expression
1226        value of the chosen feature, enabling interpretation of spatial patterns
1227        of gene activity or metadata distribution in low-dimensional space.
1228
1229        Parameters
1230        ----------
1231        feature_name : str
1232           Name of the feature to plot.
1233
1234        features_data : pandas.DataFrame or None, default None
1235            If None, the function uses the DataFrame containing the clustering data.
1236            To plot features not used in clustering, provide a wider DataFrame
1237            containing the original feature values.
1238
1239        point_size : float, default 0.6
1240            Size of scatter points in the plot.
1241
1242        font_size : int, default 6
1243            Font size for axis labels and annotations.
1244
1245        width : int, default 8
1246            Width of the matplotlib figure.
1247
1248        height : int, default 6
1249            Height of the matplotlib figure.
1250
1251        grid : bool, default False
1252            If True, the plot grid will be visible.
1253
1254        palette : str, default 'light'
1255            Color palette for expression visualization. Options are:
1256            - 'light'
1257            - 'dark'
1258            - 'green'
1259            - 'gray'
1260
1261        rasterized : bool, default True
1262            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
1263            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
1264            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
1265
1266        Returns
1267        -------
1268        matplotlib.figure.Figure
1269            UMAP scatter plot colored by feature values.
1270        """
1271
1272        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
1273
1274        if features_data is None:
1275            features_data = self.clustering_data
1276
1277        if features_data.shape[1] != umap_df.shape[0]:
1278            raise ValueError(
1279                "Imputed 'features_data' shape does not match the number of UMAP"
1280                " cells"
1281            )
1282
1283        blist = [
1284            True if x.upper() == feature_name.upper() else False
1285            for x in features_data.index
1286        ]
1287
1288        if not any(blist):
1289            raise ValueError("Imputed feature_name is not included in the data")
1290
1291        umap_df.loc[:, "feature"] = (
1292            features_data.loc[blist, :]
1293            .apply(lambda row: row.tolist(), axis=1)
1294            .values[0]
1295        )
1296
1297        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("feature", ascending=True)
1298
1299        vals = umap_df["feature"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1300        vmin, vmax = vals.min(), vals.max()
1301
1302        if vmax > vmin:
1303            norm_vals = (vals - vmin) / (vmax - vmin)
1304        else:
1305            norm_vals = np.ones_like(vals)
1306
1307        min_scale = 0.1
1308        sizes = point_size * (min_scale + (1.0 - min_scale) * norm_vals)
1309
1310        def px_to_rgb01(px_seq):
1311            out = []
1312            for c in px_seq:
1313                rgb_255 = px.colors.unlabel_rgb(c)
1314                out.append(tuple(v / 255.0 for v in rgb_255))
1315            return out
1316
1317        def sample_colors(px_seq, n_colors):
1318            rgb_seq = px_to_rgb01(px_seq)
1319            if n_colors <= 1:
1320                return rgb_seq[:n_colors]
1321            idxs = np.linspace(0, len(rgb_seq) - 1, n_colors).round().astype(int)
1322            return [rgb_seq[i] for i in idxs]
1323
1324        n_groups = len(px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark)
1325
1326        norm = None
1327
1328        if palette in ("gray-red", "gray-blue"):
1329            base_px = (
1330                px.colors.sequential.Reds
1331                if palette == "gray-red"
1332                else px.colors.sequential.Blues
1333            )
1334            grad_colors = sample_colors(base_px[3:], max(n_groups - 1, 1))
1335            gray_rgb = (0.72, 0.72, 0.72)
1336
1337            if vmax > vmin:
1338                if vmin <= 0.0 < vmax and np.any(vals > 0.0):
1339                    eps = min(np.min(vals[vals > 0.0]) * 0.5, (vmax - 0.0) * 1e-3)
1340                    pos_bounds = np.linspace(eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1341                    bounds = np.concatenate(([min(vmin, 0.0)], pos_bounds))
1342                else:
1343                    eps = (vmax - vmin) * 1e-3
1344                    rest_bounds = np.linspace(vmin + eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1345                    bounds = np.concatenate(([vmin], rest_bounds))
1346
1347                colors_list = [gray_rgb] + grad_colors
1348                norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, ncolors=len(colors_list))
1349                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(colors_list, name=palette)
1350            else:
1351                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap([gray_rgb], name=palette)
1352
1353        else:
1354            if palette == "light":
1355                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark
1356            elif palette == "dark":
1357                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.thermal
1358            elif palette == "green":
1359                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Aggrnyl
1360            elif palette == "gray":
1361                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.gray[::-1]
1362            else:
1363                raise ValueError(
1364                    'Palette not found. Use: "light", "dark", "gray", "green",'
1365                    ' "gray-red", or "gray-blue"'
1366                )
1367
1368            converted = sample_colors(px_palette, n_groups)
1369            my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(converted, name="custom")
1370
1371        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1372        sc = ax.scatter(
1373            umap_df["UMAP1"],
1374            umap_df["UMAP2"],
1375            c=umap_df["feature"],
1376            s=sizes * 5,
1377            cmap=my_cmap,
1378            norm=norm,
1379            alpha=1,
1380            edgecolors="white",
1381            linewidths=0,
1382            rasterized=rasterized,
1383        )
1384
1385        cbar = plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1386        cbar.set_label(f"{feature_name}")
1387        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=5))
1388        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter("%.1f"))
1389
1390        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1391        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1392
1393        ax.grid(grid)
1394
1395        plt.tight_layout()
1396
1397        return fig
1398
1399    def get_umap_data(self):
1400        """
1401        Retrieve UMAP embedding data with optional cluster labels.
1402
1403        Returns the UMAP coordinates stored in `self.umap`. If clustering
1404        metadata is available (specifically `UMAP_clusters`), the corresponding
1405        cluster assignments are appended as an additional column.
1406
1407        Returns
1408        -------
1409        pandas.DataFrame
1410            DataFrame containing UMAP coordinates (columns: 'UMAP1', 'UMAP2', ...).
1411            If available, includes an extra column 'clusters' with cluster labels.
1412
1413        Notes
1414        -----
1415        - UMAP embeddings must be computed beforehand (e.g., using `perform_UMAP`).
1416        - Cluster labels are added only if present in `self.clustering_metadata`.
1417        """
1418
1419        umap_data = self.umap
1420
1421        try:
1422            umap_data["clusters"] = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]
1423        except:
1424            pass
1425
1426        return umap_data
1427
1428    def get_pca_data(self):
1429        """
1430        Retrieve PCA embedding data with optional cluster labels.
1431
1432        Returns the principal component scores stored in `self.pca`. If clustering
1433        metadata is available (specifically `PCA_clusters`), the corresponding
1434        cluster assignments are appended as an additional column.
1435
1436        Returns
1437        -------
1438        pandas.DataFrame
1439            DataFrame containing PCA coordinates (columns: 'PC1', 'PC2', ...).
1440            If available, includes an extra column 'clusters' with cluster labels.
1441
1442        Notes
1443        -----
1444        - PCA must be computed beforehand (e.g., using `perform_PCA`).
1445        - Cluster labels are added only if present in `self.clustering_metadata`.
1446        """
1447
1448        pca_data = self.pca
1449
1450        try:
1451            pca_data["clusters"] = self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"]
1452        except:
1453            pass
1454
1455        return pca_data
1456
1457    def return_clusters(self, clusters="umap"):
1458        """
1459        Retrieve cluster labels from UMAP or PCA clustering results.
1460
1461        Parameters
1462        ----------
1463        clusters : str, default 'umap'
1464            Source of cluster labels to return. Must be one of:
1465            - 'umap': return cluster labels from UMAP embeddings.
1466            - 'pca' : return cluster labels from PCA embeddings.
1467
1468        Returns
1469        -------
1470        list
1471            Cluster labels corresponding to the selected embedding method.
1472
1473        Raises
1474        ------
1475        ValueError
1476            If `clusters` is not 'umap' or 'pca'.
1477
1478        Notes
1479        -----
1480        Requires that clustering has already been performed
1481        (e.g., using `find_clusters_UMAP` or `find_clusters_PCA`).
1482        """
1483
1484        if clusters.lower() == "umap":
1485            clusters_vector = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]
1486        elif clusters.lower() == "pca":
1487            clusters_vector = self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"]
1488        else:
1489            raise ValueError("Parameter 'clusters' must be either 'umap' or 'pca'.")
1490
1491        return clusters_vector
1492
1493
1494class COMPsc(Clustering):
1495    """
1496    A class `COMPsc` (Comparison of single-cell data) designed for the integration,
1497    analysis, and visualization of single-cell datasets.
1498    The class supports independent dataset integration, subclustering of existing clusters,
1499    marker detection, and multiple visualization strategies.
1500
1501    The COMPsc class provides methods for:
1502
1503        - Normalizing and filtering single-cell data
1504        - Loading and saving sparse 10x-style datasets
1505        - Computing differential expression and marker genes
1506        - Clustering and subclustering analysis
1507        - Visualizing similarity and spatial relationships
1508        - Aggregating data by cell and set annotations
1509        - Managing metadata and renaming labels
1510        - Plotting gene detection histograms and feature dot plots
1511
1512    Methods
1513    -------
1514    project_dir(path_to_directory, project_list)
1515        Scans a directory to create a COMPsc instance mapping project names to their paths.
1516
1517    save_project(name, path=os.getcwd())
1518        Saves the COMPsc object to a pickle file on disk.
1519
1520    load_project(path)
1521        Loads a previously saved COMPsc object from a pickle file.
1522
1523    reduce_cols(reg, inc_set=False)
1524        Removes columns from data tables where column names contain a specified name or partial substring.
1525
1526    reduce_rows(reg, inc_set=False)
1527        Removes rows from data tables where column names contain a specified feature (gene) name.
1528
1529    get_data(set_info=False)
1530        Returns normalized data with optional set annotations in column names.
1531
1532    get_metadata()
1533        Returns the stored input metadata.
1534
1535    get_partial_data(names=None, features=None, name_slot='cell_names')
1536        Return a subset of the data by sample names and/or features.
1537
1538    gene_calculation()
1539        Calculates and stores per-cell gene detection counts as a pandas Series.
1540
1541    gene_histograme(bins=100)
1542        Plots a histogram of genes detected per cell with an overlaid normal distribution.
1543
1544    gene_threshold(min_n=None, max_n=None)
1545        Filters cells based on minimum and/or maximum gene detection thresholds.
1546
1547    load_sparse_from_projects(normalized_data=False)
1548        Loads and concatenates sparse 10x-style datasets from project paths into count or normalized data.
1549
1550    rename_names(mapping, slot='cell_names')
1551        Renames entries in a specified metadata column using a provided mapping dictionary.
1552
1553    rename_subclusters(mapping)
1554        Renames subcluster labels using a provided mapping dictionary.
1555
1556    save_sparse(path_to_save=os.getcwd(), name_slot='cell_names', data_slot='normalized')
1557        Exports data as 10x-compatible sparse files (matrix.mtx, barcodes.tsv, genes.tsv).
1558
1559    normalize_data(normalize=True, normalize_factor=100000)
1560        Normalizes raw counts to counts-per-specified factor (e.g., CPM-like).
1561
1562    statistic(cells=None, sets=None, min_exp=0.01, min_pct=0.1, n_proc=10)
1563        Computes per-feature differential expression statistics (Mann-Whitney U) comparing target vs. rest groups.
1564
1565    calculate_difference_markers(min_exp=0, min_pct=0.25, n_proc=10, force=False)
1566        Computes and caches differential markers using the statistic method.
1567
1568    clustering_features(features_list=None, name_slot='cell_names', p_val=0.05, top_n=25, adj_mean=True, beta=0.4)
1569        Prepares clustering input by selecting marker features and optionally smoothing cell values.
1570
1571    average()
1572        Aggregates normalized data by averaging across (cell_name, set) pairs.
1573
1574    estimating_similarity(method='pearson', p_val=0.05, top_n=25)
1575        Computes pairwise correlation and Euclidean distance between aggregated samples.
1576
1577    cell_genes_distribution(cells_names, cells_sets=None, image_width=10, image_high=7)
1578        Compares the distributions of detected genes per cell across selected cell populations using overlapping histograms.
1579
1580    mm_cell_genes(cells_names, cells_sets=None, non_include_zeros=True, image_width=7, image_high=10)
1581        Calculates and visualizes the mean and median gene expression across selected cell populations as a grouped bar plot.
1582
1583    cell_dispersion(cells_names, cells_sets=None, image_width=7, image_high=10)
1584        Assesses within-cluster transcriptional dispersion by calculating distances between individual cells and their cluster centroids, visualized via violin plots.
1585
1586    similarity_plot(split_sets=True, set_info=True, cmap='seismic', width=12, height=10)
1587        Visualizes pairwise similarity as a dot plot with correlation as hue and scaled distance as point size.
1588
1589    spatial_similarity(set_info=True, bandwidth=1, n_neighbors=5, min_dist=0.1, legend_split=2, point_size=20, ...)
1590        Creates a UMAP-like visualization of similarity relationships with cluster hulls and nearest-neighbor arrows.
1591
1592    subcluster_prepare(features, cluster)
1593        Initializes a Clustering object for subcluster analysis on a selected parent cluster.
1594
1595    define_subclusters(umap_num=2, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, bandwidth=1, n_neighbors=5, min_dist=0.1, ...)
1596        Performs UMAP and DBSCAN clustering on prepared subcluster data and stores cluster labels.
1597
1598    subcluster_features_dot(colors='viridis', hclust='complete', img_width=3, img_high=5, label_size=6, ...)
1599        Visualizes averaged expression and occurrence of features for subclusters as a dot plot.
1600
1601    subcluster_DEG_dot(top_n=3, min_exp=0, min_pct=0.25, p_val=0.05, colors='viridis', ...)
1602        Plots top differential features for subclusters as a features-dot visualization.
1603
1604    accept_subclusters()
1605        Commits subcluster labels to main metadata by renaming cell names and clears subcluster data.
1606
1607    Raises
1608    ------
1609    ValueError
1610        For invalid parameters, mismatched dimensions, or missing metadata.
1611
1612    """
1613
1614    def __init__(
1615        self,
1616        objects=None,
1617    ):
1618        """
1619        Initialize the COMPsc class for single-cell data integration and analysis.
1620
1621        Parameters
1622        ----------
1623        objects : list or None, optional
1624            Optional list of data objects to initialize the instance with.
1625
1626        Attributes
1627        ----------
1628        -objects : list or None
1629        -input_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1630        -input_metadata : pandas.DataFrame or None
1631        -normalized_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1632        -agg_metadata : pandas.DataFrame or None
1633        -agg_normalized_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1634        -similarity : pandas.DataFrame or None
1635        -var_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1636        -subclusters_ : instance of Clustering class or None
1637        -cells_calc : pandas.Series or None
1638        -gene_calc : pandas.Series or None
1639        -composition_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1640        """
1641
1642        self.objects = objects
1643        """ Stores the input data objects."""
1644
1645        self.input_data = None
1646        """Raw input data for clustering or integration analysis."""
1647
1648        self.input_metadata = None
1649        """Metadata associated with the input data."""
1650
1651        self.normalized_data = None
1652        """Normalized version of the input data."""
1653
1654        self.agg_metadata = None
1655        '''Aggregated metadata for all sets in object related to "agg_normalized_data"'''
1656
1657        self.agg_normalized_data = None
1658        """Aggregated and normalized data across multiple sets."""
1659
1660        self.similarity = None
1661        """Similarity data between cells across all samples. and sets"""
1662
1663        self.var_data = None
1664        """DEG analysis results summarizing variance across all samples in the object."""
1665
1666        self.subclusters_ = None
1667        """Placeholder for information about subclusters analysis; if computed."""
1668
1669        self.cells_calc = None
1670        """Number of cells detected per sample (grouped by lineage, e.g., cluster or name), reflecting data composition."""
1671
1672        self.gene_calc = None
1673        """Number of genes detected per sample (cell), reflecting the sequencing depth."""
1674
1675        self.composition_data = None
1676        """Data describing composition of cells across clusters or sets."""

1678    @classmethod
1679    def project_dir(cls, path_to_directory, project_list):
1680        """
1681        Scan a directory and build a COMPsc instance mapping provided project names
1682        to their paths.
1683
1684        Parameters
1685        ----------
1686        path_to_directory : str
1687            Path containing project subfolders.
1688
1689        project_list : list[str]
1690            List of filenames (folder names) to include in the returned object map.
1691
1692        Returns
1693        -------
1694        COMPsc
1695            New COMPsc instance with `objects` populated.
1696
1697        Raises
1698        ------
1699        Exception
1700            A generic exception is caught and a message printed if scanning fails.
1701
1702        Notes
1703        -----
1704        Function attempts to match entries in `project_list` to directory
1705        names and constructs a simplified object key from the folder name.
1706        """
1707        try:
1708            objects = {}
1709            for filename in tqdm(os.listdir(path_to_directory)):
1710                for c in project_list:
1711                    f = os.path.join(path_to_directory, filename)
1712                    if c == filename and os.path.isdir(f):
1713                        objects[str(c)] = f
1714
1715            return cls(objects)
1716
1717        except:
1718            print("Something went wrong. Check the function input data and try again!")
1719
1720    def save_project(self, name, path: str = os.getcwd()):
1721        """
1722        Save the COMPsc object to disk using pickle.
1723
1724        Parameters
1725        ----------
1726        name : str
1727            Base filename (without extension) to use when saving.
1728
1729        path : str, default os.getcwd()
1730            Directory in which to save the project file.
1731
1732        Returns
1733        -------
1734        None
1735
1736        Side Effects
1737        ------------
1738        - Writes a file `<path>/<name>.jpkl` containing the pickled object.
1739        - Prints a confirmation message with saved path.
1740        """
1741
1742        full = os.path.join(path, f"{name}.jpkl")
1743
1744        with open(full, "wb") as f:
1745            pickle.dump(self, f)
1746
1747        print(f"Project saved as {full}")
1748
1749    @classmethod
1750    def load_project(cls, path):
1751        """
1752        Load a previously saved COMPsc project from a pickle file.
1753
1754        Parameters
1755        ----------
1756        path : str
1757            Full path to the pickled project file.
1758
1759        Returns
1760        -------
1761        COMPsc
1762            The unpickled COMPsc object.
1763
1764        Raises
1765        ------
1766        FileNotFoundError
1767            If the provided path does not exist.
1768        """
1769
1770        if not os.path.exists(path):
1771            raise FileNotFoundError("File does not exist!")
1772        with open(path, "rb") as f:
1773            obj = pickle.load(f)
1774        return obj

1776    def reduce_cols(
1777        self,
1778        reg: str | None = None,
1779        full: str | None = None,
1780        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
1781        inc_set: bool = False,
1782    ):
1783        """
1784        Remove columns (cells) whose names contain a substring `reg` or
1785        full name `full` from available tables.
1786
1787        Parameters
1788        ----------
1789        reg : str | None
1790            Substring to search for in column/cell names; matching columns will be removed.
1791            If not None, `full` must be None.
1792
1793        full : str | None
1794            Full name to search for in column/cell names; matching columns will be removed.
1795            If not None, `reg` must be None.
1796
1797        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
1798            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
1799
1800        inc_set : bool, default False
1801            If True, column names are interpreted as 'cell_name # set' when matching.
1802
1803        Update
1804        ------------
1805        Mutates `self.input_data`, `self.normalized_data`, `self.input_metadata`,
1806        `self.agg_normalized_data`, and `self.agg_metadata` (if they exist),
1807        removing columns/rows that match `reg`.
1808
1809        Raises
1810        ------
1811        Raises ValueError if nothing matches the reduction mask.
1812        """
1813
1814        if reg is None and full is None:
1815            raise ValueError(
1816                "Both 'reg' and 'full' arguments not provided. Please provide at least one of them!"
1817            )
1818
1819        if reg is not None and full is not None:
1820            raise ValueError(
1821                "Both 'reg' and 'full' arguments are provided. "
1822                "Please provide only one of them!\n"
1823                "'reg' is used when only part of the name must be detected.\n"
1824                "'full' is used if the full name must be detected."
1825            )
1826
1827        if reg is not None:
1828
1829            if self.input_data is not None:
1830
1831                if inc_set:
1832
1833                    self.input_data.columns = (
1834                        self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1835                        + " # "
1836                        + self.input_metadata["sets"]
1837                    )
1838
1839                else:
1840
1841                    self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1842
1843                mask = [reg.upper() not in x.upper() for x in self.input_data.columns]
1844
1845                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
1846                    raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
1847
1848                self.input_data = self.input_data.loc[:, mask]
1849
1850            if self.normalized_data is not None:
1851
1852                if inc_set:
1853
1854                    self.normalized_data.columns = (
1855                        self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1856                        + " # "
1857                        + self.input_metadata["sets"]
1858                    )
1859
1860                else:
1861
1862                    self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1863
1864                mask = [
1865                    reg.upper() not in x.upper() for x in self.normalized_data.columns
1866                ]
1867
1868                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
1869                    raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
1870
1871                self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.loc[:, mask]
1872
1873            if self.input_metadata is not None:
1874
1875                if inc_set:
1876
1877                    self.input_metadata["drop"] = (
1878                        self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1879                        + " # "
1880                        + self.input_metadata["sets"]
1881                    )
1882
1883                else:
1884
1885                    self.input_metadata["drop"] = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1886
1887                mask = [
1888                    reg.upper() not in x.upper() for x in self.input_metadata["drop"]
1889                ]
1890
1891                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
1892                    raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
1893
1894                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.loc[mask, :].reset_index(
1895                    drop=True
1896                )
1897
1898                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.drop(
1899                    columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
1900                )
1901
1902            if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
1903
1904                if inc_set:
1905
1906                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = (
1907                        self.agg_metadata[name_slot] + " # " + self.agg_metadata["sets"]
1908                    )
1909
1910                else:
1911
1912                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata[name_slot]
1913
1914                mask = [
1915                    reg.upper() not in x.upper()
1916                    for x in self.agg_normalized_data.columns
1917                ]
1918
1919                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
1920                    raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
1921
1922                self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.loc[:, mask]
1923
1924            if self.agg_metadata is not None:
1925
1926                if inc_set:
1927
1928                    self.agg_metadata["drop"] = (
1929                        self.agg_metadata[name_slot] + " # " + self.agg_metadata["sets"]
1930                    )
1931
1932                else:
1933
1934                    self.agg_metadata["drop"] = self.agg_metadata[name_slot]
1935
1936                mask = [reg.upper() not in x.upper() for x in self.agg_metadata["drop"]]
1937
1938                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
1939                    raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
1940
1941                self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.loc[mask, :].reset_index(
1942                    drop=True
1943                )
1944
1945                self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.drop(
1946                    columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
1947                )
1948
1949        elif full is not None:
1950
1951            if self.input_data is not None:
1952
1953                if inc_set:
1954
1955                    self.input_data.columns = (
1956                        self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1957                        + " # "
1958                        + self.input_metadata["sets"]
1959                    )
1960
1961                    if "#" not in full:
1962
1963                        self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1964
1965                        print(
1966                            "Not include the set info (name # set) in the 'full' argument, where 'inc_set' is True"
1967                            "Only the names will be compared, without considering the set information."
1968                        )
1969
1970                else:
1971
1972                    self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1973

2211    def get_partial_data(
2212        self,
2213        names: list | str | None = None,
2214        features: list | str | None = None,
2215        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
2216        inc_metadata: bool = False,
2217    ):
2218        """
2219        Return a subset of the data filtered by sample names and/or feature names.
2220
2221        Parameters
2222        ----------
2223        names : list, str, or None
2224            Names of samples to include. If None, all samples are considered.
2225
2226        features : list, str, or None
2227            Names of features to include. If None, all features are considered.
2228
2229        name_slot : str
2230            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
2231
2232        inc_metadata : bool
2233            If True return tuple (data, metadata)
2234
2235        Returns
2236        -------
2237        pandas.DataFrame
2238            Subset of the normalized data based on the specified names and features.
2239        """
2240
2241        data = self.normalized_data.copy()
2242        metadata = self.input_metadata
2243
2244        if name_slot in self.input_metadata.columns:
2245            data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2246        else:
2247            raise ValueError("'name_slot' not occured in data!'")
2248
2249        if isinstance(features, str):
2250            features = [features]
2251        elif features is None:
2252            features = []
2253
2254        if isinstance(names, str):
2255            names = [names]
2256        elif names is None:
2257            names = []
2258
2259        features = [x.upper() for x in features]
2260        names = [x.upper() for x in names]
2261
2262        columns_names = [x.upper() for x in data.columns]
2263        features_names = [x.upper() for x in data.index]
2264
2265        columns_bool = [True if x in names else False for x in columns_names]
2266        features_bool = [True if x in features else False for x in features_names]
2267
2268        if True not in columns_bool and True not in features_bool:
2269            print("Missing 'names' and/or 'features'. Returning full dataset instead.")
2270
2271        if True in columns_bool:
2272            data = data.loc[:, columns_bool]
2273            metadata = metadata.loc[columns_bool, :]
2274
2275        if True in features_bool:
2276            data = data.loc[features_bool, :]
2277
2278        not_in_features = [y for y in features if y not in features_names]
2279
2280        if len(not_in_features) > 0:
2281            print("\nThe following features were not found in data:")
2282            print("\n".join(not_in_features))
2283
2284        not_in_names = [y for y in names if y not in columns_names]
2285
2286        if len(not_in_names) > 0:
2287            print("\nThe following names were not found in data:")
2288            print("\n".join(not_in_names))
2289
2290        if inc_metadata:
2291            return data, metadata
2292        else:
2293            return data
