4638    def bar_composition(
4639        self,
4640        cmap="tab20b",
4641        width=2,
4642        height=6,
4643        font_size=15,
4644        legend_split_col: int = 1,
4645        legend_bbox: tuple = (1.3, 1),
4646    ):
4647        """
4648        Visualize the composition of cell lineages using bar plots.
4649
4650        Produces bar plots showing the distribution of features stored in
4651        `self.composition_data`. If multiple sets are present, a separate
4652        bar is drawn for each set. Percentages are annotated alongside the bars.
4653
4654        Parameters
4655        ----------
4656        cmap : str, default 'tab20b'
4657            Colormap used for stacked bars.
4658
4659        width : int, default 2
4660            Width of each subplot (per set).
4661
4662        height : int, default 6
4663            Height of the figure.
4664
4665        font_size : int, default 15
4666            Font size for labels and annotations.
4667
4668        legend_split_col : int, default 1
4669            Number of columns in the legend.
4670
4671        legend_bbox : tuple, default (1.3, 1)
4672            Bounding box anchor position for the legend.
4673
4674        Returns
4675        -------
4676        matplotlib.figure.Figure
4677            Stacked bar plot visualization of composition data.
4678        """
4679
4680        df = self.composition_data
4681        df["num"] = range(1, len(df) + 1)
4682
4683        if "set" in df.columns and len(set(df["set"])) > 1:
4684
4685            sets = list(set(df["set"]))
4686            fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(sets), figsize=(width * len(sets), height))
4687
4688            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4689
4690            set_nam = len(set(df["name"]))
4691
4692            legend_labels = list(set(df["name"]))
4693
4694            colors = [cmap(i / set_nam) for i in range(set_nam)]
4695
4696            cmap_dict = dict(zip(legend_labels, colors))
4697
4698            for idx, s in enumerate(sets):
4699                ax = axes[idx]
4700
4701                tmp_df = df[df["set"] == s].reset_index(drop=True)
4702
4703                values = tmp_df["n"].values
4704                total = sum(values)
4705                values = [v / total * 100 for v in values]
4706                values = [round(v, 2) for v in values]
4707
4708                idx_max = np.argmax(values)
4709                correction = 100 - sum(values)
4710                values[idx_max] += correction
4711
4712                names = tmp_df["name"].values
4713                perc = tmp_df["pct"].values
4714                nums = tmp_df["num"].values
4715
4716                bottom = 0
4717                centers = []
4718                for name, num, val, color in zip(names, nums, values, colors):
4719                    ax.bar(s, val, bottom=bottom, color=cmap_dict[name], label=name)
4720                    centers.append(bottom + val / 2)
4721                    bottom += val
4722
4723                y_positions = np.linspace(centers[0], centers[-1], len(centers))
4724                x_text = -0.8
4725
4726                for y_label, y_center, pct, num in zip(
4727                    y_positions, centers, perc, nums
4728                ):
4729                    ax.annotate(
4730                        f"{pct:.1f}%",
4731                        xy=(0, y_center),
4732                        xycoords="data",
4733                        xytext=(x_text, y_label),
4734                        textcoords="data",
4735                        ha="right",
4736                        va="center",
4737                        fontsize=font_size,
4738                        arrowprops=dict(
4739                            arrowstyle="->",
4740                            lw=1,
4741                            color="black",
4742                            connectionstyle="angle3,angleA=0,angleB=90",
4743                        ),
4744                    )
4745
4746                ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
4747                ax.set_xlabel(s, fontsize=font_size)
4748                ax.xaxis.label.set_rotation(30)
4749
4750                ax.set_xticks([])
4751                ax.set_yticks([])
4752                for spine in ax.spines.values():
4753                    spine.set_visible(False)
4754
4755            legend_handles = [
4756                Patch(facecolor=cmap_dict[label], edgecolor="black", label=label)
4757                for label in legend_labels
4758            ]
4759
4760            fig.legend(
4761                handles=legend_handles,
4762                loc="center right",
4763                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4764                ncol=legend_split_col,
4765                title="",
4766            )
4767
4768            plt.tight_layout()
4769            plt.show()
4770
4771        else:
4772
4773            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4774
4775            colors = [cmap(i / len(df)) for i in range(len(df))]
4776
4777            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
4778
4779            values = df["n"].values
4780            names = df["name"].values
4781            perc = df["pct"].values
4782            nums = df["num"].values
4783
4784            bottom = 0
4785            centers = []
4786            for name, num, val, color in zip(names, nums, values, colors):
4787                ax.bar(0, val, bottom=bottom, color=color, label=f"{num}) {name}")
4788                centers.append(bottom + val / 2)
4789                bottom += val
4790
4791            y_positions = np.linspace(centers[0], centers[-1], len(centers))
4792            x_text = -0.8
4793
4794            for y_label, y_center, pct, num in zip(y_positions, centers, perc, nums):
4795                ax.annotate(
4796                    f"{num}) {pct}",
4797                    xy=(0, y_center),
4798                    xycoords="data",
4799                    xytext=(x_text, y_label),
4800                    textcoords="data",
4801                    ha="right",
4802                    va="center",
4803                    fontsize=9,
4804                    arrowprops=dict(
4805                        arrowstyle="->",
4806                        lw=1,
4807                        color="black",
4808                        connectionstyle="angle3,angleA=0,angleB=90",
4809                    ),
4810                )
4811
4812            ax.set_xticks([])
4813            ax.set_yticks([])
4814            for spine in ax.spines.values():
4815                spine.set_visible(False)
4816
4817            ax.legend(
4818                title="Legend",
4819                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4820                loc="upper left",
4821                ncol=legend_split_col,
4822            )
4823
4824            plt.tight_layout()
4825            plt.show()
4826
4827        return fig

4829    def cell_regression(
4830        self,
4831        cell_x: str,
4832        cell_y: str,
4833        set_x: str | None = None,
4834        set_y: str | None = None,
4835        min_log=0.5,
4836        n_max=20,
4837        min_exp=0.1,
4838        min_pct=0.5,
4839        n_proc=10,
4840        min_esm=0.5,
4841        p_val=0.05,
4842        adj=True,
4843        image_width=12,
4844        image_high=7,
4845    ):
4846        """
4847        Perform linear regression between two selected cell populations and identify
4848        significant and top-ranked differentially expressed genes.
4849
4850        The function compares the expression profiles of two selected cells or cell
4851        populations using linear regression. Each gene is represented as a point in
4852        the regression plot, with expression in `cell_x` on the X-axis and expression
4853        in `cell_y` on the Y-axis.
4854
4855        Differential expression statistics are calculated using `calc_DEG`. Genes are
4856        first filtered according to the minimum absolute log fold change, minimum
4857        absolute effect size (ESM), and statistical significance. Among the
4858        significant genes, up to `n_max` genes are selected within each `valid_group`,
4859        prioritizing genes with the largest standardized absolute regression residuals
4860        and absolute ESM values.
4861
4862        The regression plot uses three point categories:
4863        - gray: genes that are not statistically significant,
4864        - green: statistically significant genes that pass the DEG thresholds,
4865        - blue: top `n_max` genes selected within each `valid_group`.
4866
4867        The selected top genes are additionally annotated with their gene names.
4868        The plot also displays the fitted linear regression line, R-squared,
4869        p-value, and regression equation.
4870
4871        Parameters
4872        ----------
4873        cell_x : str
4874            Name of the first cell or cell population used as the X-axis.
4875
4876        cell_y : str
4877            Name of the second cell or cell population used as the Y-axis.
4878
4879        set_x : str or None
4880            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_x`.
4881            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4882            the cell is selected only by its name.
4883
4884        set_y : str or None
4885            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_y`.
4886            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4887            the cell is selected only by its name.
4888
4889        min_log : float, default=0.5
4890            Minimum absolute log fold change required for a gene to be considered
4891            for significant DEG selection.
4892
4893        n_max : int, default=20
4894            Maximum number of top genes selected from each `valid_group`.
4895            Genes are ranked primarily by standardized absolute regression residual
4896            and secondarily by absolute Effect Size - Cohen's d.
4897
4898        min_exp : float, default=0.1
4899            Minimum expression threshold passed to `calc_DEG`.
4900
4901        min_pct : float, default=0.5
4902            Minimum fraction of cells in which a gene must be expressed, passed to
4903            `calc_DEG`.
4904
4905        n_proc : int, default=10
4906            Number of parallel processes used by `calc_DEG`.
4907
4908        min_esm : float, default=0.5
4909            Minimum absolute ESM (effect size measure) required for DEG selection.
4910
4911        p_val : float, default=0.05
4912            Maximum allowed p-value for statistical significance. If `adj=True`,
4913            this threshold is applied to the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`);
4914            otherwise, it is applied to the raw p-value (`p_val`).
4915
4916        adj : bool, default=True
4917            Whether to use the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`) instead of the raw
4918            p-value (`p_val`) for statistical significance filtering.
4919
4920        image_width : int or float, default=12
4921            Width of the regression plot in inches.
4922
4923        image_high : int or float, default=7
4924            Height of the regression plot in inches.
4925
4926
4927
4928        Returns
4929        -------
4930        deg_stats : pandas.DataFrame
4931            DataFrame containing the DEG statistics after filtering by absolute
4932            log fold change, absolute ESM, and statistical significance.
4933
4934        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
4935            Matplotlib figure containing the regression plot, including expression
4936            points, regression line, regression statistics, and annotations for
4937            the selected top genes.
4938
4939        Raises
4940        ------
4941        ValueError
4942            If `cell_x` or `cell_y` is not found in the dataset.
4943
4944        ValueError
4945            If multiple columns correspond to the same cell name and the required
4946            dataset identifiers (`set_x` and/or `set_y`) were not provided.
4947
4948        Notes
4949        -----
4950        * The function calls `self.average()` before performing the analysis.
4951        * Linear regression is calculated using `scipy.stats.linregress`.
4952        * Regression residuals are calculated as the difference between the observed
4953        Y value and the value predicted by the fitted regression model.
4954        * Standardized residuals are used to prioritize genes that deviate most
4955        strongly from the expected linear relationship.
4956        * Significant genes are filtered using absolute log fold change, absolute
4957        ESM, and either raw or adjusted p-value.
4958        * Top genes are selected separately within each `valid_group`.
4959        * The top genes are annotated on the regression plot.
4960        * The returned `deg_stats` contains the significant genes before the final
4961        `n_max` per-group selection.
4962
4963
4964        Examples
4965        --------
4966        > > > deg_stats, fig = obj.cell_regression(
4967        > > > ...     cell_x="NeuronA",
4968        > > > ...     cell_y="NeuronB",
4969        > > > ...     min_log_min=0.5,
4970        > > > ...     min_esm=0.5,
4971        > > > ...     p_val=0.05,
4972        > > > ...     n_max=20
4973        > > > ... )
4974        > > >
4975        """
4976
4977        self.average()
4978
4979        metadata = self.agg_metadata
4980        data = self.agg_normalized_data
4981        data2 = self.normalized_data
4982        metadata2 = self.input_metadata
4983
4984        if set_x is not None and set_y is not None:
4985            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
4986            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata2["sets"]
4987            cell_x = cell_x + " # " + set_x
4988            cell_y = cell_y + " # " + set_y
4989
4990            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
4991                data2,
4992                metadata_list=None,
4993                entities={
4994                    "cell_x": cell_x + " # " + set_x,
4995                    "cell_y": cell_y + " # " + set_y,
4996                },
4997                sets=None,
4998                min_exp=min_exp,
4999                min_pct=min_pct,
5000                n_proc=n_proc,
5001            )
5002
5003        else:
5004            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5005            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"]
5006
5007            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
5008                data2,
5009                metadata_list=None,
5010                entities={"cell_x": cell_x, "cell_y": cell_y},
5011                sets=None,
5012                min_exp=min_exp,
5013                min_pct=min_pct,
5014                n_proc=n_proc,
5015            )
5016
5017        # points
5018        x = data[cell_x]
5019        y = data[cell_y]
5020
5021        # regression
5022        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(x, y)
5023
5024        # prediction
5025        y_pred = slope * x + intercept
5026
5027        # residuals
5028        residual = y - y_pred
5029
5030        # residuals for DEG
5031        deg_stats["residual"] = deg_stats["feature"].map(residual)
5032        deg_stats["residual_abs"] = deg_stats["residual"].abs()
5033        deg_stats["residual_std"] = deg_stats["residual"] / residual.std()
5034        deg_stats["residual_std_abs"] = deg_stats["residual_std"].abs()
5035        deg_stats["esm_abs"] = deg_stats["esm"].abs()
5036
5037        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["log(FC)"].abs() >= min_log]
5038
5039        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["esm_abs"] >= min_esm]
5040
5041        if adj:
5042
5043            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
5044        else:
5045            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["p_val"] <= p_val]
5046
5047        deg_stats_n = (
5048            deg_stats.sort_values(
5049                ["residual_std_abs", "esm_abs"], ascending=[False, False]
5050            )
5051            .groupby("valid_group")
5052            .head(n_max)
5053        )
5054
5055        if not cell_x in data.columns:
5056            raise ValueError("'cell_x' value not in cell names!")
5057
5058        if not cell_y in data.columns:
5059            raise ValueError("'cell_y' value not in cell names!")
5060
5061        if list(data.columns).count(cell_x) > 1:
5062            raise ValueError(
5063                f"'{cell_x}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5064                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5065            )
5066
5067        if list(data.columns).count(cell_y) > 1:
5068            raise ValueError(
5069                f"'{cell_y}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5070                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5071            )
5072
5073        data["color"] = "gray"
5074
5075        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats["feature"])), "color"] = "green"
5076
5077        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats_n["feature"])), "color"] = "blue"
5078
5079        color_order = {"gray": 0, "green": 1, "blue": 2}
5080
5081        data["color_order"] = data["color"].map(color_order)
5082
5083        data = data.sort_values("color_order")
5084
5085        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5086
5087        # dots
5088        sns.scatterplot(
5089            x=cell_x,
5090            y=cell_y,
5091            data=data,
5092            hue="color",
5093            palette={"blue": "blue", "green": "green", "gray": "gray"},
5094            legend=False,
5095            ax=ax,
5096        )
5097
5098        # regression
5099        sns.regplot(x=cell_x, y=cell_y, data=data, scatter=False, color="red", ax=ax)
5100
5101        legend_elements = [
5102            Line2D(
5103                [0],
5104                [0],
5105                marker="o",
5106                color="w",
5107                markerfacecolor="gray",
5108                markersize=7,
5109                label="Not significant",
5110            ),
5111            Line2D(
5112                [0],
5113                [0],
5114                marker="o",
5115                color="w",
5116                markerfacecolor="blue",
5117                markersize=7,
5118                label="Top significant",
5119            ),
5120            Line2D(
5121                [0],
5122                [0],
5123                marker="o",
5124                color="w",
5125                markerfacecolor="green",
5126                markersize=7,
5127                label="Significant",
5128            ),
5129            Line2D([0], [0], color="red", linewidth=2, label="Linear regression"),
5130        ]
5131
5132        ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="best", frameon=False)
5133
5134        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, _ = stats.linregress(
5135            data[cell_x], data[cell_y]
5136        )
5137
5138        equation = "y = {:.2f}x + {:.2f}".format(slope, intercept)
5139
5140        ax.annotate(
5141            "R-squared = {:.2f}\nP-value = {:.2f}\n{}".format(
5142                r_value**2, p_value, equation
5143            ),
5144            xy=(0.05, 0.90),
5145            xycoords="axes fraction",
5146            fontsize=12,
5147        )
5148
5149        ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
5150        ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
5151
5152        # oznaczanie genów
5153        def annotate_outliers(x, y, features):
5154            texts = []
5155
5156            for i, (xi, yi) in enumerate(zip(x, y)):
5157                if data.index[i] in features:
5158                    text = ax.text(xi, yi, data.index[i])
5159                    texts.append(text)
5160
5161            return texts
5162
5163        features = list(set(deg_stats_n["feature"]))
5164
5165        texts = annotate_outliers(data[cell_x], data[cell_y], features)
5166
5167        adjust_text(texts, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", alpha=0.5))
5168
5169        return deg_stats, fig
5170
5171    def cell_genes_distribution(
5172        self,
5173        cells_names: list | None,
5174        cells_sets: list | None = None,
5175        image_width=10,
5176        image_high=7,
5177    ):
5178        """
5179        Compare the distributions of the number of detected genes per cell across
5180        selected cell populations.
5181
5182        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the number of
5183        detected genes in each cell, defined as the number of genes with an expression
5184        value greater than zero. The resulting distributions are visualized as
5185        overlapping histograms, allowing the gene detection levels of different cell
5186        populations to be compared.
5187
5188        This analysis can be used as a quality-control step before comparing gene
5189        expression profiles or performing differential expression analysis. Similar
5190        distributions of detected genes per cell indicate comparable levels of gene
5191        detection across the selected populations, whereas substantial differences
5192        may indicate differences in sequencing depth, RNA content, or other technical
5193        factors.
5194
5195        Parameters
5196        ----------
5197        cells_names : list
5198            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5199
5200        cells_sets : list or None
5201            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5202            element-wise to `cells_names`. This is required when the same cell
5203            population name occurs in multiple datasets and a specific dataset
5204            needs to be selected.
5205
5206        image_width : int or float, default=10
5207            Width of the histogram figure in inches.
5208
5209        image_high : int or float, default=7
5210            Height of the histogram figure in inches.
5211
5212        Returns
5213        -------
5214        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5215            Matplotlib figure containing overlapping histograms showing the
5216            distribution of the number of detected genes per cell for each selected
5217            cell population.
5218
5219        Raises
5220        ------
5221        ValueError
5222            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5223
5224        Notes
5225        -----
5226        * A gene is considered detected when its expression value is greater than zero.
5227        * The number of detected genes is calculated independently for every cell.
5228        * Each selected cell population is represented by a separate histogram.
5229        * When `cells_sets` is provided and has the same length as `cells_names`,
5230        cell populations are selected using both their population name and dataset
5231        identifier.
5232        * The function operates on `self.normalized_data`.
5233        * The resulting distributions can be used to assess whether selected cell
5234        populations have comparable gene-detection levels before downstream
5235        comparisons.
5236        """
5237
5238        metadata = self.input_metadata
5239        data = self.normalized_data
5240
5241        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5242            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5243
5244        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5245            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5246            full_cells = []
5247            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5248                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5249
5250            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5251
5252        else:
5253            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5254            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5255
5256        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5257
5258        for name in data.columns.unique():
5259            cols = data.columns == name
5260
5261            counts = (data.loc[:, cols] > 0).sum(axis=0)
5262
5263            plt.hist(counts, bins=30, alpha=0.5, label=name)
5264
5265        plt.xlabel("Number of detected genes per cell")
5266        plt.ylabel("Number of cells")
5267        plt.legend()
5268        plt.tight_layout()
5269
5270        return fig
5271
5272    def mm_cell_genes(
5273        self,
5274        cells_names: list | None,
5275        cells_sets: list | None,
5276        non_include_zeros: bool = True,
5277        image_width=7,
5278        image_high=10,
5279    ):
5280        """
5281        Compare the mean and median gene expression across selected cell populations.
5282
5283        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the mean and median
5284        expression values across all genes and cells. By default, zero-expression
5285        values are excluded from the calculation, allowing the comparison to focus on
5286        genes with detected expression. When `non_include_zeros` is set to False, zero
5287        values are included in the calculation.
5288
5289        The resulting mean and median expression values are visualized as a grouped
5290        bar plot, with separate bars representing the mean and median for each cell
5291        population. This visualization can be used to assess differences in the overall
5292        expression level and distribution between selected cell populations.
5293
5294        Parameters
5295        ----------
5296        cells_names : list
5297            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5298
5299        cells_sets : list or None
5300            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5301            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5302            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5303            name and dataset identifier.
5304
5305        non_include_zeros : bool, default=True
5306            Whether to exclude zero-expression values before calculating the mean and
5307            median. If True, only non-zero expression values are used. If False, all
5308            expression values, including zeros, are used.
5309
5310        image_width : int or float, default=7
5311            Width of the figure in inches.
5312
5313        image_high : int or float, default=10
5314            Height of the figure in inches.
5315
5316        Returns
5317        -------
5318        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5319            Matplotlib figure containing grouped bar plots showing the mean and median
5320            expression for each selected cell population.
5321
5322        Raises
5323        ------
5324        ValueError
5325            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5326
5327        Notes
5328        -----
5329        * Expression values are obtained from `self.normalized_data`.
5330        * The mean and median are calculated independently for each selected cell
5331        population.
5332        * When `non_include_zeros=True`, zero-expression values are excluded before
5333        calculating both statistics.
5334        * When `non_include_zeros=False`, zero-expression values contribute to both
5335        the mean and median.
5336        * The analysis uses all genes and cells belonging to each selected population.
5337        * The resulting statistics describe the overall distribution of expression
5338        values and can be used to compare the expression levels of different cell
5339        populations.
5340        """
5341
5342        metadata = self.input_metadata
5343        data = self.normalized_data
5344
5345        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5346            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5347
5348        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5349            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5350            full_cells = []
5351            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5352                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5353
5354            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5355
5356        else:
5357            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5358            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5359
5360        groups = data.columns.unique()
5361
5362        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5363
5364        mean_expression = {}
5365        median_expression = {}
5366
5367        for name in groups:
5368            cols = data.columns == name
5369
5370            values = data.loc[:, cols].values.flatten()
5371
5372            if non_include_zeros:
5373                values = values[values != 0]
5374
5375            mean_expression[name] = values.mean()
5376            median_expression[name] = np.median(values)
5377
5378        mean_expression = pd.Series(mean_expression)
5379        median_expression = pd.Series(median_expression)
5380
5381        x = np.arange(len(groups))
5382        width = 0.35
5383
5384        plt.bar(x - width / 2, mean_expression.values, width, label="Mean")
5385
5386        plt.bar(x + width / 2, median_expression.values, width, label="Median")
5387
5388        plt.xlabel("Cell")
5389        plt.ylabel("Expression")
5390        plt.xticks(x, groups, rotation=45)
5391        plt.legend()
5392
5393        plt.tight_layout()
5394
5395        return fig
5396
5397    def cell_dispersion(
5398        self,
5399        cells_names: list | None,
5400        cells_sets: list | None,
5401        image_width=7,
5402        image_high=10,
5403    ):
5404        """
5405        Assess the within-cluster dispersion of cell gene expression profiles.
5406
5407        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the centroid of
5408        the population as the mean expression profile across all cells in the cluster.
5409        The Euclidean distance between each individual cell and its corresponding
5410        cluster centroid is then calculated to quantify how much the cell's expression
5411        profile deviates from the average profile of the cluster.
5412
5413        The resulting distributions of distances are visualized using violin plots,
5414        with each violin representing one selected cell population. The distribution
5415        shows the degree of transcriptional heterogeneity within each cluster:
5416        smaller distances indicate cells with more similar expression profiles,
5417        whereas larger distances indicate greater within-cluster variability.
5418
5419        This analysis can be used to assess the internal consistency and transcriptional
5420        heterogeneity of cell populations before comparing their expression profiles
5421        between clusters.
5422
5423        Parameters
5424        ----------
5425        self : object
5426            self object containing the input metadata and normalized expression
5427            data.
5428
5429        cells_names : list
5430            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5431
5432        cells_sets : list or None
5433            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5434            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5435            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5436            name and dataset identifier.
5437
5438        image_width : int or float, default=7
5439            Width of the figure in inches.
5440
5441        image_high : int or float, default=10
5442            Height of the figure in inches.
5443
5444        Returns
5445        -------
5446        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5447            Matplotlib figure containing violin plots showing the distribution of
5448            Euclidean distances between individual cells and their respective cluster
5449            centroids.
5450
5451        Raises
5452        ------
5453        ValueError
5454            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5455
5456        Notes
5457        -----
5458        * Expression values are obtained from `self.normalized_data`.
5459        * A cluster centroid is calculated as the mean expression profile across all
5460        cells belonging to that cluster.
5461        * The distance of each cell from the centroid is calculated using Euclidean
5462        distance across all genes.
5463        * Each cell contributes one distance value to the distribution of its cluster.
5464        * Smaller distances indicate lower within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5465        * Larger distances indicate greater within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5466        * The violin plot includes a box plot showing the median and interquartile
5467        range of the distance distribution.
5468        * Differences in dispersion between clusters can be used to assess their
5469        relative transcriptional homogeneity before downstream comparisons.
5470        """
5471
5472        metadata = self.input_metadata
5473        data = self.normalized_data
5474
5475        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5476            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5477
5478        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5479            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5480            full_cells = []
5481            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5482                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5483
5484            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5485
5486        else:
5487            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5488            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5489
5490        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5491
5492        dispersion_long = []
5493
5494        for cluster in data.columns.unique():
5495
5496            cells = data.loc[:, data.columns == cluster]
5497
5498            centroid = cells.mean(axis=1)
5499
5500            distances = np.sqrt(((cells.sub(centroid, axis=0)) ** 2).sum(axis=0))
5501
5502            for cell, distance in distances.items():
5503                dispersion_long.append(
5504                    {"cluster": cluster, "cell": cell, "distance_to_centroid": distance}
5505                )
5506
5507        dispersion_long = pd.DataFrame(dispersion_long)
5508
5509        sns.violinplot(
5510            data=dispersion_long, x="cluster", y="distance_to_centroid", inner="box"
5511        )
5512
5513        plt.ylabel("Distance from cluster centroid")
5514        plt.xlabel("Cluster")
5515        plt.xticks(rotation=45)
5516        plt.tight_layout()
5517
5518        return fig
class Clustering: 
  35class Clustering:
  36    """
  37    A class for performing dimensionality reduction, clustering, and visualization
  38    on high-dimensional data (e.g., single-cell gene expression).
  39
  40    The class provides methods for:
  41    - Normalizing and extracting subsets of data
  42    - Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and related clustering
  43    - Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) and clustering
  44    - Visualization of PCA and UMAP embeddings
  45    - Harmonization of batch effects
  46    - Accessing processed data and cluster labels
  47
  48    Methods
  49    -------
  50    add_data_frame(data, metadata)
  51        Class method to create a Clustering instance from a DataFrame and metadata.
  52
  53    harmonize_sets()
  54        Perform batch effect harmonization on PCA data.
  55
  56    perform_PCA(pc_num=100, width=8, height=6)
  57        Perform PCA on the dataset and visualize the first two PCs.
  58
  59    knee_plot_PCA(width=8, height=6)
  60        Plot the cumulative variance explained by PCs to determine optimal dimensionality.
  61
  62    find_clusters_PCA(pc_num=0, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6, harmonized=False)
  63        Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize results.
  64
  65    perform_UMAP(factorize=False, umap_num=100, pc_num=0, harmonized=False, ...)
  66        Compute UMAP embeddings with optional parameter tuning.
  67
  68    knee_plot_umap(eps=0.5, min_samples=10)
  69        Determine optimal UMAP dimensionality using silhouette scores.
  70
  71    find_clusters_UMAP(umap_n=5, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6)
  72        Apply DBSCAN clustering on UMAP embeddings and visualize clusters.
  73
  74    UMAP_vis(names_slot='cell_names', set_sep=True, point_size=0.6, ...)
  75        Visualize UMAP embeddings with labels and optional cluster numbering.
  76
  77    UMAP_feature(feature_name, features_data=None, point_size=0.6, ...)
  78        Plot a single feature over UMAP coordinates with customizable colormap.
  79
  80    get_umap_data()
  81        Return the UMAP embeddings along with cluster labels if available.
  82
  83    get_pca_data()
  84        Return the PCA results along with cluster labels if available.
  85
  86    return_clusters(clusters='umap')
  87        Return the cluster labels for UMAP or PCA embeddings.
  88
  89    Raises
  90    ------
  91    ValueError
  92        For invalid parameters, mismatched dimensions, or missing metadata.
  93    """
  94
  95    def __init__(self, data, metadata):
  96        """
  97        Initialize the clustering class with data and optional metadata.
  98
  99        Parameters
 100        ----------
 101        data : pandas.DataFrame
 102            Input data for clustering. Columns are considered as samples.
 103
 104        metadata : pandas.DataFrame, optional
 105            Metadata for the samples. If None, a default DataFrame with column
 106            names as 'cell_names' is created.
 107
 108        Attributes
 109        ----------
 110        -clustering_data : pandas.DataFrame
 111        -clustering_metadata : pandas.DataFrame
 112        -subclusters : None or dict
 113        -explained_var : None or numpy.ndarray
 114        -cumulative_var : None or numpy.ndarray
 115        -pca : None or pandas.DataFrame
 116        -harmonized_pca : None or pandas.DataFrame
 117        -umap : None or pandas.DataFrame
 118        """
 119
 120        self.clustering_data = data
 121        """The input data used for clustering."""
 122
 123        if metadata is None:
 124            metadata = pd.DataFrame({"cell_names": list(data.columns)})
 125
 126        self.clustering_metadata = metadata
 127        """Metadata associated with the samples."""
 128
 129        self.subclusters = None
 130        """Placeholder for storing subcluster information."""
 131
 132        self.explained_var = None
 133        """Explained variance from PCA, initialized as None."""
 134
 135        self.cumulative_var = None
 136        """Cumulative explained variance from PCA, initialized as None."""
 137
 138        self.pca = None
 139        """PCA-transformed data, initialized as None."""
 140
 141        self.harmonized_pca = None
 142        """PCA data after batch effect harmonization, initialized as None."""
 143
 144        self.umap = None
 145        """UMAP embeddings, initialized as None."""
 146
 147    @classmethod
 148    def add_data_frame(cls, data: pd.DataFrame, metadata: pd.DataFrame | None):
 149        """
 150        Create a Clustering instance from a DataFrame and optional metadata.
 151
 152        Parameters
 153        ----------
 154        data : pandas.DataFrame
 155            Input data with features as rows and samples/cells as columns.
 156
 157        metadata : pandas.DataFrame or None
 158            Optional metadata for the samples.
 159            Each row corresponds to a sample/cell, and column names in this DataFrame
 160            should match the sample/cell names in `data`. Columns can contain additional
 161            information such as cell type, experimental condition, batch, sets, etc.
 162
 163        Returns
 164        -------
 165        Clustering
 166            A new instance of the Clustering class.
 167        """
 168
 169        return cls(data, metadata)

 171    def sort_data(
 172        self,
 173        value_to_sort: str,
 174        ascending: bool = True,
 175        sort_order: list | None = None,
 176    ):
 177        """
 178        Sort metadata and synchronize all associated data matrices and embeddings.
 179
 180        This method reorders sample metadata based on a specified column and
 181        propagates the new sample order across all initialized data slots
 182        (e.g., expression matrices, PCA, harmonized PCA, and UMAP embeddings).
 183
 184        Parameters
 185        ----------
 186        value_to_sort : str
 187            Name of the metadata column used as the sorting key.
 188
 189        ascending : bool, default=True
 190            Sort ascending vs. descending. Ignored if `sort_order` is provided
 191            unless reversed sorting of the custom order is intended.
 192
 193        sort_order : list or None, default=None
 194            Explicit list defining the exact custom order of unique categories
 195            in `value_to_sort`. Must contain the exact same unique values as
 196            the target column.
 197
 198        Raises
 199        ------
 200        ValueError
 201            If `value_to_sort` does not exist in the metadata columns, or if
 202            `sort_order` does not match the unique values present in the column.
 203        """
 204
 205        # methode part for COMPsc project
 206        if "input_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
 207            if value_to_sort not in self.input_metadata.columns:
 208                available_cols = list(self.input_metadata.columns)
 209                raise ValueError(
 210                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in input_metadata. "
 211                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
 212                )
 213
 214            # step 1
 215            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.input_metadata))
 216            self.input_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 217
 218            if self.normalized_data is not None:
 219                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
 220
 221            if self.input_data is not None:
 222                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
 223
 224            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 225                unique_vals = set(self.input_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 226                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 227                    unique_vals
 228                ):
 229                    self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 230                        self.input_metadata[value_to_sort],
 231                        categories=sort_order,
 232                        ordered=True,
 233                    )
 234                    self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
 235                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 236                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 237                else:
 238                    raise ValueError(
 239                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 240                    )
 241            else:
 242                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
 243                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 244                ).reset_index(drop=True)
 245
 246            new_order = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 247
 248            if self.normalized_data is not None:
 249                self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 250                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
 251
 252            if self.input_data is not None:
 253                self.input_data = self.input_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 254                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
 255
 256            self.input_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 257            self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.input_metadata[
 258                value_to_sort
 259            ].astype(str)
 260
 261            # step 2
 262            if self.agg_metadata is not None:
 263                sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.agg_metadata))
 264                self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 265
 266                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
 267                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"]
 268
 269                if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 270                    unique_vals = set(self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 271                    if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 272                        unique_vals
 273                    ):
 274                        self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 275                            self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort],
 276                            categories=sort_order,
 277                            ordered=True,
 278                        )
 279                        self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
 280                            value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 281                        ).reset_index(drop=True)
 282                    else:
 283                        raise ValueError(
 284                            "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 285                        )
 286                else:
 287                    self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
 288                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 289                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 290
 291                new_order = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 292
 293                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
 294                    self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.iloc[
 295                        :, new_order
 296                    ]
 297                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["cell_names"]
 298
 299                self.agg_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 300                self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.agg_metadata[
 301                    value_to_sort
 302                ].astype(str)
 303
 304        # method for Clustering
 305
 306        if "clustering_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
 307            if value_to_sort not in self.clustering_metadata.columns:
 308                available_cols = list(self.clustering_metadata.columns)
 309                raise ValueError(
 310                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in clustering_metadata. "
 311                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
 312                )
 313
 314            # step 1
 315            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.clustering_metadata))
 316            self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
 317
 318            if (
 319                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
 320                and self.clustering_data is not None
 321            ):
 322                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 323
 324            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
 325                tmp_pca = self.pca
 326                tmp_pca.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 327
 328            if (
 329                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
 330                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
 331            ):
 332                tmp_pca_harmonize = self.harmonized_pca
 333                tmp_pca_harmonize.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 334
 335            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
 336                tmp_umap = self.umap
 337                tmp_umap.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
 338
 339            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
 340                unique_vals = set(self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
 341                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
 342                    unique_vals
 343                ):
 344                    self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
 345                        self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort],
 346                        categories=sort_order,
 347                        ordered=True,
 348                    )
 349                    self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
 350                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 351                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
 352                else:
 353                    raise ValueError(
 354                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
 355                    )
 356            else:
 357                self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
 358                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
 359                ).reset_index(drop=True)
 360
 361            new_order = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"].values
 362
 363            if (
 364                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
 365                and self.clustering_data is not None
 366            ):
 367                self.clustering_data = self.clustering_data.iloc[:, new_order]
 368                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["cell_names"]
 369
 370            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
 371                tmp_pca = tmp_pca.loc[new_order, :]
 372                self.pca = tmp_pca.reset_index(drop=True)
 373                del tmp_pca
 374
 375            if (
 376                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
 377                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
 378            ):
 379                tmp_pca_harmonize = tmp_pca_harmonize.loc[new_order, :]
 380                self.harmonized_pca = tmp_pca_harmonize.reset_index(drop=True)
 381                del tmp_pca_harmonize
 382
 383            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
 384                tmp_umap = tmp_umap.loc[new_order, :]
 385                self.umap = tmp_umap.reset_index(drop=True)
 386                del tmp_umap
 387
 388            self.clustering_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
 389            self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.clustering_metadata[
 390                value_to_sort
 391            ].astype(str)

 393    def harmonize_sets(self, batch_col: str = "sets"):
 394        """
 395        Perform batch effect harmonization on PCA embeddings.
 396
 397        Parameters
 398        ----------
 399        batch_col : str, default 'sets'
 400            Name of the column in `metadata` that contains batch information for the samples/cells.
 401
 402        Returns
 403        -------
 404        None
 405            Updates the `harmonized_pca` attribute with harmonized data.
 406        """
 407
 408        data_mat = np.array(self.pca)
 409
 410        metadata = self.clustering_metadata
 411
 412        self.harmonized_pca = pd.DataFrame(
 413            harmonize.run_harmony(data_mat, metadata, vars_use=batch_col).Z_corr
 414        ).T
 415
 416        self.harmonized_pca.columns = self.pca.columns
 417
 418    def perform_PCA(self, pc_num: int = 100, width=8, height=6):
 419        """
 420        Perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the dataset.
 421
 422        This method standardizes the data, applies PCA, stores results as attributes,
 423        and generates a scatter plot of the first two principal components.
 424
 425        Parameters
 426        ----------
 427        pc_num : int, default 100
 428            Number of principal components to compute.
 429            If 0, computes all available components.
 430
 431        width : int or float, default 8
 432            Width of the PCA figure.
 433
 434        height : int or float, default 6
 435            Height of the PCA figure.
 436
 437        Returns
 438        -------
 439        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 440            Scatter plot showing the first two principal components.
 441
 442        Updates
 443        -------
 444        self.pca : pandas.DataFrame
 445            DataFrame with principal component scores for each sample.
 446
 447        self.explained_var : numpy.ndarray
 448            Percentage of variance explained by each principal component.
 449
 450        self.cumulative_var : numpy.ndarray
 451            Cumulative explained variance.
 452        """
 453
 454        scaler = StandardScaler()
 455        data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
 456
 457        if pc_num == 0 or pc_num > data_scaled.shape[0]:
 458            pc_num = data_scaled.shape[0]
 459
 460        pca = PCA(n_components=pc_num, random_state=42)
 461
 462        principal_components = pca.fit_transform(data_scaled)
 463
 464        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(
 465            data=principal_components,
 466            columns=["PC" + str(x + 1) for x in range(pc_num)],
 467        )
 468
 469        self.explained_var = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
 470        self.cumulative_var = np.cumsum(self.explained_var)
 471
 472        self.pca = pca_df
 473
 474        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 475        plt.scatter(pca_df["PC1"], pca_df["PC2"], alpha=0.7)
 476        plt.xlabel("PC 1")
 477        plt.ylabel("PC 2")
 478        plt.grid(True)
 479        plt.show()
 480
 481        return fig
 482
 483    def knee_plot_PCA(self, width: int = 8, height: int = 6):
 484        """
 485        Plot cumulative explained variance to determine the optimal number of PCs.
 486
 487        Parameters
 488        ----------
 489        width : int, default 8
 490            Width of the figure.
 491
 492        height : int or, default 6
 493            Height of the figure.
 494
 495        Returns
 496        -------
 497        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 498            Line plot showing cumulative variance explained by each PC.
 499        """
 500
 501        fig_knee = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 502        plt.plot(range(1, len(self.explained_var) + 1), self.cumulative_var, marker="o")
 503        plt.xlabel("PC (n components)")
 504        plt.ylabel("Cumulative explained variance (%)")
 505        plt.grid(True)
 506
 507        xticks = [1] + list(range(5, len(self.explained_var) + 1, 5))
 508        plt.xticks(xticks, rotation=60)
 509
 510        plt.show()
 511
 512        return fig_knee

 514    def find_clusters_PCA(
 515        self,
 516        pc_num: int = 2,
 517        eps: float = 0.5,
 518        min_samples: int = 10,
 519        width: int = 8,
 520        height: int = 6,
 521        harmonized: bool = False,
 522    ):
 523        """
 524        Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize the results.
 525
 526        This method performs density-based clustering (DBSCAN) on the PCA-reduced
 527        dataset. Cluster labels are stored in the object's metadata, and a scatter
 528        plot of the first two principal components with cluster annotations is returned.
 529
 530        Parameters
 531        ----------
 532        pc_num : int, default 2
 533            Number of principal components to use for clustering.
 534            If 0, uses all available components.
 535
 536        eps : float, default 0.5
 537            Maximum distance between two points for them to be considered
 538            as neighbors (DBSCAN parameter).
 539
 540        min_samples : int, default 10
 541            Minimum number of samples required to form a cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 542
 543        width : int, default 8
 544            Width of the output scatter plot.
 545
 546        height : int, default 6
 547            Height of the output scatter plot.
 548
 549        harmonized : bool, default False
 550            If True, use harmonized PCA data (`self.harmonized_pca`).
 551            If False, use standard PCA results (`self.pca`).
 552
 553        Returns
 554        -------
 555        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 556            Scatter plot of the first two principal components colored by
 557            cluster assignments.
 558
 559        Updates
 560        -------
 561        self.clustering_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list
 562            Cluster labels assigned to each cell/sample.
 563
 564        self.input_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list, optional
 565            Cluster labels stored in input metadata (if available).
 566        """
 567
 568        dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 569
 570        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
 571            PCA = self.harmonized_pca
 572
 573        elif pc_num == 0:
 574            PCA = self.pca
 575
 576        else:
 577            if harmonized:
 578
 579                PCA = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 580            else:
 581
 582                PCA = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 583
 584        dbscan_labels = dbscan.fit_predict(PCA)
 585
 586        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(PCA)
 587        pca_df["Cluster"] = dbscan_labels
 588
 589        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 590
 591        clusters = sorted(pca_df["Cluster"].unique())
 592        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(clusters))
 593
 594        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
 595            cluster_data = pca_df[pca_df["Cluster"] == cluster_id]
 596            plt.scatter(
 597                cluster_data["PC1"],
 598                cluster_data["PC2"],
 599                label=f"Cluster {cluster_id}",
 600                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
 601                alpha=0.7,
 602            )
 603
 604        plt.xlabel("PC 1")
 605        plt.ylabel("PC 2")
 606        plt.legend(title="Clusters", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
 607
 608        plt.grid(True)
 609        plt.show()
 610
 611        self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 612
 613        try:
 614            self.input_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 615        except:
 616            pass
 617
 618        return fig

 620    def perform_UMAP(
 621        self,
 622        factorize: bool = False,
 623        umap_num: int = 100,
 624        pc_num: int = 0,
 625        harmonized: bool = False,
 626        n_neighbors: int = 5,
 627        min_dist: float | int = 0.1,
 628        spread: float | int = 1.0,
 629        set_op_mix_ratio: float | int = 1.0,
 630        local_connectivity: int = 1,
 631        repulsion_strength: float | int = 1.0,
 632        negative_sample_rate: int = 5,
 633        width: int = 8,
 634        height: int = 6,
 635    ):
 636        """
 637        Compute and visualize UMAP embeddings of the dataset.
 638
 639        This method applies Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)
 640        for dimensionality reduction on either raw, PCA, or harmonized PCA data.
 641        Results are stored as a DataFrame (`self.umap`) and a scatter plot figure
 642        (`self.UMAP_plot`).
 643
 644        Parameters
 645        ----------
 646        factorize : bool, default False
 647            If True, categorical sample labels (from column names) are factorized
 648            and used as supervision in UMAP fitting.
 649
 650        umap_num : int, default 100
 651            Number of UMAP dimensions to compute. If 0, matches the input dimension.
 652
 653        pc_num : int, default 0
 654            Number of principal components to use as UMAP input.
 655            If 0, use all available components or raw data.
 656
 657        harmonized : bool, default False
 658            If True, use harmonized PCA embeddings (`self.harmonized_pca`).
 659            If False, use standard PCA or raw scaled data.
 660
 661        n_neighbors : int, default 5
 662            UMAP parameter controlling the size of the local neighborhood.
 663
 664        min_dist : float, default 0.1
 665            UMAP parameter controlling minimum allowed distance between embedded points.
 666
 667        spread : int | float, default 1.0
 668            Effective scale of embedded space (UMAP parameter).
 669
 670        set_op_mix_ratio : int | float, default 1.0
 671            Interpolation parameter between union and intersection in fuzzy sets.
 672
 673        local_connectivity : int, default 1
 674            Number of nearest neighbors assumed for each point.
 675
 676        repulsion_strength : int | float, default 1.0
 677            Weighting applied to negative samples during optimization.
 678
 679        negative_sample_rate : int, default 5
 680            Number of negative samples per positive sample in optimization.
 681
 682        width : int, default 8
 683            Width of the output scatter plot.
 684
 685        height : int, default 6
 686            Height of the output scatter plot.
 687
 688        Updates
 689        -------
 690        self.umap : pandas.DataFrame
 691            Table of UMAP embeddings with columns `UMAP1 ... UMAPn`.
 692
 693        Notes
 694        -----
 695        For supervised UMAP (`factorize=True`), categorical codes from column
 696        names of the dataset are used as labels.
 697        """
 698
 699        scaler = StandardScaler()
 700
 701        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
 702            data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca
 703
 704        elif pc_num == 0:
 705            data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
 706
 707        else:
 708            if harmonized:
 709
 710                data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 711            else:
 712
 713                data_scaled = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
 714
 715        if umap_num == 0 or umap_num > data_scaled.shape[1]:
 716
 717            umap_num = data_scaled.shape[1]
 718
 719            reducer = umap.UMAP(
 720                n_components=len(data_scaled.T),
 721                random_state=42,
 722                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
 723                min_dist=min_dist,
 724                spread=spread,
 725                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
 726                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
 727                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
 728                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
 729                n_jobs=1,
 730            )
 731
 732        else:
 733
 734            reducer = umap.UMAP(
 735                n_components=umap_num,
 736                random_state=42,
 737                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
 738                min_dist=min_dist,
 739                spread=spread,
 740                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
 741                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
 742                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
 743                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
 744                n_jobs=1,
 745            )
 746
 747        if factorize:
 748            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(
 749                X=data_scaled, y=pd.Categorical(self.clustering_data.columns).codes
 750            )
 751        else:
 752            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X=data_scaled)
 753
 754        umap_df = pd.DataFrame(
 755            embedding, columns=["UMAP" + str(x + 1) for x in range(umap_num)]
 756        )
 757
 758        plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 759        plt.scatter(umap_df["UMAP1"], umap_df["UMAP2"], alpha=0.7)
 760        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
 761        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
 762        plt.grid(True)
 763
 764        plt.show()
 765
 766        self.umap = umap_df
 767
 768    def knee_plot_umap(self, eps: int | float = 0.5, min_samples: int = 10):
 769        """
 770        Plot silhouette scores for different UMAP dimensions to determine optimal n_components.
 771
 772        Parameters
 773        ----------
 774        eps : float, default 0.5
 775            DBSCAN eps parameter for clustering each UMAP dimension.
 776
 777        min_samples : int, default 10
 778            Minimum number of samples to form a cluster in DBSCAN.
 779
 780        Returns
 781        -------
 782        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 783            Silhouette score plot across UMAP dimensions.
 784        """
 785
 786        umap_range = range(2, len(self.umap.T) + 1)
 787
 788        silhouette_scores = []
 789        component = []
 790        for n in umap_range:
 791
 792            db = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 793            labels = db.fit_predict(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n])
 794
 795            mask = labels != -1
 796            if len(set(labels[mask])) > 1:
 797                score = silhouette_score(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n][mask], labels[mask])
 798            else:
 799                score = -1
 800
 801            silhouette_scores.append(score)
 802            component.append(n)
 803
 804        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
 805        plt.plot(component, silhouette_scores, marker="o")
 806        plt.xlabel("UMAP (n_components)")
 807        plt.ylabel("Silhouette Score")
 808        plt.grid(True)
 809        plt.xticks(range(int(min(component)), int(max(component)) + 1, 1))
 810
 811        plt.show()
 812
 813        return fig
 814
 815    def find_clusters_UMAP(
 816        self,
 817        umap_n: int = 5,
 818        eps: float | float = 0.5,
 819        min_samples: int = 10,
 820        width: int = 8,
 821        height: int = 6,
 822    ):
 823        """
 824        Apply DBSCAN clustering on UMAP embeddings and visualize clusters.
 825
 826        This method performs density-based clustering (DBSCAN) on the UMAP-reduced
 827        dataset. Cluster labels are stored in the object's metadata, and a scatter
 828        plot of the first two UMAP components with cluster annotations is returned.
 829
 830        Parameters
 831        ----------
 832        umap_n : int, default 5
 833            Number of UMAP dimensions to use for DBSCAN clustering.
 834            Must be <= number of columns in `self.umap`.
 835
 836        eps : float | int, default 0.5
 837            Maximum neighborhood distance between two samples for them to be considered
 838            as in the same cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 839
 840        min_samples : int, default 10
 841            Minimum number of samples in a neighborhood to form a cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
 842
 843        width : int, default 8
 844            Figure width.
 845
 846        height : int, default 6
 847            Figure height.
 848
 849        Returns
 850        -------
 851        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 852            Scatter plot of the first two UMAP components colored by
 853            cluster assignments.
 854
 855        Updates
 856        -------
 857        self.clustering_metadata['UMAP_clusters'] : list
 858            Cluster labels assigned to each cell/sample.
 859
 860        self.input_metadata['UMAP_clusters'] : list, optional
 861            Cluster labels stored in input metadata (if available).
 862        """
 863
 864        dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
 865        dbscan_labels = dbscan.fit_predict(np.array(self.umap)[:, :umap_n])
 866
 867        umap_df = self.umap
 868        umap_df["Cluster"] = dbscan_labels
 869
 870        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
 871
 872        colors_1 = plt.cm.tab20b(np.linspace(0, 1, 20))
 873        colors_2 = plt.cm.tab20c(np.linspace(0, 1, 20))
 874        color_palette = np.vstack((colors_1, colors_2))
 875
 876        clusters = sorted(umap_df["Cluster"].unique())
 877
 878        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):
 879            cluster_data = umap_df[umap_df["Cluster"] == cluster_id]
 880
 881            plt.scatter(
 882                cluster_data["UMAP1"],
 883                cluster_data["UMAP2"],
 884                label=f"Cluster {cluster_id}",
 885                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
 886                alpha=0.7,
 887            )
 888
 889        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
 890        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
 891        plt.legend(title="Clusters", loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5))
 892        plt.grid(True)
 893
 894        self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 895
 896        try:
 897            self.input_metadata["UMAP_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
 898        except:
 899            pass
 900
 901        return fig
