 903    def UMAP_vis(
 904        self,
 905        names_slot: str = "cell_names",
 906        set_sep: bool = True,
 907        point_size: int | float = 0.6,
 908        font_size: int | float = 6,
 909        legend_split_col: int = 2,
 910        width: int = 8,
 911        height: int = 6,
 912        inc_num: bool = True,
 913        inc_bbox: bool = True,
 914        size_sort: bool = True,
 915        grid: bool = False,
 916        rasterized: bool = True,
 917    ):
 918        """
 919        Visualize UMAP embeddings with sample labels based on specyfic metadata slot.
 920
 921        Parameters
 922        ----------
 923        names_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
 924            Column in metadata to use as sample labels.
 925
 926        set_sep : bool, default True
 927            If True, separate points by dataset.
 928
 929        point_size : float, default 0.6
 930            Size of scatter points.
 931
 932        font_size : int, default 6
 933            Font size for numbers on points.
 934
 935        legend_split_col : int, default 2
 936            Number of columns in legend.
 937
 938        width : int, default 8
 939            Figure width.
 940
 941        height : int, default 6
 942            Figure height.
 943
 944        inc_num : bool, default True
 945            If True, annotate points with numeric labels.
 946
 947        inc_bbox : bool, default True
 948            If True, annotate points with a background box (bbox).
 949
 950        size_sort : bool, default=True
 951            If True, cluster names are sorted in descending order by cluster size.
 952             If False, cluster names follow the order of their first appearance in `names_slot`.
 953
 954        grid : bool, default False
 955            If True, the plot grid will be visible.
 956
 957        rasterized : bool, default True
 958            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
 959            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
 960            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
 961
 962
 963        Returns
 964        -------
 965        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 966            UMAP scatter plot figure.
 967        """
 968
 969        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
 970        umap_df["names"] = list(self.clustering_metadata[names_slot])
 971
 972        if set_sep:
 973
 974            if "sets" in list(self.clustering_metadata.columns):
 975                umap_df["dataset"] = list(self.clustering_metadata["sets"])
 976            else:
 977                umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 978
 979        else:
 980            umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 981
 982        umap_df["tmp_nam"] = list(umap_df["names"] + umap_df["dataset"])
 983
 984        umap_df["count"] = umap_df["tmp_nam"].map(umap_df["tmp_nam"].value_counts())
 985
 986        queue = pd.unique(umap_df["names"])
 987
 988        umap_df["names"] = pd.Categorical(
 989            umap_df["names"], categories=queue, ordered=True
 990        )
 991
 992        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("names").reset_index(drop=True)
 993
 994        umap_df["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(umap_df["names"])[0]
 995
 996        numeric_df = (
 997            pd.DataFrame(umap_df[["count", "tmp_nam", "names", "id_vec"]].copy())
 998            .drop_duplicates()
 999            .sort_values("count", ascending=False)
1000        )
1001
1002        numeric_df["numeric_values"] = range(0, numeric_df.shape[0])
1003
1004        if size_sort:
1005            numeric_df["id_vec"] = numeric_df["numeric_values"]
1006
1007        umap_df = umap_df.merge(
1008            numeric_df[["tmp_nam", "numeric_values"]], on="tmp_nam", how="left"
1009        )
1010
1011        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1012
1013        markers = ["o", "s", "^", "D", "P", "*", "X"]
1014        marker_map = {
1015            ds: markers[i % len(markers)]
1016            for i, ds in enumerate(umap_df["dataset"].unique())
1017        }
1018
1019        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(numeric_df["tmp_nam"]))
1020
1021        cord_list = []
1022
1023        numeric_df = numeric_df.reset_index(drop=True)
1024
1025        id_counts = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec")["id_vec"].transform("count")
1026        id_cum = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec").cumcount() + 1
1027
1028        numeric_df["id_vec"] = np.where(
1029            id_counts > 1,
1030            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str) + "." + id_cum.astype(str),
1031            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str),
1032        )
1033
1034        for idx, (num, nam) in enumerate(
1035            zip(numeric_df["numeric_values"], numeric_df["names"])
1036        ):
1037
1038            cluster_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] == num]
1039
1040            rest_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] != num]
1041
1042            current_size = max(point_size, 0.25)
1043
1044            ax.scatter(
1045                cluster_data["UMAP1"],
1046                cluster_data["UMAP2"],
1047                label=f"{numeric_df['id_vec'][idx]} - {nam}",
1048                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
1049                marker=marker_map[cluster_data["dataset"].iloc[0]],
1050                alpha=0.6,
1051                s=current_size,
1052                rasterized=rasterized,
1053            )
1054
1055            coords = np.round(cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1056            rest_coords = np.round(rest_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1057
1058            coords_tuples = set(map(tuple, rest_coords))
1059            should_keep = [tuple(pt) not in coords_tuples for pt in coords]
1060
1061            coords = coords[should_keep]
1062
1063            if len(coords) == 0:
1064                coords = cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values
1065
1066            if len(coords) > 0:
1067                mean_x = np.mean(coords[:, 0])
1068                mean_y = np.mean(coords[:, 1])
1069
1070                q1 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1071                q2 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1072                q3 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1073                q4 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1074
1075                quadrants = [q for q in [q1, q2, q3, q4] if len(q) > 0]
1076
1077                if quadrants:
1078                    quadrants.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
1079
1080                    top1 = quadrants[0]
1081                    center1 = np.mean(top1, axis=0)
1082
1083                    if len(quadrants) > 1:
1084                        top2 = quadrants[1]
1085                        center2 = np.mean(top2, axis=0)
1086
1087                        dist_between_tops = np.linalg.norm(center1 - center2)
1088
1089                        cluster_spread = np.mean(
1090                            np.linalg.norm(coords - [mean_x, mean_y], axis=1)
1091                        )
1092                        threshold = cluster_spread * 0.6
1093
1094                        if dist_between_tops < threshold:
1095                            combined_tops = np.vstack([top1, top2])
1096                            center_point = np.mean(combined_tops, axis=0)
1097                        else:
1098                            center_point = center1
1099                    else:
1100                        center_point = center1
1101                else:
1102                    center_point = np.array([mean_x, mean_y])
1103
1104                cluster_median = np.median(coords, axis=0)
1105                alpha = 0.5
1106                center_point = (1 - alpha) * center_point + alpha * cluster_median
1107
1108            else:
1109                center_point = np.array([0, 0])
1110
1111            cord_list.append(center_point)
1112
1113        if inc_num:
1114
1115            bbox_props = (
1116                dict(
1117                    boxstyle="round,pad=0.1",
1118                    facecolor="white",
1119                    edgecolor="none",
1120                    alpha=0.7,
1121                )
1122                if inc_bbox
1123                else None
1124            )
1125
1126            texts = []
1127            repeat_lab = []
1128            for (x, y), num in zip(cord_list, numeric_df["id_vec"]):
1129                if num not in repeat_lab:
1130                    texts.append(
1131                        ax.text(
1132                            x,
1133                            y,
1134                            str(num),
1135                            ha="center",
1136                            va="center",
1137                            fontsize=font_size,
1138                            color="black",
1139                            bbox=bbox_props,
1140                        )
1141                    )
1142                    repeat_lab.append(num)
1143
1144            adjust_text(
1145                texts,
1146                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", lw=0.5),
1147                force_text=(1.2, 1.2),
1148                force_points=(1.0, 1.0),
1149                expand_text=(1.3, 1.3),
1150                expand_points=(1.3, 1.3),
1151                lim=500,
1152            )
1153
1154        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1155        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1156
1157        ax.grid(grid)
1158
1159        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1160
1161        def sort_key(item):
1162            num_str = item[1].split(" - ")[0]
1163            parts = num_str.split(".")
1164            main_num = int(parts[0])
1165            sub_num = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
1166            return (main_num, sub_num)
1167
1168        sorted_pairs = sorted(zip(handles, labels), key=sort_key)
1169        sorted_handles, sorted_labels = zip(*sorted_pairs)
1170
1171        if not inc_num:
1172            sorted_labels = [lbl.split(" - ", 1)[1] for lbl in sorted_labels]
1173
1174        unique_datasets = umap_df["dataset"].unique()
1175        dataset_handles = list(sorted_handles)
1176        dataset_labels = list(sorted_labels)
1177
1178        if len(unique_datasets) > 1:
1179            for ds in unique_datasets:
1180                proxy_marker = Line2D(
1181                    [0],
1182                    [0],
1183                    marker=marker_map[ds],
1184                    color="w",
1185                    markerfacecolor="gray",
1186                    markeredgecolor="black",
1187                    markersize=current_size * 2,
1188                    linestyle="None",
1189                    label=f"Set: {ds}",
1190                )
1191
1192                dataset_handles.append(proxy_marker)
1193                dataset_labels.append(f"Data: {ds}")
1194
1195        ax.legend(
1196            dataset_handles,
1197            dataset_labels,
1198            title="",
1199            loc="center left",
1200            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.5),
1201            ncol=legend_split_col,
1202            markerscale=15,
1203        )
1204
1205        ax.grid(grid, which="both")
1206
1207        plt.tight_layout()
1208
1209        return fig

1211    def UMAP_feature(
1212        self,
1213        feature_name: str,
1214        features_data: pd.DataFrame | None,
1215        point_size: int | float = 0.6,
1216        font_size: int | float = 6,
1217        width: int = 8,
1218        height: int = 6,
1219        palette="light",
1220        grid: bool = False,
1221        rasterized: bool = True,
1222    ):
1223        """
1224        Visualize UMAP embedding with expression levels of a selected feature.
1225
1226        Each point (cell) in the UMAP plot is colored according to the expression
1227        value of the chosen feature, enabling interpretation of spatial patterns
1228        of gene activity or metadata distribution in low-dimensional space.
1229
1230        Parameters
1231        ----------
1232        feature_name : str
1233           Name of the feature to plot.
1234
1235        features_data : pandas.DataFrame or None, default None
1236            If None, the function uses the DataFrame containing the clustering data.
1237            To plot features not used in clustering, provide a wider DataFrame
1238            containing the original feature values.
1239
1240        point_size : float, default 0.6
1241            Size of scatter points in the plot.
1242
1243        font_size : int, default 6
1244            Font size for axis labels and annotations.
1245
1246        width : int, default 8
1247            Width of the matplotlib figure.
1248
1249        height : int, default 6
1250            Height of the matplotlib figure.
1251
1252        grid : bool, default False
1253            If True, the plot grid will be visible.
1254
1255        palette : str, default 'light'
1256            Color palette for expression visualization. Options are:
1257            - 'light'
1258            - 'dark'
1259            - 'green'
1260            - 'gray'
1261
1262        rasterized : bool, default True
1263            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
1264            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
1265            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
1266
1267        Returns
1268        -------
1269        matplotlib.figure.Figure
1270            UMAP scatter plot colored by feature values.
1271        """
1272
1273        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
1274
1275        if features_data is None:
1276            features_data = self.clustering_data
1277
1278        if features_data.shape[1] != umap_df.shape[0]:
1279            raise ValueError(
1280                "Imputed 'features_data' shape does not match the number of UMAP"
1281                " cells"
1282            )
1283
1284        blist = [
1285            True if x.upper() == feature_name.upper() else False
1286            for x in features_data.index
1287        ]
1288
1289        if not any(blist):
1290            raise ValueError("Imputed feature_name is not included in the data")
1291
1292        umap_df.loc[:, "feature"] = (
1293            features_data.loc[blist, :]
1294            .apply(lambda row: row.tolist(), axis=1)
1295            .values[0]
1296        )
1297
1298        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("feature", ascending=True)
1299
1300        vals = umap_df["feature"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1301        vmin, vmax = vals.min(), vals.max()
1302
1303        if vmax > vmin:
1304            norm_vals = (vals - vmin) / (vmax - vmin)
1305        else:
1306            norm_vals = np.ones_like(vals)
1307
1308        min_scale = 0.1
1309        sizes = point_size * (min_scale + (1.0 - min_scale) * norm_vals)
1310
1311        def px_to_rgb01(px_seq):
1312            out = []
1313            for c in px_seq:
1314                rgb_255 = px.colors.unlabel_rgb(c)
1315                out.append(tuple(v / 255.0 for v in rgb_255))
1316            return out
1317
1318        def sample_colors(px_seq, n_colors):
1319            rgb_seq = px_to_rgb01(px_seq)
1320            if n_colors <= 1:
1321                return rgb_seq[:n_colors]
1322            idxs = np.linspace(0, len(rgb_seq) - 1, n_colors).round().astype(int)
1323            return [rgb_seq[i] for i in idxs]
1324
1325        n_groups = len(px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark)
1326
1327        norm = None
1328
1329        if palette in ("gray-red", "gray-blue"):
1330            base_px = (
1331                px.colors.sequential.Reds
1332                if palette == "gray-red"
1333                else px.colors.sequential.Blues
1334            )
1335            grad_colors = sample_colors(base_px[3:], max(n_groups - 1, 1))
1336            gray_rgb = (0.72, 0.72, 0.72)
1337
1338            if vmax > vmin:
1339                if vmin <= 0.0 < vmax and np.any(vals > 0.0):
1340                    eps = min(np.min(vals[vals > 0.0]) * 0.5, (vmax - 0.0) * 1e-3)
1341                    pos_bounds = np.linspace(eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1342                    bounds = np.concatenate(([min(vmin, 0.0)], pos_bounds))
1343                else:
1344                    eps = (vmax - vmin) * 1e-3
1345                    rest_bounds = np.linspace(vmin + eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1346                    bounds = np.concatenate(([vmin], rest_bounds))
1347
1348                colors_list = [gray_rgb] + grad_colors
1349                norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, ncolors=len(colors_list))
1350                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(colors_list, name=palette)
1351            else:
1352                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap([gray_rgb], name=palette)
1353
1354        else:
1355            if palette == "light":
1356                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark
1357            elif palette == "dark":
1358                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.thermal
1359            elif palette == "green":
1360                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Aggrnyl
1361            elif palette == "gray":
1362                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.gray[::-1]
1363            else:
1364                raise ValueError(
1365                    'Palette not found. Use: "light", "dark", "gray", "green",'
1366                    ' "gray-red", or "gray-blue"'
1367                )
1368
1369            converted = sample_colors(px_palette, n_groups)
1370            my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(converted, name="custom")
1371
1372        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1373        sc = ax.scatter(
1374            umap_df["UMAP1"],
1375            umap_df["UMAP2"],
1376            c=umap_df["feature"],
1377            s=sizes * 5,
1378            cmap=my_cmap,
1379            norm=norm,
1380            alpha=1,
1381            edgecolors="white",
1382            linewidths=0,
1383            rasterized=rasterized,
1384        )
1385
1386        cbar = plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1387        cbar.set_label(f"{feature_name}")
1388        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=5))
1389        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter("%.1f"))
1390
1391        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1392        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1393
1394        ax.grid(grid)
1395
1396        plt.tight_layout()
1397
1398        return fig

1400    def get_umap_data(self):
1401        """
1402        Retrieve UMAP embedding data with optional cluster labels.
1403
1404        Returns the UMAP coordinates stored in `self.umap`. If clustering
1405        metadata is available (specifically `UMAP_clusters`), the corresponding
1406        cluster assignments are appended as an additional column.
1407
1408        Returns
1409        -------
1410        pandas.DataFrame
1411            DataFrame containing UMAP coordinates (columns: 'UMAP1', 'UMAP2', ...).
1412            If available, includes an extra column 'clusters' with cluster labels.
1413
1414        Notes
1415        -----
1416        - UMAP embeddings must be computed beforehand (e.g., using `perform_UMAP`).
1417        - Cluster labels are added only if present in `self.clustering_metadata`.
1418        """
1419
1420        umap_data = self.umap
1421
1422        try:
1423            umap_data["clusters"] = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]
1424        except:
1425            pass
1426
1427        return umap_data
1428
1429    def get_pca_data(self):
1430        """
1431        Retrieve PCA embedding data with optional cluster labels.
1432
1433        Returns the principal component scores stored in `self.pca`. If clustering
1434        metadata is available (specifically `PCA_clusters`), the corresponding
1435        cluster assignments are appended as an additional column.
1436
1437        Returns
1438        -------
1439        pandas.DataFrame
1440            DataFrame containing PCA coordinates (columns: 'PC1', 'PC2', ...).
1441            If available, includes an extra column 'clusters' with cluster labels.
1442
1443        Notes
1444        -----
1445        - PCA must be computed beforehand (e.g., using `perform_PCA`).
1446        - Cluster labels are added only if present in `self.clustering_metadata`.
1447        """
1448
1449        pca_data = self.pca
1450
1451        try:
1452            pca_data["clusters"] = self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"]
1453        except:
1454            pass
1455
1456        return pca_data
1457
1458    def return_clusters(self, clusters="umap"):
1459        """
1460        Retrieve cluster labels from UMAP or PCA clustering results.
1461
1462        Parameters
1463        ----------
1464        clusters : str, default 'umap'
1465            Source of cluster labels to return. Must be one of:
1466            - 'umap': return cluster labels from UMAP embeddings.
1467            - 'pca' : return cluster labels from PCA embeddings.
1468
1469        Returns
1470        -------
1471        list
1472            Cluster labels corresponding to the selected embedding method.
1473
1474        Raises
1475        ------
1476        ValueError
1477            If `clusters` is not 'umap' or 'pca'.
1478
1479        Notes
1480        -----
1481        Requires that clustering has already been performed
1482        (e.g., using `find_clusters_UMAP` or `find_clusters_PCA`).
1483        """
1484
1485        if clusters.lower() == "umap":
1486            clusters_vector = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]
1487        elif clusters.lower() == "pca":
1488            clusters_vector = self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"]
1489        else:
1490            raise ValueError("Parameter 'clusters' must be either 'umap' or 'pca'.")
1491
1492        return clusters_vector

A class for performing dimensionality reduction, clustering, and visualization on high-dimensional data (e.g., single-cell gene expression).

The class provides methods for:

  • Normalizing and extracting subsets of data
  • Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and related clustering
  • Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) and clustering
  • Visualization of PCA and UMAP embeddings
  • Harmonization of batch effects
  • Accessing processed data and cluster labels

Methods

add_data_frame(data, metadata) Class method to create a Clustering instance from a DataFrame and metadata.

harmonize_sets() Perform batch effect harmonization on PCA data.

perform_PCA(pc_num=100, width=8, height=6) Perform PCA on the dataset and visualize the first two PCs.

knee_plot_PCA(width=8, height=6) Plot the cumulative variance explained by PCs to determine optimal dimensionality.

find_clusters_PCA(pc_num=0, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6, harmonized=False) Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize results.

perform_UMAP(factorize=False, umap_num=100, pc_num=0, harmonized=False, ...) Compute UMAP embeddings with optional parameter tuning.

knee_plot_umap(eps=0.5, min_samples=10) Determine optimal UMAP dimensionality using silhouette scores.

find_clusters_UMAP(umap_n=5, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, width=8, height=6) Apply DBSCAN clustering on UMAP embeddings and visualize clusters.

UMAP_vis(names_slot='cell_names', set_sep=True, point_size=0.6, ...) Visualize UMAP embeddings with labels and optional cluster numbering.

UMAP_feature(feature_name, features_data=None, point_size=0.6, ...) Plot a single feature over UMAP coordinates with customizable colormap.

get_umap_data() Return the UMAP embeddings along with cluster labels if available.

get_pca_data() Return the PCA results along with cluster labels if available.

return_clusters(clusters='umap') Return the cluster labels for UMAP or PCA embeddings.

Raises

ValueError For invalid parameters, mismatched dimensions, or missing metadata.

def sort_data( self, value_to_sort: str, ascending: bool = True, sort_order: list | None = None): 
171    def sort_data(
172        self,
173        value_to_sort: str,
174        ascending: bool = True,
175        sort_order: list | None = None,
176    ):
177        """
178        Sort metadata and synchronize all associated data matrices and embeddings.
179
180        This method reorders sample metadata based on a specified column and
181        propagates the new sample order across all initialized data slots
182        (e.g., expression matrices, PCA, harmonized PCA, and UMAP embeddings).
183
184        Parameters
185        ----------
186        value_to_sort : str
187            Name of the metadata column used as the sorting key.
188
189        ascending : bool, default=True
190            Sort ascending vs. descending. Ignored if `sort_order` is provided
191            unless reversed sorting of the custom order is intended.
192
193        sort_order : list or None, default=None
194            Explicit list defining the exact custom order of unique categories
195            in `value_to_sort`. Must contain the exact same unique values as
196            the target column.
197
198        Raises
199        ------
200        ValueError
201            If `value_to_sort` does not exist in the metadata columns, or if
202            `sort_order` does not match the unique values present in the column.
203        """
204
205        # methode part for COMPsc project
206        if "input_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
207            if value_to_sort not in self.input_metadata.columns:
208                available_cols = list(self.input_metadata.columns)
209                raise ValueError(
210                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in input_metadata. "
211                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
212                )
213
214            # step 1
215            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.input_metadata))
216            self.input_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
217
218            if self.normalized_data is not None:
219                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
220
221            if self.input_data is not None:
222                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"]
223
224            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
225                unique_vals = set(self.input_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
226                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
227                    unique_vals
228                ):
229                    self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
230                        self.input_metadata[value_to_sort],
231                        categories=sort_order,
232                        ordered=True,
233                    )
234                    self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
235                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
236                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
237                else:
238                    raise ValueError(
239                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
240                    )
241            else:
242                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.sort_values(
243                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
244                ).reset_index(drop=True)
245
246            new_order = self.input_metadata["sorting_id"].values
247
248            if self.normalized_data is not None:
249                self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.iloc[:, new_order]
250                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
251
252            if self.input_data is not None:
253                self.input_data = self.input_data.iloc[:, new_order]
254                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
255
256            self.input_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
257            self.input_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.input_metadata[
258                value_to_sort
259            ].astype(str)
260
261            # step 2
262            if self.agg_metadata is not None:
263                sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.agg_metadata))
264                self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
265
266                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
267                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"]
268
269                if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
270                    unique_vals = set(self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
271                    if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
272                        unique_vals
273                    ):
274                        self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
275                            self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort],
276                            categories=sort_order,
277                            ordered=True,
278                        )
279                        self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
280                            value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
281                        ).reset_index(drop=True)
282                    else:
283                        raise ValueError(
284                            "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
285                        )
286                else:
287                    self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.sort_values(
288                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
289                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
290
291                new_order = self.agg_metadata["sorting_id"].values
292
293                if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
294                    self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.iloc[
295                        :, new_order
296                    ]
297                    self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata["cell_names"]
298
299                self.agg_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
300                self.agg_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.agg_metadata[
301                    value_to_sort
302                ].astype(str)
303
304        # method for Clustering
305
306        if "clustering_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
307            if value_to_sort not in self.clustering_metadata.columns:
308                available_cols = list(self.clustering_metadata.columns)
309                raise ValueError(
310                    f"Column '{value_to_sort}' not found in clustering_metadata. "
311                    f"Available columns: {available_cols}"
312                )
313
314            # step 1
315            sorting_id = np.arange(len(self.clustering_metadata))
316            self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"] = sorting_id
317
318            if (
319                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
320                and self.clustering_data is not None
321            ):
322                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
323
324            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
325                tmp_pca = self.pca
326                tmp_pca.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
327
328            if (
329                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
330                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
331            ):
332                tmp_pca_harmonize = self.harmonized_pca
333                tmp_pca_harmonize.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
334
335            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
336                tmp_umap = self.umap
337                tmp_umap.index = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"]
338
339            if sort_order is not None and len(sort_order) > 0:
340                unique_vals = set(self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort].dropna())
341                if set(sort_order) == unique_vals and len(sort_order) == len(
342                    unique_vals
343                ):
344                    self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = pd.Categorical(
345                        self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort],
346                        categories=sort_order,
347                        ordered=True,
348                    )
349                    self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
350                        value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
351                    ).reset_index(drop=True)
352                else:
353                    raise ValueError(
354                        "Sort order list does not match the unique values in the data."
355                    )
356            else:
357                self.clustering_metadata = self.clustering_metadata.sort_values(
358                    value_to_sort, ascending=ascending
359                ).reset_index(drop=True)
360
361            new_order = self.clustering_metadata["sorting_id"].values
362
363            if (
364                "clustering_data" in self.__dict__.keys()
365                and self.clustering_data is not None
366            ):
367                self.clustering_data = self.clustering_data.iloc[:, new_order]
368                self.clustering_data.columns = self.clustering_metadata["cell_names"]
369
370            if "pca" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.pca is not None:
371                tmp_pca = tmp_pca.loc[new_order, :]
372                self.pca = tmp_pca.reset_index(drop=True)
373                del tmp_pca
374
375            if (
376                "harmonized_pca" in self.__dict__.keys()
377                and self.harmonized_pca is not None
378            ):
379                tmp_pca_harmonize = tmp_pca_harmonize.loc[new_order, :]
380                self.harmonized_pca = tmp_pca_harmonize.reset_index(drop=True)
381                del tmp_pca_harmonize
382
383            if "umap" in self.__dict__.keys() and self.umap is not None:
384                tmp_umap = tmp_umap.loc[new_order, :]
385                self.umap = tmp_umap.reset_index(drop=True)
386                del tmp_umap
387
388            self.clustering_metadata.drop(columns=["sorting_id"], inplace=True)
389            self.clustering_metadata[value_to_sort] = self.clustering_metadata[
390                value_to_sort
391            ].astype(str)

Sort metadata and synchronize all associated data matrices and embeddings.

This method reorders sample metadata based on a specified column and propagates the new sample order across all initialized data slots (e.g., expression matrices, PCA, harmonized PCA, and UMAP embeddings).

Parameters

value_to_sort : str Name of the metadata column used as the sorting key.

ascending : bool, default=True Sort ascending vs. descending. Ignored if sort_order is provided unless reversed sorting of the custom order is intended.

sort_order : list or None, default=None Explicit list defining the exact custom order of unique categories in value_to_sort. Must contain the exact same unique values as the target column.

Raises

ValueError If value_to_sort does not exist in the metadata columns, or if sort_order does not match the unique values present in the column.

def perform_PCA(self, pc_num: int = 100, width=8, height=6): 
418    def perform_PCA(self, pc_num: int = 100, width=8, height=6):
419        """
420        Perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the dataset.
421
422        This method standardizes the data, applies PCA, stores results as attributes,
423        and generates a scatter plot of the first two principal components.
424
425        Parameters
426        ----------
427        pc_num : int, default 100
428            Number of principal components to compute.
429            If 0, computes all available components.
430
431        width : int or float, default 8
432            Width of the PCA figure.
433
434        height : int or float, default 6
435            Height of the PCA figure.
436
437        Returns
438        -------
439        matplotlib.figure.Figure
440            Scatter plot showing the first two principal components.
441
442        Updates
443        -------
444        self.pca : pandas.DataFrame
445            DataFrame with principal component scores for each sample.
446
447        self.explained_var : numpy.ndarray
448            Percentage of variance explained by each principal component.
449
450        self.cumulative_var : numpy.ndarray
451            Cumulative explained variance.
452        """
453
454        scaler = StandardScaler()
455        data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
456
457        if pc_num == 0 or pc_num > data_scaled.shape[0]:
458            pc_num = data_scaled.shape[0]
459
460        pca = PCA(n_components=pc_num, random_state=42)
461
462        principal_components = pca.fit_transform(data_scaled)
463
464        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(
465            data=principal_components,
466            columns=["PC" + str(x + 1) for x in range(pc_num)],
467        )
468
469        self.explained_var = pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100
470        self.cumulative_var = np.cumsum(self.explained_var)
471
472        self.pca = pca_df
473
474        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
475        plt.scatter(pca_df["PC1"], pca_df["PC2"], alpha=0.7)
476        plt.xlabel("PC 1")
477        plt.ylabel("PC 2")
478        plt.grid(True)
479        plt.show()
480
481        return fig

def find_clusters_PCA( self, pc_num: int = 2, eps: float = 0.5, min_samples: int = 10, width: int = 8, height: int = 6, harmonized: bool = False): 
514    def find_clusters_PCA(

524        Apply DBSCAN clustering to PCA embeddings and visualize the results.
525
526        This method performs density-based clustering (DBSCAN) on the PCA-reduced
527        dataset. Cluster labels are stored in the object's metadata, and a scatter
528        plot of the first two principal components with cluster annotations is returned.
529
530        Parameters
531        ----------
532        pc_num : int, default 2
533            Number of principal components to use for clustering.
534            If 0, uses all available components.
535
536        eps : float, default 0.5
537            Maximum distance between two points for them to be considered
538            as neighbors (DBSCAN parameter).
539
540        min_samples : int, default 10
541            Minimum number of samples required to form a cluster (DBSCAN parameter).
542
543        width : int, default 8
544            Width of the output scatter plot.
545
546        height : int, default 6
547            Height of the output scatter plot.
548
549        harmonized : bool, default False

551            If False, use standard PCA results (`self.pca`).

553        Returns

557            cluster assignments.

559        Updates

561        self.clustering_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list
562            Cluster labels assigned to each cell/sample.
563
564        self.input_metadata['PCA_clusters'] : list, optional
565            Cluster labels stored in input metadata (if available).

567
568        dbscan = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
569
570        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
571            PCA = self.harmonized_pca
572
573        elif pc_num == 0:
574            PCA = self.pca
575
576        else:
577            if harmonized:
578
579                PCA = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
580            else:
581
582                PCA = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
583
584        dbscan_labels = dbscan.fit_predict(PCA)
585
586        pca_df = pd.DataFrame(PCA)
587        pca_df["Cluster"] = dbscan_labels
588
589        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
590
591        clusters = sorted(pca_df["Cluster"].unique())
592        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(clusters))
593
594        for idx, cluster_id in enumerate(clusters):

602            )

608        plt.grid(True)

611        self.clustering_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
612
613        try:
614            self.input_metadata["PCA_clusters"] = [str(x) for x in dbscan_labels]
615        except:
616            pass

618        return fig

def perform_UMAP( self, factorize: bool = False, umap_num: int = 100, pc_num: int = 0, harmonized: bool = False, n_neighbors: int = 5, min_dist: float | int = 0.1, spread: float | int = 1.0, set_op_mix_ratio: float | int = 1.0, local_connectivity: int = 1, repulsion_strength: float | int = 1.0, negative_sample_rate: int = 5, width: int = 8, height: int = 6): 
620    def perform_UMAP(
621        self,
622        factorize: bool = False,
623        umap_num: int = 100,
624        pc_num: int = 0,
625        harmonized: bool = False,
626        n_neighbors: int = 5,
627        min_dist: float | int = 0.1,
628        spread: float | int = 1.0,
629        set_op_mix_ratio: float | int = 1.0,
630        local_connectivity: int = 1,
631        repulsion_strength: float | int = 1.0,
632        negative_sample_rate: int = 5,
633        width: int = 8,
634        height: int = 6,
635    ):
636        """
637        Compute and visualize UMAP embeddings of the dataset.
638
639        This method applies Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP)
640        for dimensionality reduction on either raw, PCA, or harmonized PCA data.
641        Results are stored as a DataFrame (`self.umap`) and a scatter plot figure
642        (`self.UMAP_plot`).
643
644        Parameters
645        ----------
646        factorize : bool, default False
647            If True, categorical sample labels (from column names) are factorized
648            and used as supervision in UMAP fitting.
649
650        umap_num : int, default 100
651            Number of UMAP dimensions to compute. If 0, matches the input dimension.
652
653        pc_num : int, default 0
654            Number of principal components to use as UMAP input.
655            If 0, use all available components or raw data.
656
657        harmonized : bool, default False
658            If True, use harmonized PCA embeddings (`self.harmonized_pca`).
659            If False, use standard PCA or raw scaled data.
660
661        n_neighbors : int, default 5
662            UMAP parameter controlling the size of the local neighborhood.
663
664        min_dist : float, default 0.1
665            UMAP parameter controlling minimum allowed distance between embedded points.
666
667        spread : int | float, default 1.0
668            Effective scale of embedded space (UMAP parameter).
669
670        set_op_mix_ratio : int | float, default 1.0
671            Interpolation parameter between union and intersection in fuzzy sets.
672
673        local_connectivity : int, default 1
674            Number of nearest neighbors assumed for each point.
675
676        repulsion_strength : int | float, default 1.0
677            Weighting applied to negative samples during optimization.
678
679        negative_sample_rate : int, default 5
680            Number of negative samples per positive sample in optimization.
681
682        width : int, default 8
683            Width of the output scatter plot.
684
685        height : int, default 6
686            Height of the output scatter plot.
687
688        Updates
689        -------
690        self.umap : pandas.DataFrame
691            Table of UMAP embeddings with columns `UMAP1 ... UMAPn`.
692
693        Notes
694        -----
695        For supervised UMAP (`factorize=True`), categorical codes from column
696        names of the dataset are used as labels.
697        """
698
699        scaler = StandardScaler()
700
701        if pc_num == 0 and harmonized:
702            data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca
703
704        elif pc_num == 0:
705            data_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(self.clustering_data.T)
706
707        else:
708            if harmonized:
709
710                data_scaled = self.harmonized_pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
711            else:
712
713                data_scaled = self.pca.iloc[:, 0:pc_num]
714
715        if umap_num == 0 or umap_num > data_scaled.shape[1]:
716
717            umap_num = data_scaled.shape[1]
718
719            reducer = umap.UMAP(
720                n_components=len(data_scaled.T),
721                random_state=42,
722                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
723                min_dist=min_dist,
724                spread=spread,
725                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
726                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
727                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
728                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
729                n_jobs=1,
730            )
731
732        else:
733
734            reducer = umap.UMAP(
735                n_components=umap_num,
736                random_state=42,
737                n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
738                min_dist=min_dist,
739                spread=spread,
740                set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
741                local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
742                repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
743                negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
744                n_jobs=1,
745            )
746
747        if factorize:
748            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(
749                X=data_scaled, y=pd.Categorical(self.clustering_data.columns).codes
750            )
751        else:
752            embedding = reducer.fit_transform(X=data_scaled)
753
754        umap_df = pd.DataFrame(
755            embedding, columns=["UMAP" + str(x + 1) for x in range(umap_num)]
756        )
757
758        plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
759        plt.scatter(umap_df["UMAP1"], umap_df["UMAP2"], alpha=0.7)
760        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
761        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
762        plt.grid(True)
763
764        plt.show()
765
766        self.umap = umap_df

def knee_plot_umap(self, eps: int | float = 0.5, min_samples: int = 10): 
768    def knee_plot_umap(self, eps: int | float = 0.5, min_samples: int = 10):
769        """
770        Plot silhouette scores for different UMAP dimensions to determine optimal n_components.
771
772        Parameters
773        ----------
774        eps : float, default 0.5
775            DBSCAN eps parameter for clustering each UMAP dimension.
776
777        min_samples : int, default 10
778            Minimum number of samples to form a cluster in DBSCAN.
779
780        Returns
781        -------
782        matplotlib.figure.Figure
783            Silhouette score plot across UMAP dimensions.
784        """
785
786        umap_range = range(2, len(self.umap.T) + 1)
787
788        silhouette_scores = []
789        component = []
790        for n in umap_range:
791
792            db = DBSCAN(eps=eps, min_samples=min_samples)
793            labels = db.fit_predict(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n])
794
795            mask = labels != -1
796            if len(set(labels[mask])) > 1:
797                score = silhouette_score(np.array(self.umap)[:, :n][mask], labels[mask])
798            else:
799                score = -1
800
801            silhouette_scores.append(score)
802            component.append(n)
803
804        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))
805        plt.plot(component, silhouette_scores, marker="o")
806        plt.xlabel("UMAP (n_components)")
807        plt.ylabel("Silhouette Score")
808        plt.grid(True)
809        plt.xticks(range(int(min(component)), int(max(component)) + 1, 1))
810
811        plt.show()
812
813        return fig

 958            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
 959            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
 960            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
 961
 962
 963        Returns
 964        -------
 965        matplotlib.figure.Figure
 966            UMAP scatter plot figure.
 967        """
 968
 969        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
 970        umap_df["names"] = list(self.clustering_metadata[names_slot])
 971
 972        if set_sep:
 973
 974            if "sets" in list(self.clustering_metadata.columns):
 975                umap_df["dataset"] = list(self.clustering_metadata["sets"])
 976            else:
 977                umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 978
 979        else:
 980            umap_df["dataset"] = "default"
 981
 982        umap_df["tmp_nam"] = list(umap_df["names"] + umap_df["dataset"])
 983
 984        umap_df["count"] = umap_df["tmp_nam"].map(umap_df["tmp_nam"].value_counts())
 985
 986        queue = pd.unique(umap_df["names"])
 987
 988        umap_df["names"] = pd.Categorical(
 989            umap_df["names"], categories=queue, ordered=True
 990        )
 991
 992        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("names").reset_index(drop=True)
 993
 994        umap_df["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(umap_df["names"])[0]
 995
 996        numeric_df = (
 997            pd.DataFrame(umap_df[["count", "tmp_nam", "names", "id_vec"]].copy())
 998            .drop_duplicates()
 999            .sort_values("count", ascending=False)
1000        )
1001
1002        numeric_df["numeric_values"] = range(0, numeric_df.shape[0])
1003
1004        if size_sort:
1005            numeric_df["id_vec"] = numeric_df["numeric_values"]
1006
1007        umap_df = umap_df.merge(
1008            numeric_df[["tmp_nam", "numeric_values"]], on="tmp_nam", how="left"
1009        )
1010
1011        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1012
1013        markers = ["o", "s", "^", "D", "P", "*", "X"]
1014        marker_map = {
1015            ds: markers[i % len(markers)]
1016            for i, ds in enumerate(umap_df["dataset"].unique())
1017        }
1018
1019        color_palette = get_mixed_palette(len(numeric_df["tmp_nam"]))
1020
1021        cord_list = []
1022
1023        numeric_df = numeric_df.reset_index(drop=True)
1024
1025        id_counts = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec")["id_vec"].transform("count")
1026        id_cum = numeric_df.groupby("id_vec").cumcount() + 1
1027
1028        numeric_df["id_vec"] = np.where(
1029            id_counts > 1,
1030            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str) + "." + id_cum.astype(str),
1031            numeric_df["id_vec"].astype(str),
1032        )
1033
1034        for idx, (num, nam) in enumerate(
1035            zip(numeric_df["numeric_values"], numeric_df["names"])
1036        ):
1037
1038            cluster_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] == num]
1039
1040            rest_data = umap_df[umap_df["numeric_values"] != num]
1041
1042            current_size = max(point_size, 0.25)
1043
1044            ax.scatter(
1045                cluster_data["UMAP1"],
1046                cluster_data["UMAP2"],
1047                label=f"{numeric_df['id_vec'][idx]} - {nam}",
1048                color=color_palette[idx % len(color_palette)],
1049                marker=marker_map[cluster_data["dataset"].iloc[0]],
1050                alpha=0.6,
1051                s=current_size,
1052                rasterized=rasterized,
1053            )
1054
1055            coords = np.round(cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1056            rest_coords = np.round(rest_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values, decimals=2)
1057
1058            coords_tuples = set(map(tuple, rest_coords))
1059            should_keep = [tuple(pt) not in coords_tuples for pt in coords]
1060
1061            coords = coords[should_keep]
1062
1063            if len(coords) == 0:
1064                coords = cluster_data[["UMAP1", "UMAP2"]].values
1065
1066            if len(coords) > 0:
1067                mean_x = np.mean(coords[:, 0])
1068                mean_y = np.mean(coords[:, 1])
1069
1070                q1 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1071                q2 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] >= mean_y)]
1072                q3 = coords[(coords[:, 0] < mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1073                q4 = coords[(coords[:, 0] >= mean_x) & (coords[:, 1] < mean_y)]
1074
1075                quadrants = [q for q in [q1, q2, q3, q4] if len(q) > 0]
1076
1077                if quadrants:
1078                    quadrants.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
1079
1080                    top1 = quadrants[0]
1081                    center1 = np.mean(top1, axis=0)
1082
1083                    if len(quadrants) > 1:
1084                        top2 = quadrants[1]
1085                        center2 = np.mean(top2, axis=0)
1086
1087                        dist_between_tops = np.linalg.norm(center1 - center2)
1088
1089                        cluster_spread = np.mean(
1090                            np.linalg.norm(coords - [mean_x, mean_y], axis=1)
1091                        )
1092                        threshold = cluster_spread * 0.6
1093
1094                        if dist_between_tops < threshold:
1095                            combined_tops = np.vstack([top1, top2])
1096                            center_point = np.mean(combined_tops, axis=0)
1097                        else:
1098                            center_point = center1
1099                    else:
1100                        center_point = center1
1101                else:
1102                    center_point = np.array([mean_x, mean_y])
1103
1104                cluster_median = np.median(coords, axis=0)
1105                alpha = 0.5
1106                center_point = (1 - alpha) * center_point + alpha * cluster_median
1107
1108            else:
1109                center_point = np.array([0, 0])
1110
1111            cord_list.append(center_point)
1112
1113        if inc_num:
1114
1115            bbox_props = (
1116                dict(
1117                    boxstyle="round,pad=0.1",
1118                    facecolor="white",
1119                    edgecolor="none",
1120                    alpha=0.7,
1121                )
1122                if inc_bbox
1123                else None
1124            )
1125
1126            texts = []
1127            repeat_lab = []
1128            for (x, y), num in zip(cord_list, numeric_df["id_vec"]):
1129                if num not in repeat_lab:
1130                    texts.append(
1131                        ax.text(
1132                            x,
1133                            y,
1134                            str(num),
1135                            ha="center",
1136                            va="center",
1137                            fontsize=font_size,
1138                            color="black",
1139                            bbox=bbox_props,
1140                        )
1141                    )
1142                    repeat_lab.append(num)
1143
1144            adjust_text(
1145                texts,
1146                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", lw=0.5),
1147                force_text=(1.2, 1.2),
1148                force_points=(1.0, 1.0),
1149                expand_text=(1.3, 1.3),
1150                expand_points=(1.3, 1.3),
1151                lim=500,
1152            )
1153
1154        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1155        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1156
1157        ax.grid(grid)
1158
1159        handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
1160
1161        def sort_key(item):
1162            num_str = item[1].split(" - ")[0]
1163            parts = num_str.split(".")
1164            main_num = int(parts[0])
1165            sub_num = int(parts[1]) if len(parts) > 1 else 0
1166            return (main_num, sub_num)
1167
1168        sorted_pairs = sorted(zip(handles, labels), key=sort_key)
1169        sorted_handles, sorted_labels = zip(*sorted_pairs)
1170
1171        if not inc_num:
1172            sorted_labels = [lbl.split(" - ", 1)[1] for lbl in sorted_labels]
1173
1174        unique_datasets = umap_df["dataset"].unique()
1175        dataset_handles = list(sorted_handles)
1176        dataset_labels = list(sorted_labels)
1177
1178        if len(unique_datasets) > 1:
1179            for ds in unique_datasets:
1180                proxy_marker = Line2D(
1181                    [0],
1182                    [0],
1183                    marker=marker_map[ds],
1184                    color="w",
1185                    markerfacecolor="gray",
1186                    markeredgecolor="black",
1187                    markersize=current_size * 2,
1188                    linestyle="None",
1189                    label=f"Set: {ds}",
1190                )
1191
1192                dataset_handles.append(proxy_marker)
1193                dataset_labels.append(f"Data: {ds}")
1194
1195        ax.legend(
1196            dataset_handles,
1197            dataset_labels,
1198            title="",
1199            loc="center left",
1200            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 0.5),
1201            ncol=legend_split_col,
1202            markerscale=15,
1203        )
1204
1205        ax.grid(grid, which="both")
1206
1207        plt.tight_layout()
1208
1209        return fig

Visualize UMAP embeddings with sample labels based on specyfic metadata slot.

Parameters

def UMAP_feature( self, feature_name: str, features_data: pandas.core.frame.DataFrame | None, point_size: int | float = 0.6, font_size: int | float = 6, width: int = 8, height: int = 6, palette='light', grid: bool = False, rasterized: bool = True): 
1211    def UMAP_feature(
1212        self,
1213        feature_name: str,
1214        features_data: pd.DataFrame | None,
1215        point_size: int | float = 0.6,
1216        font_size: int | float = 6,
1217        width: int = 8,
1218        height: int = 6,
1219        palette="light",
1220        grid: bool = False,
1221        rasterized: bool = True,
1222    ):
1223        """
1224        Visualize UMAP embedding with expression levels of a selected feature.
1225
1226        Each point (cell) in the UMAP plot is colored according to the expression
1227        value of the chosen feature, enabling interpretation of spatial patterns
1228        of gene activity or metadata distribution in low-dimensional space.
1229
1230        Parameters
1231        ----------
1232        feature_name : str
1233           Name of the feature to plot.
1234
1235        features_data : pandas.DataFrame or None, default None
1236            If None, the function uses the DataFrame containing the clustering data.
1237            To plot features not used in clustering, provide a wider DataFrame
1238            containing the original feature values.
1239
1240        point_size : float, default 0.6
1241            Size of scatter points in the plot.
1242
1243        font_size : int, default 6
1244            Font size for axis labels and annotations.
1245
1246        width : int, default 8
1247            Width of the matplotlib figure.
1248
1249        height : int, default 6
1250            Height of the matplotlib figure.
1251
1252        grid : bool, default False
1253            If True, the plot grid will be visible.
1254
1255        palette : str, default 'light'
1256            Color palette for expression visualization. Options are:
1257            - 'light'
1258            - 'dark'
1259            - 'green'
1260            - 'gray'
1261
1262        rasterized : bool, default True
1263            If True, rasterizes scatter/point collections when saving vector
1264            formats (such as SVG or PDF) to keep file sizes small for large
1265            datasets while keeping text, labels, axes, and legends as crisp vectors.
1266
1267        Returns
1268        -------
1269        matplotlib.figure.Figure
1270            UMAP scatter plot colored by feature values.
1271        """
1272
1273        umap_df = self.umap.iloc[:, 0:2].copy()
1274
1275        if features_data is None:
1276            features_data = self.clustering_data
1277
1278        if features_data.shape[1] != umap_df.shape[0]:
1279            raise ValueError(
1280                "Imputed 'features_data' shape does not match the number of UMAP"
1281                " cells"
1282            )
1283
1284        blist = [
1285            True if x.upper() == feature_name.upper() else False
1286            for x in features_data.index
1287        ]
1288
1289        if not any(blist):
1290            raise ValueError("Imputed feature_name is not included in the data")
1291
1292        umap_df.loc[:, "feature"] = (
1293            features_data.loc[blist, :]
1294            .apply(lambda row: row.tolist(), axis=1)
1295            .values[0]
1296        )
1297
1298        umap_df = umap_df.sort_values("feature", ascending=True)
1299
1300        vals = umap_df["feature"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
1301        vmin, vmax = vals.min(), vals.max()
1302
1303        if vmax > vmin:
1304            norm_vals = (vals - vmin) / (vmax - vmin)
1305        else:
1306            norm_vals = np.ones_like(vals)
1307
1308        min_scale = 0.1
1309        sizes = point_size * (min_scale + (1.0 - min_scale) * norm_vals)
1310
1311        def px_to_rgb01(px_seq):
1312            out = []
1313            for c in px_seq:
1314                rgb_255 = px.colors.unlabel_rgb(c)
1315                out.append(tuple(v / 255.0 for v in rgb_255))
1316            return out
1317
1318        def sample_colors(px_seq, n_colors):
1319            rgb_seq = px_to_rgb01(px_seq)
1320            if n_colors <= 1:
1321                return rgb_seq[:n_colors]
1322            idxs = np.linspace(0, len(rgb_seq) - 1, n_colors).round().astype(int)
1323            return [rgb_seq[i] for i in idxs]
1324
1325        n_groups = len(px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark)
1326
1327        norm = None
1328
1329        if palette in ("gray-red", "gray-blue"):
1330            base_px = (
1331                px.colors.sequential.Reds
1332                if palette == "gray-red"
1333                else px.colors.sequential.Blues
1334            )
1335            grad_colors = sample_colors(base_px[3:], max(n_groups - 1, 1))
1336            gray_rgb = (0.72, 0.72, 0.72)
1337
1338            if vmax > vmin:
1339                if vmin <= 0.0 < vmax and np.any(vals > 0.0):
1340                    eps = min(np.min(vals[vals > 0.0]) * 0.5, (vmax - 0.0) * 1e-3)
1341                    pos_bounds = np.linspace(eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1342                    bounds = np.concatenate(([min(vmin, 0.0)], pos_bounds))
1343                else:
1344                    eps = (vmax - vmin) * 1e-3
1345                    rest_bounds = np.linspace(vmin + eps, vmax, len(grad_colors) + 1)
1346                    bounds = np.concatenate(([vmin], rest_bounds))
1347
1348                colors_list = [gray_rgb] + grad_colors
1349                norm = mcolors.BoundaryNorm(bounds, ncolors=len(colors_list))
1350                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(colors_list, name=palette)
1351            else:
1352                my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap([gray_rgb], name=palette)
1353
1354        else:
1355            if palette == "light":
1356                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Sunsetdark
1357            elif palette == "dark":
1358                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.thermal
1359            elif palette == "green":
1360                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.Aggrnyl
1361            elif palette == "gray":
1362                px_palette = px.colors.sequential.gray[::-1]
1363            else:
1364                raise ValueError(
1365                    'Palette not found. Use: "light", "dark", "gray", "green",'
1366                    ' "gray-red", or "gray-blue"'
1367                )
1368
1369            converted = sample_colors(px_palette, n_groups)
1370            my_cmap = mcolors.ListedColormap(converted, name="custom")
1371
1372        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
1373        sc = ax.scatter(
1374            umap_df["UMAP1"],
1375            umap_df["UMAP2"],
1376            c=umap_df["feature"],
1377            s=sizes * 5,
1378            cmap=my_cmap,
1379            norm=norm,
1380            alpha=1,
1381            edgecolors="white",
1382            linewidths=0,
1383            rasterized=rasterized,
1384        )
1385
1386        cbar = plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
1387        cbar.set_label(f"{feature_name}")
1388        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MaxNLocator(nbins=5))
1389        cbar.ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FormatStrFormatter("%.1f"))
1390
1391        ax.set_xlabel("UMAP 1")
1392        ax.set_ylabel("UMAP 2")
1393
1394        ax.grid(grid)
1395
1396        plt.tight_layout()
1397
1398        return fig

Visualize UMAP embedding with expression levels of a selected feature.

Returns

matplotlib.figure.Figure UMAP scatter plot colored by feature values.

def get_umap_data(self): 
1400    def get_umap_data(self):
1401        """
1402        Retrieve UMAP embedding data with optional cluster labels.
1403
1404        Returns the UMAP coordinates stored in `self.umap`. If clustering
1405        metadata is available (specifically `UMAP_clusters`), the corresponding
1406        cluster assignments are appended as an additional column.
1407
1408        Returns
1409        -------
1410        pandas.DataFrame
1411            DataFrame containing UMAP coordinates (columns: 'UMAP1', 'UMAP2', ...).
1412            If available, includes an extra column 'clusters' with cluster labels.
1413
1414        Notes
1415        -----
1416        - UMAP embeddings must be computed beforehand (e.g., using `perform_UMAP`).
1417        - Cluster labels are added only if present in `self.clustering_metadata`.
1418        """
1419
1420        umap_data = self.umap
1421
1422        try:
1423            umap_data["clusters"] = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]
1424        except:
1425            pass
1426
1427        return umap_data

1458    def return_clusters(self, clusters="umap"):
1459        """
1460        Retrieve cluster labels from UMAP or PCA clustering results.
1461
1462        Parameters
1463        ----------

1466            - 'umap': return cluster labels from UMAP embeddings.
1467            - 'pca' : return cluster labels from PCA embeddings.

1470        -------

1474        Raises
1475        ------
1476        ValueError
1477            If `clusters` is not 'umap' or 'pca'.
1478
1479        Notes
1480        -----
1481        Requires that clustering has already been performed
1482        (e.g., using `find_clusters_UMAP` or `find_clusters_PCA`).
1483        """
1484
1485        if clusters.lower() == "umap":
1486            clusters_vector = self.clustering_metadata["UMAP_clusters"]

class COMPsc(Clustering): 
1495class COMPsc(Clustering):
1496    """
1497    A class `COMPsc` (Comparison of single-cell data) designed for the integration,
1498    analysis, and visualization of single-cell datasets.
1499    The class supports independent dataset integration, subclustering of existing clusters,
1500    marker detection, and multiple visualization strategies.
1501
1502    The COMPsc class provides methods for:
1503
1504        - Normalizing and filtering single-cell data
1505        - Loading and saving sparse 10x-style datasets
1506        - Computing differential expression and marker genes
1507        - Clustering and subclustering analysis
1508        - Visualizing similarity and spatial relationships
1509        - Aggregating data by cell and set annotations
1510        - Managing metadata and renaming labels
1511        - Plotting gene detection histograms and feature dot plots
1512

1615    def __init__(

1634        -agg_normalized_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1635        -similarity : pandas.DataFrame or None
1636        -var_data : pandas.DataFrame or None

1638        -cells_calc : pandas.Series or None
1639        -gene_calc : pandas.Series or None
1640        -composition_data : pandas.DataFrame or None
1641        """
1642
1643        self.objects = objects
1644        """ Stores the input data objects."""

1646        self.input_data = None
1647        """Raw input data for clustering or integration analysis."""

1649        self.input_metadata = None
1650        """Metadata associated with the input data."""

1653        """Normalized version of the input data."""

1655        self.agg_metadata = None

1658        self.agg_normalized_data = None

1679    @classmethod
1680    def project_dir(cls, path_to_directory, project_list):
1681        """
1682        Scan a directory and build a COMPsc instance mapping provided project names
1683        to their paths.
1684
1685        Parameters
1686        ----------
1687        path_to_directory : str
1688            Path containing project subfolders.
1689
1690        project_list : list[str]
1691            List of filenames (folder names) to include in the returned object map.
1692
1693        Returns
1694        -------
1695        COMPsc
1696            New COMPsc instance with `objects` populated.
1697
1698        Raises
1699        ------
1700        Exception
1701            A generic exception is caught and a message printed if scanning fails.
1702
1703        Notes
1704        -----
1705        Function attempts to match entries in `project_list` to directory
1706        names and constructs a simplified object key from the folder name.
1707        """
1708        try:
1709            objects = {}
1710            for filename in tqdm(os.listdir(path_to_directory)):
1711                for c in project_list:
1712                    f = os.path.join(path_to_directory, filename)
1713                    if c == filename and os.path.isdir(f):
1714                        objects[str(c)] = f
1715
1716            return cls(objects)
1717
1718        except:
1719            print("Something went wrong. Check the function input data and try again!")
1720
1721    def save_project(self, name, path: str = os.getcwd()):
1722        """
1723        Save the COMPsc object to disk using pickle.
1724
1725        Parameters
1726        ----------
1727        name : str
1728            Base filename (without extension) to use when saving.
1729
1730        path : str, default os.getcwd()
1731            Directory in which to save the project file.
1732
1733        Returns
1734        -------
1735        None
1736
1737        Side Effects
1738        ------------
1739        - Writes a file `<path>/<name>.jpkl` containing the pickled object.
1740        - Prints a confirmation message with saved path.
1741        """
1742
1743        full = os.path.join(path, f"{name}.jpkl")
1744
1745        with open(full, "wb") as f:
1746            pickle.dump(self, f)
1747
1748        print(f"Project saved as {full}")
1749
1750    @classmethod
1751    def load_project(cls, path):
1752        """
1753        Load a previously saved COMPsc project from a pickle file.
1754
1755        Parameters
1756        ----------
1757        path : str
1758            Full path to the pickled project file.
1759
1760        Returns
1761        -------
1762        COMPsc
1763            The unpickled COMPsc object.
1764
1765        Raises
1766        ------
1767        FileNotFoundError
1768            If the provided path does not exist.
1769        """
1770
1771        if not os.path.exists(path):
1772            raise FileNotFoundError("File does not exist!")
1773        with open(path, "rb") as f:
1774            obj = pickle.load(f)
1775        return obj

1777    def reduce_cols(

1780        full: str | None = None,
1781        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
1782        inc_set: bool = False,
1783    ):
1784        """
1785        Remove columns (cells) whose names contain a substring `reg` or
1786        full name `full` from available tables.

1804        Update

1806        Mutates `self.input_data`, `self.normalized_data`, `self.input_metadata`,
1807        `self.agg_normalized_data`, and `self.agg_metadata` (if they exist),
1808        removing columns/rows that match `reg`.

1810        Raises
1811        ------
1812        Raises ValueError if nothing matches the reduction mask.
1813        """
1814
1815        if reg is None and full is None:

1817                "Both 'reg' and 'full' arguments not provided. Please provide at least one of them!"
1818            )
1819
1820        if reg is not None and full is not None:

1822                "Both 'reg' and 'full' arguments are provided. "

1829

1831

1833

1835                        self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1836                        + " # "

1839

1841
1842                    self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
1843
1844                mask = [reg.upper() not in x.upper() for x in self.input_data.columns]
1845

2113    def reduce_rows(self, features_list: list):
2114        """
2115        Remove rows (features) whose names are included in features_list.
2116
2117        Parameters
2118        ----------
2119        features_list : list
2120            List of features to search for in index/gene names; matching entries will be removed.
2121
2122        Update
2123        ------------
2124        Mutates `self.input_data`, `self.normalized_data`, `self.input_metadata`,
2125        `self.agg_normalized_data`, and `self.agg_metadata` (if they exist),
2126        removing columns/rows that match `reg`.
2127
2128        Raises
2129        ------
2130        Prints a message listing features that are not found in the data.
2131        """
2132
2133        if self.input_data is not None:
2134
2135            res = find_features(self.input_data, features=features_list)
2136
2137            res_list = [x.upper() for x in res["included"]]
2138
2139            mask = [x.upper() not in res_list for x in self.input_data.index]
2140
2141            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2142                raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
2143
2144            self.input_data = self.input_data.loc[mask, :]
2145
2146        if self.normalized_data is not None:
2147
2148            res = find_features(self.normalized_data, features=features_list)
2149
2150            res_list = [x.upper() for x in res["included"]]
2151
2152            mask = [x.upper() not in res_list for x in self.normalized_data.index]
2153
2154            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2155                raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
2156
2157            self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.loc[mask, :]
2158
2159        if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
2160
2161            res = find_features(self.agg_normalized_data, features=features_list)
2162
2163            res_list = [x.upper() for x in res["included"]]
2164
2165            mask = [x.upper() not in res_list for x in self.agg_normalized_data.index]
2166
2167            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2168                raise ValueError("Nothing found to reduce")
2169
2170            self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.loc[mask, :]
2171
2172        if len(res["not_included"]) > 0:
2173            print("\nFeatures not found:")
2174            for i in res["not_included"]:
2175                print(i)
2176
2177        self.gene_calculation()
2178        self.cells_calculation()

2180    def get_data(self, set_info: bool = False):

2197        AttributeError
2198            If `self.normalized_data` or `self.input_metadata` is missing.
2199        """
2200
2201        to_return = self.normalized_data
2202
2203        if set_info:
2204            to_return.columns = (
2205                self.input_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + self.input_metadata["sets"]
2206            )
2207        else:
2208            to_return.columns = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
2209
2210        return to_return
2211
2212    def get_partial_data(
2213        self,
2214        names: list | str | None = None,
2215        features: list | str | None = None,
2216        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
2217        inc_metadata: bool = False,
2218    ):
2219        """
2220        Return a subset of the data filtered by sample names and/or feature names.
2221
2222        Parameters
2223        ----------
2224        names : list, str, or None
2225            Names of samples to include. If None, all samples are considered.
2226
2227        features : list, str, or None
2228            Names of features to include. If None, all features are considered.
2229
2230        name_slot : str
2231            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
2232
2233        inc_metadata : bool
2234            If True return tuple (data, metadata)
2235
2236        Returns
2237        -------
2238        pandas.DataFrame
2239            Subset of the normalized data based on the specified names and features.
2240        """
2241
2242        data = self.normalized_data.copy()
2243        metadata = self.input_metadata
2244
2245        if name_slot in self.input_metadata.columns:
2246            data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2247        else:
2248            raise ValueError("'name_slot' not occured in data!'")
2249
2250        if isinstance(features, str):
2251            features = [features]
2252        elif features is None:
2253            features = []
2254
2255        if isinstance(names, str):
2256            names = [names]
2257        elif names is None:
2258            names = []
2259
2260        features = [x.upper() for x in features]
2261        names = [x.upper() for x in names]
2262
2263        columns_names = [x.upper() for x in data.columns]
2264        features_names = [x.upper() for x in data.index]
2265
2266        columns_bool = [True if x in names else False for x in columns_names]
2267        features_bool = [True if x in features else False for x in features_names]
2268
2269        if True not in columns_bool and True not in features_bool:
2270            print("Missing 'names' and/or 'features'. Returning full dataset instead.")
2271
2272        if True in columns_bool:
2273            data = data.loc[:, columns_bool]
2274            metadata = metadata.loc[columns_bool, :]
2275
2276        if True in features_bool:
2277            data = data.loc[features_bool, :]
2278
2279        not_in_features = [y for y in features if y not in features_names]
2280
2281        if len(not_in_features) > 0:
2282            print("\nThe following features were not found in data:")
2283            print("\n".join(not_in_features))
2284
2285        not_in_names = [y for y in names if y not in columns_names]
2286
2287        if len(not_in_names) > 0:
2288            print("\nThe following names were not found in data:")
2289            print("\n".join(not_in_names))
2290
2291        if inc_metadata:
2292            return data, metadata
2293        else:
2294            return data
2295
2296    def get_metadata(self):

2302        pandas.DataFrame

2304        """
2305
