2310    def gene_calculation(self):
2311        """
2312        Calculate and store per-cell counts (e.g., number of detected genes).
2313
2314        The method computes a binary (presence/absence) per cell and sums across
2315        features to produce `self.gene_calc`.
2316
2317        Update
2318        ------
2319        Sets `self.gene_calc` as a pandas.Series.
2320
2321        Side Effects
2322        ------------
2323        Uses `self.input_data` when available, otherwise `self.normalized_data`.
2324        """
2325
2326        if self.input_data is not None:
2327
2328            bin_col = self.input_data.columns.copy()
2329
2330            bin_col = bin_col.where(bin_col <= 0, 1)
2331
2332            sum_data = bin_col.sum(axis=0)
2333
2334            self.gene_calc = sum_data
2335
2336        elif self.normalized_data is not None:
2337
2338            bin_col = self.normalized_data.copy()
2339
2340            bin_col = bin_col.where(bin_col <= 0, 1)
2341
2342            sum_data = bin_col.sum(axis=0)
2343
2344            self.gene_calc = sum_data
2345
2346    def gene_histograme(self, bins=100):
2347        """
2348        Plot a histogram of the number of genes detected per cell.
2349
2350        Parameters
2351        ----------
2352        bins : int, default 100
2353            Number of histogram bins.
2354
2355        Returns
2356        -------
2357        matplotlib.figure.Figure
2358            Figure containing the histogram of gene contents.
2359
2360        Notes
2361        -----
2362        Requires `self.gene_calc` to be computed prior to calling.
2363        """
2364
2365        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
2366
2367        _, bin_edges, _ = ax.hist(
2368            self.gene_calc, bins=bins, edgecolor="black", alpha=0.6
2369        )
2370
2371        mu, sigma = np.mean(self.gene_calc), np.std(self.gene_calc)
2372
2373        x = np.linspace(min(self.gene_calc), max(self.gene_calc), 1000)
2374        y = norm.pdf(x, mu, sigma)
2375
2376        y_scaled = y * len(self.gene_calc) * (bin_edges[1] - bin_edges[0])
2377
2378        ax.plot(
2379            x, y_scaled, "r-", linewidth=2, label=f"Normal(μ={mu:.2f}, σ={sigma:.2f})"
2380        )
2381
2382        ax.set_xlabel("Value")
2383        ax.set_ylabel("Count")
2384        ax.set_title("Histogram of genes detected per cell")
2385
2386        ax.set_xticks(np.linspace(min(self.gene_calc), max(self.gene_calc), 20))
2387        ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=90)
2388
2389        ax.legend()
2390
2391        return fig

2393    def gene_threshold(self, min_n: int | None, max_n: int | None):
2394        """
2395        Filter cells by gene-detection thresholds (min and/or max).
2396
2397        Parameters
2398        ----------
2399        min_n : int or None
2400            Minimum number of detected genes required to keep a cell.
2401
2402        max_n : int or None
2403            Maximum number of detected genes allowed to keep a cell.
2404
2405        Update
2406        -------
2407        Filters `self.input_data`, `self.normalized_data`, `self.input_metadata`
2408        (and calls `average()` if `self.agg_normalized_data` exists).
2409
2410        Side Effects
2411        ------------
2412        Raises ValueError if both bounds are None or if filtering removes all cells.
2413        """
2414
2415        if min_n is not None and max_n is not None:
2416            mask = (self.gene_calc > min_n) & (self.gene_calc < max_n)
2417        elif min_n is None and max_n is not None:
2418            mask = self.gene_calc < max_n
2419        elif min_n is not None and max_n is None:
2420            mask = self.gene_calc > min_n
2421        else:
2422            raise ValueError("Lack of both min_n and max_n values")
2423
2424        if self.input_data is not None:
2425
2426            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2427                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2428
2429            self.input_data = self.input_data.loc[:, mask.values]
2430
2431        if self.normalized_data is not None:
2432
2433            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2434                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2435
2436            self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.loc[:, mask.values]
2437
2438        if self.input_metadata is not None:
2439
2440            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2441                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2442
2443            self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.loc[mask.values, :].reset_index(
2444                drop=True
2445            )
2446
2447            self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.drop(
2448                columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
2449            )
2450
2451        if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
2452            self.average()
2453
2454        self.gene_calculation()
2455        self.cells_calculation()
2456
2457    def cells_calculation(self, name_slot="cell_names"):
2458        """
2459        Calculate number of cells per  call name / cluster.
2460
2461        The method computes a binary (presence/absence) per cell name / cluster and sums across
2462        cells.
2463
2464        Parameters
2465        ----------
2466        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
2467            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
2468
2469        Update
2470        ------
2471        Sets `self.cells_calc` as a pd.DataFrame.
2472        """
2473
2474        ls = list(self.input_metadata[name_slot])
2475
2476        df = pd.DataFrame(
2477            {
2478                "cluster": pd.Series(ls).value_counts().index,
2479                "n": pd.Series(ls).value_counts().values,
2480            }
2481        )
2482
2483        self.cells_calc = df
2484

2547    def cluster_threshold(self, min_n: int | None, name_slot: str = "cell_names"):
2548        """
2549        Filter cell names / clusters by cell-detection threshold.
2550
2551        Parameters
2552        ----------
2553        min_n : int or None
2554            Minimum number of detected genes required to keep a cell.

2556        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'

2559
2560        Update
2561        -------

2563        (and calls `average()` if `self.agg_normalized_data` exists).

2565
2566        if name_slot != "cell_names":
2567            self.cells_calculation(name_slot=name_slot)
2568
2569        if min_n is not None:
2570            names = self.cells_calc["cluster"][self.cells_calc["n"] < min_n]
2571        else:
2572            raise ValueError("Lack of min_n value")
2573
2574        if len(names) > 0:
2575
2576            if self.input_data is not None:
2577
2578                self.input_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2579
2580                mask = [not any(r in x for r in names) for x in self.input_data.columns]
2581
2582                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) > 0:
2583
2584                    self.input_data = self.input_data.loc[:, mask]
2585
2586            if self.normalized_data is not None:
2587
2588                self.normalized_data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2589
2590                mask = [
2591                    not any(r in x for r in names) for x in self.normalized_data.columns
2592                ]
2593
2594                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) > 0:
2595
2596                    self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.loc[:, mask]
2597
2598            if self.input_metadata is not None:
2599
2600                self.input_metadata["drop"] = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2601
2602                mask = [
2603                    not any(r in x for r in names) for x in self.input_metadata["drop"]
2604                ]
2605
2606                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) > 0:
2607
2608                    self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.loc[mask, :].reset_index(
2609                        drop=True
2610                    )
2611
2612                self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.drop(
2613                    columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
2614                )
2615
2616            if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
2617
2618                self.agg_normalized_data.columns = self.agg_metadata[name_slot]
2619
2620                mask = [
2621                    not any(r in x for r in names)
2622                    for x in self.agg_normalized_data.columns
2623                ]
2624
2625                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) > 0:
2626
2627                    self.agg_normalized_data = self.agg_normalized_data.loc[:, mask]
2628
2629            if self.agg_metadata is not None:
2630
2631                self.agg_metadata["drop"] = self.agg_metadata[name_slot]
2632
2633                mask = [
2634                    not any(r in x for r in names) for x in self.agg_metadata["drop"]
2635                ]
2636
2637                if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) > 0:
2638
2639                    self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.loc[mask, :].reset_index(
2640                        drop=True
2641                    )
2642
2643                self.agg_metadata = self.agg_metadata.drop(
2644                    columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
2645                )
2646
2647            self.gene_calculation()
2648            self.cells_calculation()

2650    def load_sparse_from_projects(self, normalized_data: bool = False):
2651        """
2652        Load sparse 10x-style datasets from stored project paths, concatenate them,
2653        and populate `input_data` / `normalized_data` and `input_metadata`.
2654
2655        Parameters
2656        ----------
2657        normalized_data : bool, default False
2658            If True, store concatenated tables in `self.normalized_data`.
2659            If False, store them in `self.input_data` and normalization
2660            is needed using normalize_data() method.
2661
2662        Side Effects
2663        ------------
2664        - Reads each project using `load_sparse(...)` (expects matrix.mtx, genes.tsv, barcodes.tsv).
2665        - Concatenates all projects column-wise and sets `self.input_metadata`.
2666        - Replaces NaNs with zeros and updates `self.gene_calc`.
2667        """
2668
2669        obj = self.objects
2670
2671        full_data = pd.DataFrame()
2672        full_metadata = pd.DataFrame()
2673
2674        for ke in obj.keys():
2675            print(ke)
2676
2677            dt, met = load_sparse(path=obj[ke], name=ke)
2678
2679            full_data = pd.concat([full_data, dt], axis=1)
2680            full_metadata = pd.concat([full_metadata, met], axis=0)
2681
2682        full_data[np.isnan(full_data)] = 0
2683
2684        if normalized_data:
2685            self.normalized_data = full_data
2686            self.input_metadata = full_metadata
2687        else:
2688
2689            self.input_data = full_data
2690            self.input_metadata = full_metadata
2691
2692        self.gene_calculation()
2693        self.cells_calculation()
2694
2695    def rename_names(self, mapping: dict, slot: str = "cell_names"):
2696        """
2697        Rename entries in `self.input_metadata[slot]` according to a provided mapping.
2698
2699        Parameters
2700        ----------
2701        mapping : dict
2702            Dictionary with keys 'old_name' and 'new_name', each mapping to a list
2703            of equal length describing replacements.
2704
2705        slot : str, default 'cell_names'
2706            Metadata column to operate on.
2707
2708        Update
2709        -------
2710        Updates `self.input_metadata[slot]` in-place with renamed values.
2711
2712        Raises
2713        ------
2714        ValueError
2715            If mapping keys are incorrect, lengths differ, or some 'old_name' values
2716            are not present in the metadata column.
2717        """
2718
2719        if set(["old_name", "new_name"]) != set(mapping.keys()):
2720            raise ValueError(
2721                "Mapping dictionary must contain keys 'old_name' and 'new_name', "
2722                "each with a list of names to change."
2723            )
2724
2725        if len(mapping["old_name"]) != len(mapping["new_name"]):
2726            raise ValueError(
2727                "Mapping dictionary lists 'old_name' and 'new_name' "
2728                "must have the same length!"
2729            )
2730
2731        names_vector = list(self.input_metadata[slot])
2732
2733        if not all(elem in names_vector for elem in list(mapping["old_name"])):
2734            raise ValueError(
2735                f"Some entries from 'old_name' do not exist in the names of slot {slot}."
2736            )
2737
2738        replace_dict = dict(zip(mapping["old_name"], mapping["new_name"]))
2739
2740        names_vector_ret = [replace_dict.get(item, item) for item in names_vector]
2741
2742        self.input_metadata[slot] = names_vector_ret
2743
2744    def rename_subclusters(self, mapping):
2745        """
2746        Rename labels stored in `self.subclusters_.subclusters` according to mapping.
2747
2748        Parameters
2749        ----------

2751            Mapping with keys 'old_name' and 'new_name' (lists of equal length).
2752
2753        Update
2754        -------
2755        Updates `self.subclusters_.subclusters` with renamed labels.
2756
2757        Raises
2758        ------
2759        ValueError
2760            If mapping is invalid or old names are not present.
2761        """
2762
2763        if set(["old_name", "new_name"]) != set(mapping.keys()):
2764            raise ValueError(
2765                "Mapping dictionary must contain keys 'old_name' and 'new_name', "
2766                "each with a list of names to change."
2767            )
2768
2769        if len(mapping["old_name"]) != len(mapping["new_name"]):
2770            raise ValueError(
2771                "Mapping dictionary lists 'old_name' and 'new_name' "
2772                "must have the same length!"
2773            )
2774
2775        names_vector = list(self.subclusters_.subclusters)
2776
2777        if not all(elem in names_vector for elem in list(mapping["old_name"])):
2778            raise ValueError(
2779                "Some entries from 'old_name' do not exist in the subcluster names."
2780            )
2781
2782        replace_dict = dict(zip(mapping["old_name"], mapping["new_name"]))
2783
2784        names_vector_ret = [replace_dict.get(item, item) for item in names_vector]

2788    def save_sparse(
2789        self,
2790        path_to_save: str = os.getcwd(),
2791        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
2792        data_slot: str = "normalized",
2793    ):
2794        """
2795        Export data as 10x-compatible sparse files (matrix.mtx, barcodes.tsv, genes.tsv).
2796
2797        Parameters
2798        ----------
2799        path_to_save : str, default current working directory
2800            Directory where files will be written.
2801
2802        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
2803            Metadata column providing cell names for barcodes.tsv.
2804
2805        data_slot : str, default 'normalized'
2806            Either 'normalized' (uses self.normalized_data) or 'count' (uses self.input_data).
2807
2808        Raises
2809        ------
2810        ValueError
2811            If `data_slot` is not 'normalized' or 'count'.
2812        """
2813
2814        names = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2815
2816        if data_slot.lower() == "normalized":
2817
2818            features = list(self.normalized_data.index)
2819            mtx = sparse.csr_matrix(self.normalized_data)
2820
2821        elif data_slot.lower() == "count":
2822
2823            features = list(self.input_data.index)
2824            mtx = sparse.csr_matrix(self.input_data)
2825
2826        else:
2827            raise ValueError("'data_slot' must be included in 'normalized' or 'count'")
2828
2829        os.makedirs(path_to_save, exist_ok=True)
2830
2831        mmwrite(os.path.join(path_to_save, "matrix.mtx"), mtx)
2832
2833        pd.Series(names).to_csv(
2834            os.path.join(path_to_save, "barcodes.tsv"),
2835            index=False,
2836            header=False,
2837            sep="\t",
2838        )
2839
2840        pd.Series(features).to_csv(
2841            os.path.join(path_to_save, "genes.tsv"), index=False, header=False, sep="\t"
2842        )
2843
2844    def normalize_counts(
2845        self, normalize_factor: int = 100000, log_transform: bool = True
2846    ):
2847        """
2848        Normalize raw counts to counts-per-(normalize_factor)
2849        (e.g., CPM, TPM - depending on normalize_factor).
2850
2851        Parameters
2852        ----------
2853        normalize_factor : int, default 100000
2854            Scaling factor used after dividing by column sums.
2855
2856        log_transform : bool, default True
2857            If True, apply log2(x+1) transformation to normalized values.
2858
2859        Update
2860        -------
2861            Sets `self.normalized_data` to normalized values (fills NaNs with 0).
2862
2863        Raises
2864        ------
2865        ValueError
2866            If `self.input_data` is missing (cannot normalize).
2867        """
2868        if self.input_data is None:
2869            raise ValueError("Input data is missing, cannot normalize.")
2870
2871        sum_col = self.input_data.sum()
2872        self.normalized_data = self.input_data.div(sum_col).fillna(0) * normalize_factor
2873
2874        if log_transform:
2875            # log2(x + 1) to avoid -inf for zeros
2876            self.normalized_data = np.log2(self.normalized_data + 1)
2877
2878    def statistic(
2879        self,
2880        cells=None,
2881        sets=None,
2882        with_sets_names: bool = False,
2883        min_exp: float = 0.01,
2884        min_pct: float = 0.1,
2885        n_proc: int = 10,
2886    ):
2887        """
2888        Compute per-feature statistics (Mann–Whitney U) comparing target vs rest.
2889
2890        This is a wrapper similar to `calc_DEG` tailored to use `self.normalized_data`
2891        and `self.input_metadata`. It returns per-feature statistics including p-values,
2892        adjusted p-values, means, variances, effect-size measures and fold-changes.
2893
2894        Parameters
2895        ----------
2896        cells : list, 'All', dict, or None
2897            Defines the target cells or groups for comparison (several modes supported).
2898
2899        sets : 'All', dict, or None
2900            Alternative grouping mode (operate on `self.input_metadata['sets']`).
2901
2902        min_exp : float, default 0.01
2903            Minimum expression threshold used when filtering features.
2904
2905        min_pct : float, default 0.1
2906            Minimum proportion of expressing cells in the target group required to test a feature.
2907
2908        n_proc : int, default 10
2909            Number of parallel jobs to use.
2910
2911        Returns
2912        -------
2913        pandas.DataFrame or dict
2914            Results DataFrame (or dict containing valid/control cells + DataFrame),
2915            similar to `calc_DEG` interface.
2916
2917        Raises
2918        ------
2919        ValueError
2920            If neither `cells` nor `sets` is provided, or input metadata mismatch occurs.
2921
2922        Notes
2923        -----
2924        Multiple modes supported: single-list entities, 'All', pairwise dicts, etc.
2925        """
2926
2927        offset = 1e-100
2928
2929        def stat_calc(choose, feature_name):
2930            target_values = choose.loc[choose["DEG"] == "target", feature_name]
2931            rest_values = choose.loc[choose["DEG"] == "rest", feature_name]
2932
2933            pct_valid = (target_values > 0).sum() / len(target_values)
2934            pct_rest = (rest_values > 0).sum() / len(rest_values)
2935
2936            avg_valid = np.mean(target_values)
2937            avg_ctrl = np.mean(rest_values)
2938            sd_valid = np.std(target_values, ddof=1)
2939            sd_ctrl = np.std(rest_values, ddof=1)
2940            esm = (avg_valid - avg_ctrl) / np.sqrt(((sd_valid**2 + sd_ctrl**2) / 2))
2941
2942            if np.sum(target_values) == np.sum(rest_values):
2943                p_val = 1.0
2944            else:
2945                _, p_val = stats.mannwhitneyu(
2946                    target_values, rest_values, alternative="two-sided"
2947                )
2948
2949            return {
2950                "feature": feature_name,
2951                "p_val": p_val,
2952                "pct_valid": pct_valid,
2953                "pct_ctrl": pct_rest,
2954                "avg_valid": avg_valid,
2955                "avg_ctrl": avg_ctrl,
2956                "sd_valid": sd_valid,
2957                "sd_ctrl": sd_ctrl,
2958                "esm": esm,
2959            }
2960
2961        def prepare_and_run_stat(choose, valid_group, min_exp, min_pct, n_proc):
2962
2963            def safe_min_half(series):
2964                filtered = series[(series > ((2**-1074) * 2)) & (series.notna())]
2965                return filtered.min() / 2 if not filtered.empty else 0
2966
2967            tmp_dat = choose[choose["DEG"] == "target"]
2968            tmp_dat = tmp_dat.drop("DEG", axis=1)
2969
2970            counts = (tmp_dat > min_exp).sum(axis=0)
2971
2972            total_count = tmp_dat.shape[0]
2973
2974            info = pd.DataFrame(
2975                {"feature": list(tmp_dat.columns), "pct": list(counts / total_count)}
2976            )
2977
2978            del tmp_dat
2979
2980            drop_col = info["feature"][info["pct"] <= min_pct]
2981
2982            if len(drop_col) + 1 == len(choose.columns):
2983                drop_col = info["feature"][info["pct"] == 0]
2984
2985            del info
2986
2987            choose = choose.drop(list(drop_col), axis=1)
2988
2989            results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_proc)(
2990                delayed(stat_calc)(choose, feature)
2991                for feature in tqdm(choose.columns[choose.columns != "DEG"])
2992            )
2993
2994            df = pd.DataFrame(results)
2995            df = df[(df["avg_valid"] > 0) | (df["avg_ctrl"] > 0)]
2996
2997            df["valid_group"] = str(valid_group)
2998            df.sort_values(by="p_val", inplace=True)
2999
3000            num_tests = len(df)
3001            df["adj_pval"] = np.minimum(
3002                1, (df["p_val"] * num_tests) / np.arange(1, num_tests + 1)
3003            )
3004
3005            valid_factor = safe_min_half(df["avg_valid"])
3006            ctrl_factor = safe_min_half(df["avg_ctrl"])
3007
3008            cv_factor = min(valid_factor, ctrl_factor)
3009
3010            if cv_factor == 0:
3011                cv_factor = max(valid_factor, ctrl_factor)
3012
3013            if not np.isfinite(cv_factor) or cv_factor == 0:
3014                cv_factor += offset
3015
3016            valid = df["avg_valid"].where(
3017                df["avg_valid"] != 0, df["avg_valid"] + cv_factor
3018            )
3019            ctrl = df["avg_ctrl"].where(df["avg_ctrl"] != 0, df["avg_ctrl"] + cv_factor)
3020
3021            df["FC"] = valid / ctrl
3022
3023            df["log(FC)"] = np.log2(df["FC"])
3024            df["norm_diff"] = df["avg_valid"] - df["avg_ctrl"]
3025
3026            return df
3027
3028        choose = self.normalized_data.copy().T
3029
3030        final_results = []
3031
3032        if isinstance(cells, list) and sets is None:
3033            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing selected cells to the whole set...")
3034            choose.index = (
3035                self.input_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3036            )
3037
3038            if "#" not in cells[0]:
3039                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3040
3041                print(
3042                    "Not include the set info (name # set) in the 'cells' list. "
3043                    "Only the names will be compared, without considering the set information."
3044                )
3045
3046            labels = ["target" if idx in cells else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3047            valid = list(
3048                set(choose.index[[i for i, x in enumerate(labels) if x == "target"]])
3049            )
3050
3051            choose["DEG"] = labels
3052            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3053
3054            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3055                choose.reset_index(drop=True),
3056                valid_group=valid,
3057                min_exp=min_exp,
3058                min_pct=min_pct,
3059                n_proc=n_proc,
3060            )
3061            return {"valid_cells": valid, "control_cells": "rest", "DEG": result_df}
3062
3063        elif cells == "All" and sets is None:
3064            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing each type of cell to others...")
3065
3066            if with_sets_names:
3067                choose.index = (
3068                    self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3069                    + " # "
3070                    + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3071                )
3072            else:
3073                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3074
3075            unique_labels = set(choose.index)
3076
3077            for label in tqdm(unique_labels):
3078                print(f"\nCalculating statistics for {label}")
3079                labels = ["target" if idx == label else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3080                choose["DEG"] = labels
3081                choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3082                result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3083                    choose.copy(),
3084                    valid_group=label,
3085                    min_exp=min_exp,
3086                    min_pct=min_pct,
3087                    n_proc=n_proc,
3088                )
3089                final_results.append(result_df)
3090
3091            return pd.concat(final_results, ignore_index=True)
3092
3093        elif cells is None and sets == "All":
3094            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing each set/group to others...")
3095            choose.index = self.input_metadata["sets"]
3096            unique_sets = set(choose.index)
3097
3098            for label in tqdm(unique_sets):
3099                print(f"\nCalculating statistics for {label}")
3100                labels = ["target" if idx == label else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3101
3102                choose["DEG"] = labels
3103                choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3104                result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3105                    choose.copy(),
3106                    valid_group=label,
3107                    min_exp=min_exp,
3108                    min_pct=min_pct,
3109                    n_proc=n_proc,
3110                )
3111                final_results.append(result_df)
3112
3113            return pd.concat(final_results, ignore_index=True)
3114
3115        elif cells is None and isinstance(sets, dict):
3116            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing groups...")
3117
3118            choose.index = self.input_metadata["sets"]
3119
3120            group_list = list(sets.keys())
3121            if len(group_list) != 2:
3122                print("Only pairwise group comparison is supported.")
3123                return None
3124
3125            labels = [
3126                (
3127                    "target"
3128                    if idx in sets[group_list[0]]
3129                    else "rest" if idx in sets[group_list[1]] else "drop"
3130                )
3131                for idx in choose.index
3132            ]
3133            choose["DEG"] = labels
3134            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3135
3136            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3137                choose.reset_index(drop=True),
3138                valid_group=group_list[0],
3139                min_exp=min_exp,
3140                min_pct=min_pct,
3141                n_proc=n_proc,
3142            )
3143            return result_df
3144
3145        elif isinstance(cells, dict) and sets is None:
3146            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing groups...")
3147            choose.index = (
3148                self.input_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3149            )
3150
3151            if "#" not in cells[list(cells.keys())[0]][0]:
3152                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3153
3154                print(
3155                    "Not include the set info (name # set) in the 'cells' dict. "
3156                    "Only the names will be compared, without considering the set information."
3157                )
3158
3159            group_list = list(cells.keys())
3160            if len(group_list) != 2:
3161                print("Only pairwise group comparison is supported.")
3162                return None
3163
3164            labels = [
3165                (
3166                    "target"
3167                    if idx in cells[group_list[0]]
3168                    else "rest" if idx in cells[group_list[1]] else "drop"
3169                )
3170                for idx in choose.index
3171            ]
3172
3173            choose["DEG"] = labels
3174            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3175
3176            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3177                choose.reset_index(drop=True),
3178                valid_group=group_list[0],
3179                min_exp=min_exp,
3180                min_pct=min_pct,
3181                n_proc=n_proc,
3182            )
3183
3184            return result_df.reset_index(drop=True)
3185
3186        else:
3187            raise ValueError(
3188                "You must specify either 'cells' or 'sets' (or both). None were provided, which is not allowed for this analysis."
3189            )
3190
3191    def calculate_difference_markers(
3192        self, min_exp=0, min_pct=0.25, n_proc=10, force: bool = False
3193    ):
3194        """
3195        Compute differential markers (var_data) if not already present.
3196
3197        Parameters
3198        ----------
3199        min_exp : float, default 0
3200            Minimum expression threshold passed to `statistic`.
3201
3202        min_pct : float, default 0.25
3203            Minimum percent expressed in target group.
3204
3205        n_proc : int, default 10
3206            Parallel jobs.
3207
3208        force : bool, default False
3209            If True, recompute even if `self.var_data` is present.
3210
3211        Update
3212        -------
3213        Sets `self.var_data` to the result of `self.statistic(...)`.
3214
3215        Raise
3216        ------
3217        ValueError if already computed and `force` is False.
3218        """
3219
3220        if self.var_data is None or force:
3221
3222            self.var_data = self.statistic(
3223                cells="All", sets=None, min_exp=min_exp, min_pct=min_pct, n_proc=n_proc
3224            )
3225
3226        else:
3227            raise ValueError(
3228                "self.calculate_difference_markers() has already been executed. "
3229                "The results are stored in self.var. "
3230                "If you want to recalculate with different statistics, please rerun the method with force=True."
3231            )
3232
3233    def clustering_features(
3234        self,
3235        features_list: list | None,
3236        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
3237        p_val: float = 0.05,
3238        top_n: int = 25,
3239        adj_mean: bool = True,
3240        beta: float = 0.2,
3241    ):
3242        """
3243        Prepare clustering input by selecting marker features and optionally smoothing cell values
3244        toward group means.
3245
3246        Parameters
3247        ----------
3248        features_list : list or None
3249            If provided, use this list of features. If None, features are selected
3250            from `self.var_data` (adj_pval <= p_val, positive logFC) picking `top_n` per group.
3251
3252        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
3253            Metadata column used for naming.
3254
3255        p_val : float, default 0.05
3256            Adjusted p-value cutoff when selecting features automatically.
3257
3258        top_n : int, default 25
3259            Number of top features per valid group to keep if `features_list` is None.
3260
3261        adj_mean : bool, default True
3262            If True, adjust cell values toward group means using `beta`.
3263
3264        beta : float, default 0.2
3265            Adjustment strength toward group mean.
3266
3267        Update
3268        ------
3269        Sets `self.clustering_data` and `self.clustering_metadata` to the selected subset,
3270        ready for PCA/UMAP/clustering.
3271        """
3272
3273        if features_list is None or len(features_list) == 0:
3274
3275            if self.var_data is None:
3276                raise ValueError(
3277                    "Lack of 'self.var_data'. Use self.calculate_difference_markers() method first."
3278                )
3279
3280            df_tmp = self.var_data[self.var_data["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
3281            df_tmp = df_tmp[df_tmp["log(FC)"] > 0]
3282            df_tmp = (
3283                df_tmp.sort_values(
3284                    ["valid_group", "esm", "log(FC)"], ascending=[True, False, False]
3285                )
3286                .groupby("valid_group")
3287                .head(top_n)
3288            )
3289
3290            feaures_list = list(set(df_tmp["feature"]))
3291
3292        data = self.get_partial_data(
3293            names=None, features=feaures_list, name_slot=name_slot
3294        )
3295        data_avg = average(data)
3296
3297        if adj_mean:
3298            data = adjust_cells_to_group_mean(data=data, data_avg=data_avg, beta=beta)
3299
3300        self.clustering_data = data
3301
3302        self.clustering_metadata = self.input_metadata
3303
3304    def average(self):
3305        """
3306        Aggregate normalized data by (cell_name, set) pairs computing the mean per group.
3307
3308        The method constructs new column names as "cell_name # set", averages columns
3309        sharing identical labels, and populates `self.agg_normalized_data` and `self.agg_metadata`.
3310
3311        Update
3312        ------
3313        Sets `self.agg_normalized_data` (features x aggregated samples) and
3314        `self.agg_metadata` (DataFrame with 'cell_names' and 'sets').
3315        """
3316
3317        wide_data = self.normalized_data
3318
3319        wide_metadata = self.input_metadata
3320
3321        new_names = wide_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + wide_metadata["sets"]
3322
3323        wide_data.columns = list(new_names)
3324
3325        aggregated_df = wide_data.T.groupby(level=0).mean().T
3326
3327        sets = [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in aggregated_df.columns]
3328        names = [re.sub(" #.*", "", x) for x in aggregated_df.columns]
3329
3330        aggregated_df.columns = names
3331        aggregated_metadata = pd.DataFrame({"cell_names": names, "sets": sets})
3332
3333        self.agg_metadata = aggregated_metadata
3334        self.agg_normalized_data = aggregated_df
3335
3336    def estimating_similarity(
3337        self, method="pearson", p_val: float = 0.05, top_n: int = 25
3338    ):
3339        """
3340        Estimate pairwise similarity and Euclidean distance between aggregated samples.
3341
3342        Parameters
3343        ----------
3344        method : str, default 'pearson'
3345            Correlation method to use (passed to pandas.DataFrame.corr()).
3346
3347        p_val : float, default 0.05
3348            Adjusted p-value cutoff used to select marker features from `self.var_data`.
3349
3350        top_n : int, default 25
3351            Number of top features per valid group to include.
3352
3353        Update
3354        -------
3355        Computes a combined table with per-pair correlation and euclidean distance
3356        and stores it in `self.similarity`.
3357        """
3358
3359        if self.var_data is None:
3360            raise ValueError(
3361                "Lack of 'self.var_data'. Use self.calculate_difference_markers() method first."
3362            )
3363
3364        self.average()
3365        metadata = self.agg_metadata
3366        data = self.agg_normalized_data
3367
3368        df_tmp = self.var_data[self.var_data["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
3369        df_tmp = df_tmp[df_tmp["log(FC)"] > 0]
3370        df_tmp = (
3371            df_tmp.sort_values(
3372                ["valid_group", "esm", "log(FC)"], ascending=[True, False, False]
3373            )
3374            .groupby("valid_group")
3375            .head(top_n)
3376        )
3377
3378        data = data.loc[list(set(df_tmp["feature"]))]
3379
3380        if len(set(metadata["sets"])) > 1:
3381            data.columns = data.columns + " # " + [x for x in metadata["sets"]]
3382        else:
3383            data = data.copy()
3384
3385        scaler = StandardScaler()
3386
3387        scaled_data = scaler.fit_transform(data)
3388
3389        scaled_df = pd.DataFrame(scaled_data, columns=data.columns)
3390
3391        cor = scaled_df.corr(method=method)
3392        cor_df = cor.stack().reset_index()
3393        cor_df.columns = ["cell1", "cell2", "correlation"]
3394
3395        distances = pdist(scaled_df.T, metric="euclidean")
3396        dist_mat = pd.DataFrame(
3397            squareform(distances), index=scaled_df.columns, columns=scaled_df.columns
3398        )
3399        dist_df = dist_mat.stack().reset_index()
3400        dist_df.columns = ["cell1", "cell2", "euclidean_dist"]
3401
3402        full = pd.merge(cor_df, dist_df, on=["cell1", "cell2"])
3403
3404        full = full[full["cell1"] != full["cell2"]]
3405        full = full.reset_index(drop=True)
3406
3407        self.similarity = full
3408
3409    def similarity_plot(
3410        self,
3411        split_sets=True,
3412        set_info: bool = True,
3413        cmap="seismic",
3414        width=12,
3415        height=10,
3416    ):
3417        """
3418        Visualize similarity as a dot plot.
3419
3420        Parameters
3421        ----------
3422        split_sets : bool, default True
3423            If True and set information is present, split plotting area roughly into two halves to visualize cross-set pairs.
3424
3425        set_info : bool, default True
3426            If True, keep the ' # set' annotation in labels; otherwise strip it.
3427
3428        cmap : str, default 'seismic'
3429            Color map for correlation (hue).
3430
3431        width : int, default 12
3432            Figure width.
3433
3434        height : int, default 10
3435            Figure height.
3436
3437        Returns
3438        -------
3439        matplotlib.figure.Figure
3440
3441        Raises
3442        ------
3443        ValueError
3444            If `self.similarity` is None.
3445
3446        Notes
3447        -----
3448        The function filters pairs by z-scored euclidean distance > 0 to focus on closer pairs.
3449        """
3450
3451        if self.similarity is None:
3452            raise ValueError(
3453                "Similarity data is missing. Please calculate similarity using self.estimating_similarity."
3454            )
3455
3456        similarity_data = self.similarity
3457
3458        if " # " in similarity_data["cell1"][0]:
3459            similarity_data["set1"] = [
3460                re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell1"]
3461            ]
3462            similarity_data["set2"] = [
3463                re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell2"]
3464            ]
3465
3466        if split_sets and " # " in similarity_data["cell1"][0]:
3467            sets = list(
3468                set(list(similarity_data["set1"]) + list(similarity_data["set2"]))
3469            )
3470
3471            mm = math.ceil(len(sets) / 2)
3472
3473            x_s = sets[0:mm]
3474            y_s = sets[mm : len(sets)]
3475
3476            similarity_data = similarity_data[similarity_data["set1"].isin(x_s)]
3477            similarity_data = similarity_data[similarity_data["set2"].isin(y_s)]
3478
3479            similarity_data = similarity_data.sort_values(["set1", "set2"])
3480
3481        if set_info is False and " # " in similarity_data["cell1"][0]:
3482            similarity_data["cell1"] = [
3483                re.sub(" #.*", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell1"]
3484            ]
3485            similarity_data["cell2"] = [
3486                re.sub(" #.*", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell2"]
3487            ]
3488
3489        similarity_data["-euclidean_zscore"] = -zscore(
3490            similarity_data["euclidean_dist"]
3491        )
3492
3493        similarity_data = similarity_data[similarity_data["-euclidean_zscore"] > 0]
3494
3495        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
3496        sns.scatterplot(
3497            data=similarity_data,
3498            x="cell1",
3499            y="cell2",
3500            hue="correlation",
3501            size="-euclidean_zscore",
3502            sizes=(1, 100),
3503            palette=cmap,
3504            alpha=1,
3505            edgecolor="black",
3506        )
3507
3508        plt.xticks(rotation=90)
3509        plt.yticks(rotation=0)
3510        plt.xlabel("Cell 1")
3511        plt.ylabel("Cell 2")
3512        plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc="upper left")
3513
3514        plt.grid(True, alpha=0.6)
3515
3516        plt.tight_layout()
3517
3518        return fig

3520    def spatial_similarity(
3521        self,
3522        set_info: bool = True,
3523        bandwidth=1,
3524        n_neighbors=5,
3525        min_dist=0.1,
3526        legend_split=2,
3527        point_size=200,
3528        spread=1.0,
3529        set_op_mix_ratio=1.0,
3530        local_connectivity=1,
3531        repulsion_strength=1.0,
3532        negative_sample_rate=5,
3533        threshold=0.1,
3534        size_sort: bool = True,
3535        width=12,
3536        height=10,
3537    ):
3538        """
3539        Create a spatial UMAP-like visualization of similarity relationships between samples.
3540
3541        Parameters
3542        ----------
3543        set_info : bool, default True
3544            If True, retain set information in labels.
3545
3546        bandwidth : float, default 1
3547            Bandwidth used by MeanShift for clustering polygons.
3548
3549        point_size : float, default 200
3550            Size of scatter points.
3551
3552        legend_split : int, default 2
3553            Number of columns in legend.
3554
3555        n_neighbors, min_dist, spread, set_op_mix_ratio, local_connectivity, repulsion_strength, negative_sample_rate : parameters passed to UMAP.
3556
3557        threshold : float, default 0.1
3558            Minimum text distance for label adjustment to avoid overlap.
3559
3560        size_sort : bool, default=True
3561            If True, cluster names are sorted in descending order by cluster size.
3562             If False, cluster names follow the order of their first appearance in `names_slot`.
3563
3564        width : int, default 12
3565            Figure width.
3566
3567        height : int, default 10
3568            Figure height.
3569
3570        Returns
3571        -------
3572        matplotlib.figure.Figure
3573
3574        Raises
3575        ------
3576        ValueError
3577            If `self.similarity` is None.
3578
3579        Notes
3580        -----
3581        Builds a precomputed distance matrix combining correlation and euclidean distance,
3582        runs UMAP with metric='precomputed', then overlays cluster hulls (MeanShift + convex hull)
3583        and arrows to indicate nearest neighbors (minimal combined distance).
3584        """
3585
3586        if self.similarity is None:
3587            raise ValueError(
3588                "Similarity data is missing. Please calculate similarity using self.estimating_similarity."
3589            )
3590
3591        similarity_data = self.similarity
3592
3593        sim = similarity_data["correlation"]
3594        sim_scaled = (sim - sim.min()) / (sim.max() - sim.min())
3595        eu_dist = similarity_data["euclidean_dist"]
3596        eu_dist_scaled = (eu_dist - eu_dist.min()) / (eu_dist.max() - eu_dist.min())
3597
3598        similarity_data["combo_dist"] = (1 - sim_scaled) * eu_dist_scaled
3599
3600        # for nn target
3601        arrow_df = similarity_data.copy()
3602        arrow_df = similarity_data.loc[
3603            similarity_data.groupby("cell1")["combo_dist"].idxmin()
3604        ]
3605
3606        cells = sorted(set(similarity_data["cell1"]) | set(similarity_data["cell2"]))
3607        combo_matrix = pd.DataFrame(0, index=cells, columns=cells, dtype=float)
3608
3609        for _, row in similarity_data.iterrows():
3610            combo_matrix.loc[row["cell1"], row["cell2"]] = row["combo_dist"]
3611            combo_matrix.loc[row["cell2"], row["cell1"]] = row["combo_dist"]
3612
3613        tmp_data = self.input_metadata.copy()
3614
3615        tmp_data["tmp_nam"] = list(tmp_data["cell_names"] + " # " + tmp_data["sets"])
3616
3617        tmp_data["count"] = tmp_data["tmp_nam"].map(tmp_data["tmp_nam"].value_counts())
3618
3619        tmp_data = pd.DataFrame(tmp_data[["count", "tmp_nam"]].copy()).drop_duplicates()
3620
3621        queue = pd.unique(tmp_data["tmp_nam"])
3622
3623        tmp_data["tmp_nam"] = pd.Categorical(
3624            tmp_data["tmp_nam"], categories=queue, ordered=True
3625        )
3626
3627        if size_sort:
3628            tmp_data = tmp_data.sort_values("count", ascending=False).reset_index(
3629                drop=True
3630            )
3631            tmp_data["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(tmp_data["count"])[0]
3632
3633        else:
3634
3635            tmp_data = tmp_data.sort_values("tmp_nam").reset_index(drop=True)
3636            tmp_data["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(tmp_data["tmp_nam"])[0]
3637
3638        umap_model = umap.UMAP(
3639            n_components=2,
3640            metric="precomputed",
3641            n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
3642            min_dist=min_dist,
3643            spread=spread,
3644            set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
3645            local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
3646            repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
3647            negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
3648            transform_seed=42,
3649            init="spectral",
3650            random_state=42,
3651            verbose=True,
3652        )
3653
3654        coords = pd.DataFrame(umap_model.fit_transform(combo_matrix.values))
3655        coords.index = list(combo_matrix.index)
3656        coords = np.array(coords.loc[tmp_data["tmp_nam"].values, :])
3657
3658        cell_names = list(tmp_data["tmp_nam"].values)
3659        num_cells = len(cell_names)
3660        palette = sns.color_palette("tab20c", num_cells)
3661
3662        if "#" in cell_names[0]:
3663            avsets = set(
3664                [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell1"]]
3665                + [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell2"]]
3666            )
3667            num_sets = len(avsets)
3668            color_indices = [i * len(palette) // num_sets for i in range(num_sets)]
3669            color_mapping_sets = {
3670                set_name: palette[i] for i, set_name in zip(color_indices, avsets)
3671            }
3672            color_mapping = {
3673                name: color_mapping_sets[re.sub(".*# ", "", name)]
3674                for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)
3675            }
3676        else:
3677            color_mapping = {name: palette[i] for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)}
3678
3679        meanshift = MeanShift(bandwidth=bandwidth)
3680        labels = meanshift.fit_predict(coords)
3681
3682        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
3683        ax = plt.gca()
3684
3685        unique_labels = set(labels)
3686        cluster_palette = sns.color_palette("hls", len(unique_labels))
3687
3688        for label in unique_labels:
3689            if label == -1:
3690                continue
3691            cluster_coords = coords[labels == label]
3692            if len(cluster_coords) < 3:
3693                continue
3694
3695            hull = ConvexHull(cluster_coords)
3696            hull_points = cluster_coords[hull.vertices]
3697
3698            centroid = np.mean(hull_points, axis=0)
3699            expanded = hull_points + 0.05 * (hull_points - centroid)
3700
3701            poly = Polygon(
3702                expanded,
3703                closed=True,
3704                facecolor=cluster_palette[label],
3705                edgecolor="none",
3706                alpha=0.2,
3707                zorder=1,
3708            )
3709            ax.add_patch(poly)
3710
3711        texts = []
3712        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(coords):
3713            plt.scatter(
3714                x,
3715                y,
3716                s=point_size,
3717                color=color_mapping[cell_names[i]],
3718                edgecolors="black",
3719                linewidths=0.5,
3720                zorder=2,
3721            )
3722            texts.append(
3723                ax.text(
3724                    x, y, str(i), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8, color="black"
3725                )
3726            )
3727
3728        def dist(p1, p2):
3729            return np.sqrt((p1[0] - p2[0]) ** 2 + (p1[1] - p2[1]) ** 2)
3730
3731        texts_to_adjust = []
3732        for i, t1 in enumerate(texts):
3733            for j, t2 in enumerate(texts):
3734                if i >= j:
3735                    continue
3736                d = dist(
3737                    (t1.get_position()[0], t1.get_position()[1]),
3738                    (t2.get_position()[0], t2.get_position()[1]),
3739                )
3740                if d < threshold:
3741                    if t1 not in texts_to_adjust:
3742                        texts_to_adjust.append(t1)
3743                    if t2 not in texts_to_adjust:
3744                        texts_to_adjust.append(t2)
3745
3746        adjust_text(
3747            texts_to_adjust,
3748            expand_text=(1.0, 1.0),
3749            force_text=0.9,
3750            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", lw=0.1),
3751            ax=ax,
3752        )
3753
3754        for _, row in arrow_df.iterrows():
3755            try:
3756                idx1 = cell_names.index(row["cell1"])
3757                idx2 = cell_names.index(row["cell2"])
3758            except ValueError:
3759                continue
3760            x1, y1 = coords[idx1]
3761            x2, y2 = coords[idx2]
3762            arrow = FancyArrowPatch(
3763                (x1, y1),
3764                (x2, y2),
3765                arrowstyle="->",
3766                color="gray",
3767                linewidth=1.5,
3768                alpha=0.5,
3769                mutation_scale=12,
3770                zorder=0,
3771            )
3772            ax.add_patch(arrow)
3773
3774        set_names = set([re.sub(r".*# ", "", x) for x in cell_names])
3775
3776        sets = []
3777        for ic in set_names:
3778            sets.append([x for x in cell_names if ic in x][0])
3779
3780        legend_elements = [
3781            Patch(
3782                facecolor=color_mapping[name],
3783                edgecolor="black",
3784                label=f"{i} – {re.sub(' #.*', '', name)}",
3785            )
3786            for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)
3787        ]
3788
3789        if set_info is True and len(sets) > 1:
3790
3791            for ds in sets:
3792                proxy_marker = Line2D(
3793                    [0],
3794                    [0],
3795                    marker="o",
3796                    color="w",
3797                    markersize=12,
3798                    markerfacecolor=color_mapping[ds],
3799                    markeredgecolor="black",
3800                    linestyle="None",
3801                    label=f"Data: {re.sub(r'.*# ', '', ds)}",
3802                )
3803                legend_elements.append(proxy_marker)
3804
3805        plt.legend(
3806            handles=legend_elements,
3807            title="",
3808            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
3809            loc="upper left",
3810            ncol=legend_split,
3811        )
3812
3813        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
3814        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
3815        plt.grid(False)
3816        plt.show()
3817
3818        return fig

3822    def subcluster_prepare(self, features: list, cluster: str):
3823        """
3824        Prepare a `Clustering` object for subcluster analysis on a selected parent cluster.
3825
3826        Parameters
3827        ----------
3828        features : list
3829            Features to include for subcluster analysis.
3830
3831        cluster : str
3832            Parent cluster name (used to select matching cells).
3833
3834        Update
3835        ------
3836        Initializes `self.subclusters_` as a new `Clustering` instance containing the
3837        reduced data for the given cluster and stores `current_features` and `current_cluster`.
3838        """
3839
3840        dat = self.normalized_data
3841        dat.columns = list(self.input_metadata["cell_names"])
3842
3843        dat = reduce_data(self.normalized_data, features=features, names=[cluster])
3844
3845        self.subclusters_ = Clustering(data=dat, metadata=None)
3846
3847        self.subclusters_.current_features = features
3848        self.subclusters_.current_cluster = cluster

3850    def define_subclusters(
3851        self,
3852        umap_num: int = 2,
3853        eps: float = 0.5,
3854        min_samples: int = 10,
3855        n_neighbors: int = 5,
3856        min_dist: float = 0.1,
3857        spread: float = 1.0,
3858        set_op_mix_ratio: float = 1.0,
3859        local_connectivity: int = 1,
3860        repulsion_strength: float = 1.0,
3861        negative_sample_rate: int = 5,
3862        width=8,
3863        height=6,
3864    ):
3865        """
3866        Compute UMAP and DBSCAN clustering within a previously prepared subcluster dataset.
3867
3868        Parameters
3869        ----------
3870        umap_num : int, default 2
3871            Number of UMAP dimensions to compute.
3872
3873        eps : float, default 0.5
3874            DBSCAN eps parameter.
3875
3876        min_samples : int, default 10
3877            DBSCAN min_samples parameter.
3878
3879        n_neighbors, min_dist, spread, set_op_mix_ratio, local_connectivity, repulsion_strength, negative_sample_rate, width, height :
3880            Additional parameters passed to UMAP / plotting / MeanShift as appropriate.
3881
3882        Update
3883        -------
3884        Stores cluster labels in `self.subclusters_.subclusters`.
3885
3886        Raises
3887        ------
3888        RuntimeError
3889            If `self.subclusters_` has not been prepared.
3890        """
3891
3892        if self.subclusters_ is None:
3893            raise RuntimeError(
3894                "Nothing to return. 'self.subcluster_prepare' was not conducted!"
3895            )
3896
3897        self.subclusters_.perform_UMAP(
3898            factorize=False,
3899            umap_num=umap_num,
3900            pc_num=0,
3901            harmonized=False,
3902            n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
3903            min_dist=min_dist,
3904            spread=spread,
3905            set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
3906            local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
3907            repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
3908            negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
3909            width=width,
3910            height=height,
3911        )
3912
3913        fig = self.subclusters_.find_clusters_UMAP(
3914            umap_n=umap_num,
3915            eps=eps,
3916            min_samples=min_samples,
3917            width=width,
3918            height=height,
3919        )
3920
3921        clusters = self.subclusters_.return_clusters(clusters="umap")
3922
3923        self.subclusters_.subclusters = [str(x) for x in list(clusters)]
3924
3925        return fig

4033    def subcluster_DEG_dot(
4034        self,
4035        top_n=3,
4036        min_exp=0,
4037        min_pct=0.25,
4038        p_val=0.05,
4039        colors="viridis",
4040        hclust="complete",
4041        scale=False,
4042        scale_axis: Literal["x", "y"] = "y",
4043        img_width=3,
4044        img_high=5,
4045        label_size=6,
4046        size_scale=70,
4047        y_lab="Genes",
4048        legend_lab="normalized",
4049        bbox_to_anchor_scale: int = 25,
4050        bbox_to_anchor_perc: tuple = (0.91, 0.63),
4051        n_proc=10,
4052    ):
4053        """
4054        Plot top differential features (DEGs) for subclusters as a features-dot.
4055
4056        Parameters
4057        ----------
4058        top_n : int, default 3
4059            Number of top features per subcluster to show.
4060
4061        min_exp : float, default 0
4062            Minimum expression threshold passed to `statistic`.
4063
4064        min_pct : float, default 0.25
4065            Minimum percent expressed in target group.
4066
4067        p_val: float, default 0.05
4068            Maximum p-value for visualizing features.
4069
4070        n_proc : int, default 10
4071            Parallel jobs used for DEG calculation.
4072
4073        scale: bool, default False
4074            If True, expression_data will be scaled (0–1) across the rows (features).
4075
4076        scale_axis : {'x', 'y'}, default 'y'
4077            The axis along which to scale the expression data to the [0, 1] range:
4078            - 'y': Scales across columns (per sample / cell).
4079            - 'x': Scales across rows (per feature / gene).
4080            Only effective if `scale=True`.
4081
4082        colors : str, default='viridis'
4083            Colormap for expression values.
4084
4085        hclust : str or None, default='complete'
4086            Linkage method for hierarchical clustering. If None, no clustering
4087            is performed.
4088
4089        img_width : int or float, default=8
4090            Width of the plot in inches.
4091
4092        img_high : int or float, default=5
4093            Height of the plot in inches.
4094
4095        label_size : int, default=10
4096            Font size for axis labels and ticks.
4097
4098        size_scale : int or float, default=100
4099            Scaling factor for bubble sizes.
4100
4101        y_lab : str, default='Genes'
4102            Label for the x-axis.
4103
4104        legend_lab : str, default='normalized'
4105            Label for the colorbar legend.
4106
4107        bbox_to_anchor_scale : int, default=25
4108            Vertical scale (percentage) for positioning the colorbar.
4109
4110        bbox_to_anchor_perc : tuple, default=(0.91, 0.63)
4111            Anchor position for the size legend (percent bubble legend).
4112
4113        Returns
4114        -------
4115        matplotlib.figure.Figure
4116
4117        Raises
4118        ------
4119        RuntimeError
4120            If subcluster preparation/definition has not been run.
4121
4122        Notes
4123        -----
4124        Internally calls `calc_DEG` (or equivalent) to obtain statistics, filters
4125        by p-value and effect-size, selects top features per valid group and plots them.
4126        """
4127
4128        if self.subclusters_ is None or self.subclusters_.subclusters is None:
4129            raise RuntimeError(
4130                "Nothing to return. 'self.subcluster_prepare' -> 'self.define_subclusters' pip was not conducted!"
4131            )
4132
4133        dat = self.normalized_data
4134        dat.columns = list(self.input_metadata["cell_names"])
4135
4136        dat = reduce_data(
4137            self.normalized_data, names=[self.subclusters_.current_cluster]
4138        )
4139
4140        dat.columns = self.subclusters_.subclusters
4141
4142        deg_stats = calc_DEG(
4143            dat,
4144            metadata_list=None,
4145            entities="All",
4146            sets=None,
4147            min_exp=min_exp,
4148            min_pct=min_pct,
4149            n_proc=n_proc,
4150        )
4151
4152        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["p_val"] <= p_val]
4153        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["log(FC)"] > 0]
4154
4155        deg_stats = (
4156            deg_stats.sort_values(
4157                ["valid_group", "esm", "log(FC)"], ascending=[True, False, False]
4158            )
4159            .groupby("valid_group")
4160            .head(top_n)
4161        )
4162
4163        dat = reduce_data(dat, features=list(set(deg_stats["feature"])))
4164
4165        avg = average(dat)
4166        occ = occurrence(dat)
4167
4168        scatter = features_dot(
4169            expression_data=avg,
4170            occurence_data=occ,
4171            features=None,
4172            metadata_list=None,
4173            scale_axis=scale_axis,
4174            scale=scale,
4175            colors=colors,
4176            hclust=hclust,
4177            img_width=img_width,
4178            img_high=img_high,
4179            label_size=label_size,
4180            size_scale=size_scale,
4181            y_lab=y_lab,
4182            legend_lab=legend_lab,
4183            bbox_to_anchor_scale=bbox_to_anchor_scale,
4184            bbox_to_anchor_perc=bbox_to_anchor_perc,
4185        )
4186
4187        return scatter

4189    def accept_subclusters(self):
4190        """
4191        Commit subcluster labels into the main `input_metadata` by renaming cell names.
4192
4193        The method replaces occurrences of the parent cluster name in `self.input_metadata['cell_names']`
4194        with the expanded names that include subcluster suffixes (via `add_subnames`),
4195        then clears `self.subclusters_`.
4196
4197        Update
4198        ------
4199        Modifies `self.input_metadata['cell_names']`.
4200
4201        Resets `self.subclusters_` to None.
4202
4203        Raises
4204        ------
4205        RuntimeError
4206            If `self.subclusters_` is not defined or subclusters were not computed.
4207        """
4208
4209        if self.subclusters_ is None or self.subclusters_.subclusters is None:
4210            raise RuntimeError(
4211                "Nothing to return. 'self.subcluster_prepare' -> 'self.define_subclusters' pip was not conducted!"
4212            )
4213
4214        new_meta = add_subnames(
4215            list(self.input_metadata["cell_names"]),
4216            parent_name=self.subclusters_.current_cluster,
4217            new_clusters=self.subclusters_.subclusters,
4218        )
4219
4220        self.input_metadata["cell_names"] = new_meta
4221
4222        if "clustering_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
4223            self.clustering_metadata["cell_names"] = new_meta
4224
4225        self.subclusters_ = None

4227    def dot_plot(
4228        self,
4229        names: list | None = None,
4230        features: list | None = None,
4231        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
4232        scale=True,
4233        scale_axis: Literal["x", "y"] = "y",
4234        colors="viridis",
4235        hclust=None,
4236        img_width=15,
4237        img_high=1,
4238        label_size=10,
4239        size_scale=200,
4240        y_lab="Genes",
4241        legend_lab="log(CPM + 1)",
4242        set_box_size: float | int = 5,
4243        set_box_high: float | int = 5,
4244        bbox_to_anchor_scale=25,
4245        bbox_to_anchor_perc=(0.90, -0.24),
4246        bbox_to_anchor_group=(1.01, 0.4),
4247    ):
4248        """
4249        Create a dot plot of selected features across samples inside project.
4250
4251        Each point represents a feature-sample pair, where the color encodes the
4252        expression value and the size encodes occurrence or relative abundance.
4253        Optionally, hierarchical clustering can be applied to order rows and columns.
4254
4255        Parameters
4256        ----------
4257        names : list, str, or None
4258            Names of samples to include. If None, all samples are considered.
4259
4260        features : list, str, or None
4261            Names of features to include. If None, all features are considered.
4262
4263        name_slot : str
4264            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
4265
4266        scale: bool, default False
4267            If True, expression_data will be scaled (0–1) across the rows (features).
4268
4269        scale_axis : {'x', 'y'}, default 'y'
4270            The axis along which to scale the expression data to the [0, 1] range:
4271            - 'y': Scales across columns (per sample / cell).
4272            - 'x': Scales across rows (per feature / gene).
4273            Only effective if `scale=True`.
4274
4275        colors : str, default='viridis'
4276            Colormap for expression values.
4277
4278        hclust : str or None, default='complete'
4279            Linkage method for hierarchical clustering. If None, no clustering
4280            is performed.
4281
4282        img_width : int or float, default=8
4283            Width of the plot in inches.
4284
4285        img_high : int or float, default=5
4286            Height of the plot in inches.
4287
4288        label_size : int, default=10
4289            Font size for axis labels and ticks.
4290
4291        size_scale : int or float, default=100
4292            Scaling factor for bubble sizes.
4293
4294        y_lab : str, default='Genes'
4295            Label for the x-axis.
4296
4297        legend_lab : str, default='log(CPM + 1)'
4298            Label for the colorbar legend.
4299
4300        bbox_to_anchor_scale : int, default=25
4301            Vertical scale (percentage) for positioning the colorbar.
4302
4303        bbox_to_anchor_perc : tuple, default=(0.91, 0.63)
4304            Anchor position for the size legend (percent bubble legend).
4305
4306        bbox_to_anchor_group : tuple, default=(1.01, 0.4)
4307            Anchor position for the group legend.
4308
4309        Returns
4310        -------
4311        matplotlib.figure.Figure
4312            The generated dot plot figure.
4313
4314        Notes
4315        -----
4316        Colors represent expression values normalized to the colormap.
4317        """
4318
4319        prtd, met = self.get_partial_data(
4320            names=names, features=features, name_slot=name_slot, inc_metadata=True
4321        )
4322
4323        prtd.columns = prtd.columns + "#" + met["sets"]
4324
4325        prtd_avg = average(prtd)
4326
4327        meta_sets = [re.sub(".*#", "", x) for x in prtd_avg.columns]
4328
4329        prtd_avg.columns = [re.sub("#.*", "", x) for x in prtd_avg.columns]
4330
4331        prtd_occ = occurrence(prtd)
4332
4333        prtd_occ.columns = [re.sub("#.*", "", x) for x in prtd_occ.columns]
4334
4335        fig_scatter = features_dot(
4336            expression_data=prtd_avg,
4337            occurence_data=prtd_occ,
4338            scale=scale,
4339            scale_axis=scale_axis,
4340            features=None,
4341            metadata_list=meta_sets,
4342            colors=colors,
4343            hclust=hclust,
4344            img_width=img_width,
4345            img_high=img_high,
4346            label_size=label_size,
4347            size_scale=size_scale,
4348            y_lab=y_lab,
4349            legend_lab=legend_lab,
4350            set_box_size=set_box_size,
4351            set_box_high=set_box_high,
4352            bbox_to_anchor_scale=bbox_to_anchor_scale,
4353            bbox_to_anchor_perc=bbox_to_anchor_perc,
4354            bbox_to_anchor_group=bbox_to_anchor_group,
4355        )
4356
4357        return fig_scatter
4358
4359    def data_composition(
4360        self,
4361        features_count: list | None,
4362        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
4363        set_sep: bool = True,
4364    ):
4365        """
4366        Compute composition of cell types in data set.
4367
4368        This function counts the occurrences of specific cells (e.g., cell types, subtypes)
4369        within metadata entries, calculates their relative percentages, and stores
4370        the results in `self.composition_data`.
4371
4372        Parameters
4373        ----------
4374        features_count : list or None
4375            List of features (part or full names) to be counted.
4376            If None, all unique elements from the specified `name_slot` metadata field are used.
4377
4378        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
4379            Metadata field containing sample identifiers or labels.
4380
4381        set_sep : bool, default True
4382            If True and multiple sets are present in metadata, compute composition
4383            separately for each set.
4384
4385        Update
4386        -------
4387        Stores results in `self.composition_data` as a pandas DataFrame with:
4388        - 'name': feature name
4389        - 'n': number of occurrences
4390        - 'pct': percentage of occurrences
4391        - 'set' (if applicable): dataset identifier
4392        """
4393
4394        validated_list = list(self.input_metadata[name_slot])
4395        sets = list(self.input_metadata["sets"])
4396
4397        if features_count is None:
4398            features_count = list(set(self.input_metadata[name_slot]))
4399
4400        if set_sep and len(set(sets)) > 1:
4401
4402            final_res = pd.DataFrame()
4403
4404            for s in set(sets):
4405                print(s)
4406
4407                mask = [True if s == x else False for x in sets]
4408
4409                tmp_val_list = np.array(validated_list)
4410
4411                tmp_val_list = list(tmp_val_list[mask])
4412
4413                res_dict = {"name": [], "n": [], "set": []}
4414
4415                for f in tqdm(features_count):
4416                    res_dict["n"].append(
4417                        sum(1 for element in tmp_val_list if f in element)
4418                    )
4419                    res_dict["name"].append(f)
4420                    res_dict["set"].append(s)
4421                    res = pd.DataFrame(res_dict)
4422                    res["pct"] = res["n"] / sum(res["n"]) * 100
4423                    res["pct"] = res["pct"].round(2)
4424
4425                final_res = pd.concat([final_res, res])
4426
4427            res = final_res.sort_values(["set", "pct"], ascending=[True, False])
4428
4429        else:
4430
4431            res_dict = {"name": [], "n": []}
4432
4433            for f in tqdm(features_count):
4434                res_dict["n"].append(
4435                    sum(1 for element in validated_list if f in element)
4436                )
4437                res_dict["name"].append(f)
4438
4439            res = pd.DataFrame(res_dict)
4440            res["pct"] = res["n"] / sum(res["n"]) * 100
4441            res["pct"] = res["pct"].round(2)
4442
4443            res = res.sort_values("pct", ascending=False)
4444
4445        self.composition_data = res
4446
4447    def composition_pie(
4448        self,
4449        width=6,
4450        height=6,
4451        font_size=15,
4452        cmap: str = "tab20",
4453        legend_split_col: int = 1,
4454        offset_labels: float | int = 0.5,
4455        legend_bbox: tuple = (1.15, 0.95),
4456    ):
4457        """
4458        Visualize the composition of cell lineages using pie charts.
4459
4460        Generates pie charts showing the relative proportions of features stored
4461        in `self.composition_data`. If multiple sets are present, a separate
4462        chart is drawn for each set.
4463
4464        Parameters
4465        ----------
4466        width : int, default 6
4467            Width of the figure.
4468
4469        height : int, default 6
4470            Height of the figure (applied per set if multiple sets are plotted).
4471
4472        font_size : int, default 15
4473            Font size for labels and annotations.
4474
4475        cmap : str, default 'tab20'
4476            Colormap used for pie slices.
4477
4478        legend_split_col : int, default 1
4479            Number of columns in the legend.
4480
4481        offset_labels : float or int, default 0.5
4482            Spacing offset for label placement relative to pie slices.
4483
4484        legend_bbox : tuple, default (1.15, 0.95)
4485            Bounding box anchor position for the legend.
4486
4487        Returns
4488        -------
4489        matplotlib.figure.Figure
4490            Pie chart visualization of composition data.
4491        """
4492
4493        df = self.composition_data
4494
4495        if "set" in df.columns and len(set(df["set"])) > 1:
4496
4497            sets = list(set(df["set"]))
4498            fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(sets), 1, figsize=(width, height * len(sets)))
4499
4500            all_wedges = []
4501            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4502
4503            set_nam = len(set(df["name"]))
4504
4505            legend_labels = list(set(df["name"]))
4506
4507            colors = [cmap(i / set_nam) for i in range(set_nam)]
4508
4509            cmap_dict = dict(zip(legend_labels, colors))
4510
4511            for idx, s in enumerate(sets):
4512                ax = axes[idx]
4513                tmp_df = df[df["set"] == s].reset_index(drop=True)
4514
4515                labels = [f"{row['pct']:.1f}%" for _, row in tmp_df.iterrows()]
4516
4517                wedges, _ = ax.pie(
4518                    tmp_df["n"],
4519                    startangle=90,
4520                    labeldistance=1.05,
4521                    colors=[cmap_dict[x] for x in tmp_df["name"]],
4522                    wedgeprops={"linewidth": 0.5, "edgecolor": "black"},
4523                )
4524
4525                all_wedges.extend(wedges)
4526
4527                kw = dict(arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-"), zorder=0, va="center")
4528                n = 0
4529                for i, p in enumerate(wedges):
4530                    ang = (p.theta2 - p.theta1) / 2.0 + p.theta1
4531                    y = np.sin(np.deg2rad(ang))
4532                    x = np.cos(np.deg2rad(ang))
4533                    horizontalalignment = {-1: "right", 1: "left"}[int(np.sign(x))]
4534                    connectionstyle = f"angle,angleA=0,angleB={ang}"
4535                    kw["arrowprops"].update({"connectionstyle": connectionstyle})
4536                    if len(labels[i]) > 0:
4537                        n += offset_labels
4538                        ax.annotate(
4539                            labels[i],
4540                            xy=(x, y),
4541                            xytext=(1.01 * x + (n * x / 4), 1.01 * y + (n * y / 4)),
4542                            horizontalalignment=horizontalalignment,
4543                            fontsize=font_size,
4544                            weight="bold",
4545                            **kw,
4546                        )
4547
4548                circle2 = plt.Circle((0, 0), 0.6, color="white", ec="black")
4549                ax.add_artist(circle2)
4550
4551                ax.text(
4552                    0,
4553                    0,
4554                    f"{s}",
4555                    ha="center",
4556                    va="center",
4557                    fontsize=font_size,
4558                    weight="bold",
4559                )
4560
4561            legend_handles = [
4562                Patch(facecolor=cmap_dict[label], edgecolor="black", label=label)
4563                for label in legend_labels
4564            ]
4565
4566            fig.legend(
4567                handles=legend_handles,
4568                loc="center right",
4569                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4570                ncol=legend_split_col,
4571                title="",
4572            )
4573
4574            plt.tight_layout()
4575            plt.show()
4576
4577        else:
4578
4579            labels = [f"{row['pct']:.1f}%" for _, row in df.iterrows()]
4580
4581            legend_labels = [f"{row['name']}" for _, row in df.iterrows()]
4582
4583            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4584            colors = [cmap(i / len(df)) for i in range(len(df))]
4585
4586            fig, ax = plt.subplots(
4587                figsize=(width, height), subplot_kw=dict(aspect="equal")
4588            )
4589
4590            wedges, _ = ax.pie(
4591                df["n"],
4592                startangle=90,
4593                labeldistance=1.05,
4594                colors=colors,
4595                wedgeprops={"linewidth": 0.5, "edgecolor": "black"},
4596            )
4597
4598            kw = dict(arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-"), zorder=0, va="center")
4599            n = 0
4600            for i, p in enumerate(wedges):
4601                ang = (p.theta2 - p.theta1) / 2.0 + p.theta1
4602                y = np.sin(np.deg2rad(ang))
4603                x = np.cos(np.deg2rad(ang))
4604                horizontalalignment = {-1: "right", 1: "left"}[int(np.sign(x))]
4605                connectionstyle = "angle,angleA=0,angleB={}".format(ang)
4606                kw["arrowprops"].update({"connectionstyle": connectionstyle})
4607                if len(labels[i]) > 0:
4608                    n += offset_labels
4609
4610                    ax.annotate(
4611                        labels[i],
4612                        xy=(x, y),
4613                        xytext=(1.01 * x + (n * x / 4), y * 1.01 + (n * y / 4)),
4614                        horizontalalignment=horizontalalignment,
4615                        fontsize=font_size,
4616                        weight="bold",
4617                        **kw,
4618                    )
4619
4620            circle2 = plt.Circle((0, 0), 0.6, color="white")
4621            circle2.set_edgecolor("black")
4622
4623            p = plt.gcf()
4624            p.gca().add_artist(circle2)
4625
4626            ax.legend(
4627                wedges,
4628                legend_labels,
4629                title="",
4630                loc="center left",
4631                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4632                ncol=legend_split_col,
4633            )
4634
4635            plt.show()
4636
4637        return fig
