4639    def bar_composition(
4640        self,
4641        cmap="tab20b",
4642        width=2,
4643        height=6,
4644        font_size=15,
4645        legend_split_col: int = 1,
4646        legend_bbox: tuple = (1.3, 1),
4647    ):
4648        """
4649        Visualize the composition of cell lineages using bar plots.
4650
4651        Produces bar plots showing the distribution of features stored in
4652        `self.composition_data`. If multiple sets are present, a separate
4653        bar is drawn for each set. Percentages are annotated alongside the bars.
4654
4655        Parameters
4656        ----------
4657        cmap : str, default 'tab20b'
4658            Colormap used for stacked bars.
4659
4660        width : int, default 2
4661            Width of each subplot (per set).
4662
4663        height : int, default 6
4664            Height of the figure.
4665
4666        font_size : int, default 15
4667            Font size for labels and annotations.
4668
4669        legend_split_col : int, default 1
4670            Number of columns in the legend.
4671
4672        legend_bbox : tuple, default (1.3, 1)
4673            Bounding box anchor position for the legend.
4674
4675        Returns
4676        -------
4677        matplotlib.figure.Figure
4678            Stacked bar plot visualization of composition data.
4679        """
4680
4681        df = self.composition_data
4682        df["num"] = range(1, len(df) + 1)
4683
4684        if "set" in df.columns and len(set(df["set"])) > 1:
4685
4686            sets = list(set(df["set"]))
4687            fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(sets), figsize=(width * len(sets), height))
4688
4689            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4690
4691            set_nam = len(set(df["name"]))
4692
4693            legend_labels = list(set(df["name"]))
4694
4695            colors = [cmap(i / set_nam) for i in range(set_nam)]
4696
4697            cmap_dict = dict(zip(legend_labels, colors))
4698
4699            for idx, s in enumerate(sets):
4700                ax = axes[idx]
4701
4702                tmp_df = df[df["set"] == s].reset_index(drop=True)
4703
4704                values = tmp_df["n"].values
4705                total = sum(values)
4706                values = [v / total * 100 for v in values]
4707                values = [round(v, 2) for v in values]
4708
4709                idx_max = np.argmax(values)
4710                correction = 100 - sum(values)
4711                values[idx_max] += correction
4712
4713                names = tmp_df["name"].values
4714                perc = tmp_df["pct"].values
4715                nums = tmp_df["num"].values
4716
4717                bottom = 0
4718                centers = []
4719                for name, num, val, color in zip(names, nums, values, colors):
4720                    ax.bar(s, val, bottom=bottom, color=cmap_dict[name], label=name)
4721                    centers.append(bottom + val / 2)
4722                    bottom += val
4723
4724                y_positions = np.linspace(centers[0], centers[-1], len(centers))
4725                x_text = -0.8
4726
4727                for y_label, y_center, pct, num in zip(
4728                    y_positions, centers, perc, nums
4729                ):
4730                    ax.annotate(
4731                        f"{pct:.1f}%",
4732                        xy=(0, y_center),
4733                        xycoords="data",
4734                        xytext=(x_text, y_label),
4735                        textcoords="data",
4736                        ha="right",
4737                        va="center",
4738                        fontsize=font_size,
4739                        arrowprops=dict(
4740                            arrowstyle="->",
4741                            lw=1,
4742                            color="black",
4743                            connectionstyle="angle3,angleA=0,angleB=90",
4744                        ),
4745                    )
4746
4747                ax.set_ylim(0, 100)
4748                ax.set_xlabel(s, fontsize=font_size)
4749                ax.xaxis.label.set_rotation(30)
4750
4751                ax.set_xticks([])
4752                ax.set_yticks([])
4753                for spine in ax.spines.values():
4754                    spine.set_visible(False)
4755
4756            legend_handles = [
4757                Patch(facecolor=cmap_dict[label], edgecolor="black", label=label)
4758                for label in legend_labels
4759            ]
4760
4761            fig.legend(
4762                handles=legend_handles,
4763                loc="center right",
4764                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4765                ncol=legend_split_col,
4766                title="",
4767            )
4768
4769            plt.tight_layout()
4770            plt.show()
4771
4772        else:
4773
4774            cmap = plt.get_cmap(cmap)
4775
4776            colors = [cmap(i / len(df)) for i in range(len(df))]
4777
4778            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
4779
4780            values = df["n"].values
4781            names = df["name"].values
4782            perc = df["pct"].values
4783            nums = df["num"].values
4784
4785            bottom = 0
4786            centers = []
4787            for name, num, val, color in zip(names, nums, values, colors):
4788                ax.bar(0, val, bottom=bottom, color=color, label=f"{num}) {name}")
4789                centers.append(bottom + val / 2)
4790                bottom += val
4791
4792            y_positions = np.linspace(centers[0], centers[-1], len(centers))
4793            x_text = -0.8
4794
4795            for y_label, y_center, pct, num in zip(y_positions, centers, perc, nums):
4796                ax.annotate(
4797                    f"{num}) {pct}",
4798                    xy=(0, y_center),
4799                    xycoords="data",
4800                    xytext=(x_text, y_label),
4801                    textcoords="data",
4802                    ha="right",
4803                    va="center",
4804                    fontsize=9,
4805                    arrowprops=dict(
4806                        arrowstyle="->",
4807                        lw=1,
4808                        color="black",
4809                        connectionstyle="angle3,angleA=0,angleB=90",
4810                    ),
4811                )
4812
4813            ax.set_xticks([])
4814            ax.set_yticks([])
4815            for spine in ax.spines.values():
4816                spine.set_visible(False)
4817
4818            ax.legend(
4819                title="Legend",
4820                bbox_to_anchor=legend_bbox,
4821                loc="upper left",
4822                ncol=legend_split_col,
4823            )
4824
4825            plt.tight_layout()
4826            plt.show()
4827
4828        return fig

4830    def cell_regression(
4831        self,
4832        cell_x: str,
4833        cell_y: str,
4834        set_x: str | None = None,
4835        set_y: str | None = None,
4836        min_log=0.5,
4837        n_max=20,
4838        min_exp=0.1,
4839        min_pct=0.5,
4840        n_proc=10,
4841        min_esm=0.5,
4842        p_val=0.05,
4843        adj=True,
4844        image_width=12,
4845        image_high=7,
4846    ):
4847        """
4848        Perform linear regression between two selected cell populations and identify
4849        significant and top-ranked differentially expressed genes.
4850
4851        The function compares the expression profiles of two selected cells or cell
4852        populations using linear regression. Each gene is represented as a point in
4853        the regression plot, with expression in `cell_x` on the X-axis and expression
4854        in `cell_y` on the Y-axis.
4855
4856        Differential expression statistics are calculated using `calc_DEG`. Genes are
4857        first filtered according to the minimum absolute log fold change, minimum
4858        absolute effect size (ESM), and statistical significance. Among the
4859        significant genes, up to `n_max` genes are selected within each `valid_group`,
4860        prioritizing genes with the largest standardized absolute regression residuals
4861        and absolute ESM values.
4862
4863        The regression plot uses three point categories:
4864        - gray: genes that are not statistically significant,
4865        - green: statistically significant genes that pass the DEG thresholds,
4866        - blue: top `n_max` genes selected within each `valid_group`.
4867
4868        The selected top genes are additionally annotated with their gene names.
4869        The plot also displays the fitted linear regression line, R-squared,
4870        p-value, and regression equation.
4871
4872        Parameters
4873        ----------
4874        cell_x : str
4875            Name of the first cell or cell population used as the X-axis.
4876
4877        cell_y : str
4878            Name of the second cell or cell population used as the Y-axis.
4879
4880        set_x : str or None
4881            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_x`.
4882            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4883            the cell is selected only by its name.
4884
4885        set_y : str or None
4886            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_y`.
4887            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4888            the cell is selected only by its name.
4889
4890        min_log : float, default=0.5
4891            Minimum absolute log fold change required for a gene to be considered
4892            for significant DEG selection.
4893
4894        n_max : int, default=20
4895            Maximum number of top genes selected from each `valid_group`.
4896            Genes are ranked primarily by standardized absolute regression residual
4897            and secondarily by absolute Effect Size - Cohen's d.
4898
4899        min_exp : float, default=0.1
4900            Minimum expression threshold passed to `calc_DEG`.
4901
4902        min_pct : float, default=0.5
4903            Minimum fraction of cells in which a gene must be expressed, passed to
4904            `calc_DEG`.
4905
4906        n_proc : int, default=10
4907            Number of parallel processes used by `calc_DEG`.
4908
4909        min_esm : float, default=0.5
4910            Minimum absolute ESM (effect size measure) required for DEG selection.
4911
4912        p_val : float, default=0.05
4913            Maximum allowed p-value for statistical significance. If `adj=True`,
4914            this threshold is applied to the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`);
4915            otherwise, it is applied to the raw p-value (`p_val`).
4916
4917        adj : bool, default=True
4918            Whether to use the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`) instead of the raw
4919            p-value (`p_val`) for statistical significance filtering.
4920
4921        image_width : int or float, default=12
4922            Width of the regression plot in inches.
4923
4924        image_high : int or float, default=7
4925            Height of the regression plot in inches.
4926
4927
4928
4929        Returns
4930        -------
4931        deg_stats : pandas.DataFrame
4932            DataFrame containing the DEG statistics after filtering by absolute
4933            log fold change, absolute ESM, and statistical significance.
4934
4935        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
4936            Matplotlib figure containing the regression plot, including expression
4937            points, regression line, regression statistics, and annotations for
4938            the selected top genes.
4939
4940        Raises
4941        ------
4942        ValueError
4943            If `cell_x` or `cell_y` is not found in the dataset.
4944
4945        ValueError
4946            If multiple columns correspond to the same cell name and the required
4947            dataset identifiers (`set_x` and/or `set_y`) were not provided.
4948
4949        Notes
4950        -----
4951        * The function calls `self.average()` before performing the analysis.
4952        * Linear regression is calculated using `scipy.stats.linregress`.
4953        * Regression residuals are calculated as the difference between the observed
4954        Y value and the value predicted by the fitted regression model.
4955        * Standardized residuals are used to prioritize genes that deviate most
4956        strongly from the expected linear relationship.
4957        * Significant genes are filtered using absolute log fold change, absolute
4958        ESM, and either raw or adjusted p-value.
4959        * Top genes are selected separately within each `valid_group`.
4960        * The top genes are annotated on the regression plot.
4961        * The returned `deg_stats` contains the significant genes before the final
4962        `n_max` per-group selection.
4963
4964
4965        Examples
4966        --------
4967        > > > deg_stats, fig = obj.cell_regression(
4968        > > > ...     cell_x="NeuronA",
4969        > > > ...     cell_y="NeuronB",
4970        > > > ...     min_log_min=0.5,
4971        > > > ...     min_esm=0.5,
4972        > > > ...     p_val=0.05,
4973        > > > ...     n_max=20
4974        > > > ... )
4975        > > >
4976        """
4977
4978        self.average()
4979
4980        metadata = self.agg_metadata
4981        data = self.agg_normalized_data
4982        data2 = self.normalized_data
4983        metadata2 = self.input_metadata
4984
4985        if set_x is not None and set_y is not None:
4986            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
4987            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata2["sets"]
4988            cell_x = cell_x + " # " + set_x
4989            cell_y = cell_y + " # " + set_y
4990
4991            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
4992                data2,
4993                metadata_list=None,
4994                entities={
4995                    "cell_x": cell_x + " # " + set_x,
4996                    "cell_y": cell_y + " # " + set_y,
4997                },
4998                sets=None,
4999                min_exp=min_exp,
5000                min_pct=min_pct,
5001                n_proc=n_proc,
5002            )
5003
5004        else:
5005            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5006            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"]
5007
5008            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
5009                data2,
5010                metadata_list=None,
5011                entities={"cell_x": cell_x, "cell_y": cell_y},
5012                sets=None,
5013                min_exp=min_exp,
5014                min_pct=min_pct,
5015                n_proc=n_proc,
5016            )
5017
5018        # points
5019        x = data[cell_x]
5020        y = data[cell_y]
5021
5022        # regression
5023        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(x, y)
5024
5025        # prediction
5026        y_pred = slope * x + intercept
5027
5028        # residuals
5029        residual = y - y_pred
5030
5031        # residuals for DEG
5032        deg_stats["residual"] = deg_stats["feature"].map(residual)
5033        deg_stats["residual_abs"] = deg_stats["residual"].abs()
5034        deg_stats["residual_std"] = deg_stats["residual"] / residual.std()
5035        deg_stats["residual_std_abs"] = deg_stats["residual_std"].abs()
5036        deg_stats["esm_abs"] = deg_stats["esm"].abs()
5037
5038        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["log(FC)"].abs() >= min_log]
5039
5040        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["esm_abs"] >= min_esm]
5041
5042        if adj:
5043
5044            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
5045        else:
5046            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["p_val"] <= p_val]
5047
5048        deg_stats_n = (
5049            deg_stats.sort_values(
5050                ["residual_std_abs", "esm_abs"], ascending=[False, False]
5051            )
5052            .groupby("valid_group")
5053            .head(n_max)
5054        )
5055
5056        if not cell_x in data.columns:
5057            raise ValueError("'cell_x' value not in cell names!")
5058
5059        if not cell_y in data.columns:
5060            raise ValueError("'cell_y' value not in cell names!")
5061
5062        if list(data.columns).count(cell_x) > 1:
5063            raise ValueError(
5064                f"'{cell_x}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5065                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5066            )
5067
5068        if list(data.columns).count(cell_y) > 1:
5069            raise ValueError(
5070                f"'{cell_y}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5071                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5072            )
5073
5074        data["color"] = "gray"
5075
5076        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats["feature"])), "color"] = "green"
5077
5078        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats_n["feature"])), "color"] = "blue"
5079
5080        color_order = {"gray": 0, "green": 1, "blue": 2}
5081
5082        data["color_order"] = data["color"].map(color_order)
5083
5084        data = data.sort_values("color_order")
5085
5086        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5087
5088        # dots
5089        sns.scatterplot(
5090            x=cell_x,
5091            y=cell_y,
5092            data=data,
5093            hue="color",
5094            palette={"blue": "blue", "green": "green", "gray": "gray"},
5095            legend=False,
5096            ax=ax,
5097        )
5098
5099        # regression
5100        sns.regplot(x=cell_x, y=cell_y, data=data, scatter=False, color="red", ax=ax)
5101
5102        legend_elements = [
5103            Line2D(
5104                [0],
5105                [0],
5106                marker="o",
5107                color="w",
5108                markerfacecolor="gray",
5109                markersize=7,
5110                label="Not significant",
5111            ),
5112            Line2D(
5113                [0],
5114                [0],
5115                marker="o",
5116                color="w",
5117                markerfacecolor="blue",
5118                markersize=7,
5119                label="Top significant",
5120            ),
5121            Line2D(
5122                [0],
5123                [0],
5124                marker="o",
5125                color="w",
5126                markerfacecolor="green",
5127                markersize=7,
5128                label="Significant",
5129            ),
5130            Line2D([0], [0], color="red", linewidth=2, label="Linear regression"),
5131        ]
5132
5133        ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="best", frameon=False)
5134
5135        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, _ = stats.linregress(
5136            data[cell_x], data[cell_y]
5137        )
5138
5139        equation = "y = {:.2f}x + {:.2f}".format(slope, intercept)
5140
5141        ax.annotate(
5142            "R-squared = {:.2f}\nP-value = {:.2f}\n{}".format(
5143                r_value**2, p_value, equation
5144            ),
5145            xy=(0.05, 0.90),
5146            xycoords="axes fraction",
5147            fontsize=12,
5148        )
5149
5150        ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
5151        ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
5152
5153        # oznaczanie genów
5154        def annotate_outliers(x, y, features):
5155            texts = []
5156
5157            for i, (xi, yi) in enumerate(zip(x, y)):
5158                if data.index[i] in features:
5159                    text = ax.text(xi, yi, data.index[i])
5160                    texts.append(text)
5161
5162            return texts
5163
5164        features = list(set(deg_stats_n["feature"]))
5165
5166        texts = annotate_outliers(data[cell_x], data[cell_y], features)
5167
5168        adjust_text(texts, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", alpha=0.5))
5169
5170        return deg_stats, fig
5171
5172    def cell_genes_distribution(
5173        self,
5174        cells_names: list | None,
5175        cells_sets: list | None = None,
5176        image_width=10,
5177        image_high=7,
5178    ):
5179        """
5180        Compare the distributions of the number of detected genes per cell across
5181        selected cell populations.
5182
5183        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the number of
5184        detected genes in each cell, defined as the number of genes with an expression
5185        value greater than zero. The resulting distributions are visualized as
5186        overlapping histograms, allowing the gene detection levels of different cell
5187        populations to be compared.
5188
5189        This analysis can be used as a quality-control step before comparing gene
5190        expression profiles or performing differential expression analysis. Similar
5191        distributions of detected genes per cell indicate comparable levels of gene
5192        detection across the selected populations, whereas substantial differences
5193        may indicate differences in sequencing depth, RNA content, or other technical
5194        factors.
5195
5196        Parameters
5197        ----------
5198        cells_names : list
5199            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5200
5201        cells_sets : list or None
5202            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5203            element-wise to `cells_names`. This is required when the same cell
5204            population name occurs in multiple datasets and a specific dataset
5205            needs to be selected.
5206
5207        image_width : int or float, default=10
5208            Width of the histogram figure in inches.
5209
5210        image_high : int or float, default=7
5211            Height of the histogram figure in inches.
5212
5213        Returns
5214        -------
5215        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5216            Matplotlib figure containing overlapping histograms showing the
5217            distribution of the number of detected genes per cell for each selected
5218            cell population.
5219
5220        Raises
5221        ------
5222        ValueError
5223            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5224
5225        Notes
5226        -----
5227        * A gene is considered detected when its expression value is greater than zero.
5228        * The number of detected genes is calculated independently for every cell.
5229        * Each selected cell population is represented by a separate histogram.
5230        * When `cells_sets` is provided and has the same length as `cells_names`,
5231        cell populations are selected using both their population name and dataset
5232        identifier.
5233        * The function operates on `self.normalized_data`.
5234        * The resulting distributions can be used to assess whether selected cell
5235        populations have comparable gene-detection levels before downstream
5236        comparisons.
5237        """
5238
5239        metadata = self.input_metadata
5240        data = self.normalized_data
5241
5242        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5243            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5244
5245        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5246            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5247            full_cells = []
5248            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5249                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5250
5251            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5252
5253        else:
5254            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5255            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5256
5257        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5258
5259        for name in data.columns.unique():
5260            cols = data.columns == name
5261
5262            counts = (data.loc[:, cols] > 0).sum(axis=0)
5263
5264            plt.hist(counts, bins=30, alpha=0.5, label=name)
5265
5266        plt.xlabel("Number of detected genes per cell")
5267        plt.ylabel("Number of cells")
5268        plt.legend()
5269        plt.tight_layout()
5270
5271        return fig

5273    def mm_cell_genes(
5274        self,
5275        cells_names: list | None,
5276        cells_sets: list | None,
5277        non_include_zeros: bool = True,
5278        image_width=7,
5279        image_high=10,
5280    ):
5281        """
5282        Compare the mean and median gene expression across selected cell populations.
5283
5284        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the mean and median
5285        expression values across all genes and cells. By default, zero-expression
5286        values are excluded from the calculation, allowing the comparison to focus on
5287        genes with detected expression. When `non_include_zeros` is set to False, zero
5288        values are included in the calculation.
5289
5290        The resulting mean and median expression values are visualized as a grouped
5291        bar plot, with separate bars representing the mean and median for each cell
5292        population. This visualization can be used to assess differences in the overall
5293        expression level and distribution between selected cell populations.
5294
5295        Parameters
5296        ----------
5297        cells_names : list
5298            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5299
5300        cells_sets : list or None
5301            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5302            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5303            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5304            name and dataset identifier.
5305
5306        non_include_zeros : bool, default=True
5307            Whether to exclude zero-expression values before calculating the mean and
5308            median. If True, only non-zero expression values are used. If False, all
5309            expression values, including zeros, are used.
5310
5311        image_width : int or float, default=7
5312            Width of the figure in inches.
5313
5314        image_high : int or float, default=10
5315            Height of the figure in inches.
5316
5317        Returns
5318        -------
5319        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5320            Matplotlib figure containing grouped bar plots showing the mean and median
5321            expression for each selected cell population.
5322
5323        Raises
5324        ------
5325        ValueError
5326            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5327
5328        Notes
5329        -----
5330        * Expression values are obtained from `self.normalized_data`.
5331        * The mean and median are calculated independently for each selected cell
5332        population.
5333        * When `non_include_zeros=True`, zero-expression values are excluded before
5334        calculating both statistics.
5335        * When `non_include_zeros=False`, zero-expression values contribute to both
5336        the mean and median.
5337        * The analysis uses all genes and cells belonging to each selected population.
5338        * The resulting statistics describe the overall distribution of expression
5339        values and can be used to compare the expression levels of different cell
5340        populations.
5341        """
5342
5343        metadata = self.input_metadata
5344        data = self.normalized_data
5345
5346        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5347            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5348
5349        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5350            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5351            full_cells = []
5352            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5353                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5354
5355            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5356
5357        else:
5358            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5359            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5360
5361        groups = data.columns.unique()
5362
5363        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5364
5365        mean_expression = {}
5366        median_expression = {}
5367
5368        for name in groups:
5369            cols = data.columns == name
5370
5371            values = data.loc[:, cols].values.flatten()
5372
5373            if non_include_zeros:
5374                values = values[values != 0]
5375
5376            mean_expression[name] = values.mean()
5377            median_expression[name] = np.median(values)
5378
5379        mean_expression = pd.Series(mean_expression)
5380        median_expression = pd.Series(median_expression)
5381
5382        x = np.arange(len(groups))
5383        width = 0.35
5384
5385        plt.bar(x - width / 2, mean_expression.values, width, label="Mean")
5386
5387        plt.bar(x + width / 2, median_expression.values, width, label="Median")
5388
5389        plt.xlabel("Cell")
5390        plt.ylabel("Expression")
5391        plt.xticks(x, groups, rotation=45)
5392        plt.legend()
5393
5394        plt.tight_layout()
5395
5396        return fig

5398    def cell_dispersion(
5399        self,
5400        cells_names: list | None,
5401        cells_sets: list | None,
5402        image_width=7,
5403        image_high=10,
5404    ):
5405        """
5406        Assess the within-cluster dispersion of cell gene expression profiles.
5407
5408        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the centroid of
5409        the population as the mean expression profile across all cells in the cluster.
5410        The Euclidean distance between each individual cell and its corresponding
5411        cluster centroid is then calculated to quantify how much the cell's expression
5412        profile deviates from the average profile of the cluster.
5413
5414        The resulting distributions of distances are visualized using violin plots,
5415        with each violin representing one selected cell population. The distribution
5416        shows the degree of transcriptional heterogeneity within each cluster:
5417        smaller distances indicate cells with more similar expression profiles,
5418        whereas larger distances indicate greater within-cluster variability.
5419
5420        This analysis can be used to assess the internal consistency and transcriptional
5421        heterogeneity of cell populations before comparing their expression profiles
5422        between clusters.
5423
5424        Parameters
5425        ----------
5426        self : object
5427            self object containing the input metadata and normalized expression
5428            data.
5429
5430        cells_names : list
5431            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5432
5433        cells_sets : list or None
5434            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5435            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5436            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5437            name and dataset identifier.
5438
5439        image_width : int or float, default=7
5440            Width of the figure in inches.
5441
5442        image_high : int or float, default=10
5443            Height of the figure in inches.
5444
5445        Returns
5446        -------
5447        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5448            Matplotlib figure containing violin plots showing the distribution of
5449            Euclidean distances between individual cells and their respective cluster
5450            centroids.
5451
5452        Raises
5453        ------
5454        ValueError
5455            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5456
5457        Notes
5458        -----
5459        * Expression values are obtained from `self.normalized_data`.
5460        * A cluster centroid is calculated as the mean expression profile across all
5461        cells belonging to that cluster.
5462        * The distance of each cell from the centroid is calculated using Euclidean
5463        distance across all genes.
5464        * Each cell contributes one distance value to the distribution of its cluster.
5465        * Smaller distances indicate lower within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5466        * Larger distances indicate greater within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5467        * The violin plot includes a box plot showing the median and interquartile
5468        range of the distance distribution.
5469        * Differences in dispersion between clusters can be used to assess their
5470        relative transcriptional homogeneity before downstream comparisons.
5471        """
5472
5473        metadata = self.input_metadata
5474        data = self.normalized_data
5475
5476        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5477            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5478
5479        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5480            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5481            full_cells = []
5482            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5483                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5484
5485            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5486
5487        else:
5488            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5489            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5490
5491        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5492
5493        dispersion_long = []
5494
5495        for cluster in data.columns.unique():
5496
5497            cells = data.loc[:, data.columns == cluster]
5498
5499            centroid = cells.mean(axis=1)
5500
5501            distances = np.sqrt(((cells.sub(centroid, axis=0)) ** 2).sum(axis=0))
5502
5503            for cell, distance in distances.items():
5504                dispersion_long.append(
5505                    {"cluster": cluster, "cell": cell, "distance_to_centroid": distance}
5506                )
5507
5508        dispersion_long = pd.DataFrame(dispersion_long)
5509
5510        sns.violinplot(
5511            data=dispersion_long, x="cluster", y="distance_to_centroid", inner="box"
5512        )
5513
5514        plt.ylabel("Distance from cluster centroid")
5515        plt.xlabel("Cluster")
5516        plt.xticks(rotation=45)
5517        plt.tight_layout()
5518
5519        return fig

A class COMPsc (Comparison of single-cell data) designed for the integration, analysis, and visualization of single-cell datasets. The class supports independent dataset integration, subclustering of existing clusters, marker detection, and multiple visualization strategies.

The COMPsc class provides methods for:

- Normalizing and filtering single-cell data
- Loading and saving sparse 10x-style datasets
- Computing differential expression and marker genes
- Clustering and subclustering analysis
- Visualizing similarity and spatial relationships
- Aggregating data by cell and set annotations
- Managing metadata and renaming labels
- Plotting gene detection histograms and feature dot plots

Methods

project_dir(path_to_directory, project_list) Scans a directory to create a COMPsc instance mapping project names to their paths.

save_project(name, path=os.getcwd()) Saves the COMPsc object to a pickle file on disk.

load_project(path) Loads a previously saved COMPsc object from a pickle file.

reduce_cols(reg, inc_set=False) Removes columns from data tables where column names contain a specified name or partial substring.

reduce_rows(reg, inc_set=False) Removes rows from data tables where column names contain a specified feature (gene) name.

get_data(set_info=False) Returns normalized data with optional set annotations in column names.

get_metadata() Returns the stored input metadata.

get_partial_data(names=None, features=None, name_slot='cell_names') Return a subset of the data by sample names and/or features.

gene_calculation() Calculates and stores per-cell gene detection counts as a pandas Series.

gene_histograme(bins=100) Plots a histogram of genes detected per cell with an overlaid normal distribution.

gene_threshold(min_n=None, max_n=None) Filters cells based on minimum and/or maximum gene detection thresholds.

load_sparse_from_projects(normalized_data=False) Loads and concatenates sparse 10x-style datasets from project paths into count or normalized data.

rename_names(mapping, slot='cell_names') Renames entries in a specified metadata column using a provided mapping dictionary.

rename_subclusters(mapping) Renames subcluster labels using a provided mapping dictionary.

save_sparse(path_to_save=os.getcwd(), name_slot='cell_names', data_slot='normalized') Exports data as 10x-compatible sparse files (matrix.mtx, barcodes.tsv, genes.tsv).

normalize_data(normalize=True, normalize_factor=100000) Normalizes raw counts to counts-per-specified factor (e.g., CPM-like).

statistic(cells=None, sets=None, min_exp=0.01, min_pct=0.1, n_proc=10) Computes per-feature differential expression statistics (Mann-Whitney U) comparing target vs. rest groups.

calculate_difference_markers(min_exp=0, min_pct=0.25, n_proc=10, force=False) Computes and caches differential markers using the statistic method.

clustering_features(features_list=None, name_slot='cell_names', p_val=0.05, top_n=25, adj_mean=True, beta=0.4) Prepares clustering input by selecting marker features and optionally smoothing cell values.

average() Aggregates normalized data by averaging across (cell_name, set) pairs.

estimating_similarity(method='pearson', p_val=0.05, top_n=25) Computes pairwise correlation and Euclidean distance between aggregated samples.

cell_genes_distribution(cells_names, cells_sets=None, image_width=10, image_high=7) Compares the distributions of detected genes per cell across selected cell populations using overlapping histograms.

mm_cell_genes(cells_names, cells_sets=None, non_include_zeros=True, image_width=7, image_high=10) Calculates and visualizes the mean and median gene expression across selected cell populations as a grouped bar plot.

cell_dispersion(cells_names, cells_sets=None, image_width=7, image_high=10) Assesses within-cluster transcriptional dispersion by calculating distances between individual cells and their cluster centroids, visualized via violin plots.

similarity_plot(split_sets=True, set_info=True, cmap='seismic', width=12, height=10) Visualizes pairwise similarity as a dot plot with correlation as hue and scaled distance as point size.

spatial_similarity(set_info=True, bandwidth=1, n_neighbors=5, min_dist=0.1, legend_split=2, point_size=20, ...) Creates a UMAP-like visualization of similarity relationships with cluster hulls and nearest-neighbor arrows.

subcluster_prepare(features, cluster) Initializes a Clustering object for subcluster analysis on a selected parent cluster.

define_subclusters(umap_num=2, eps=0.5, min_samples=10, bandwidth=1, n_neighbors=5, min_dist=0.1, ...) Performs UMAP and DBSCAN clustering on prepared subcluster data and stores cluster labels.

subcluster_features_dot(colors='viridis', hclust='complete', img_width=3, img_high=5, label_size=6, ...) Visualizes averaged expression and occurrence of features for subclusters as a dot plot.

subcluster_DEG_dot(top_n=3, min_exp=0, min_pct=0.25, p_val=0.05, colors='viridis', ...) Plots top differential features for subclusters as a features-dot visualization.

accept_subclusters() Commits subcluster labels to main metadata by renaming cell names and clears subcluster data.

Raises

ValueError For invalid parameters, mismatched dimensions, or missing metadata.

@classmethod
def project_dir(cls, path_to_directory, project_list): 
1679    @classmethod
1680    def project_dir(cls, path_to_directory, project_list):
1681        """
1682        Scan a directory and build a COMPsc instance mapping provided project names
1683        to their paths.
1684
1685        Parameters
1686        ----------
1687        path_to_directory : str
1688            Path containing project subfolders.
1689
1690        project_list : list[str]
1691            List of filenames (folder names) to include in the returned object map.
1692
1693        Returns
1694        -------
1695        COMPsc
1696            New COMPsc instance with `objects` populated.
1697
1698        Raises
1699        ------
1700        Exception
1701            A generic exception is caught and a message printed if scanning fails.
1702
1703        Notes
1704        -----
1705        Function attempts to match entries in `project_list` to directory
1706        names and constructs a simplified object key from the folder name.
1707        """
1708        try:
1709            objects = {}
1710            for filename in tqdm(os.listdir(path_to_directory)):
1711                for c in project_list:
1712                    f = os.path.join(path_to_directory, filename)
1713                    if c == filename and os.path.isdir(f):
1714                        objects[str(c)] = f
1715
1716            return cls(objects)
1717
1718        except:
1719            print("Something went wrong. Check the function input data and try again!")

2213        self,
2214        names: list | str | None = None,
2215        features: list | str | None = None,
2216        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
2217        inc_metadata: bool = False,
2218    ):
2219        """
2220        Return a subset of the data filtered by sample names and/or feature names.
2221
2222        Parameters
2223        ----------
2224        names : list, str, or None
2225            Names of samples to include. If None, all samples are considered.
2226
2227        features : list, str, or None
2228            Names of features to include. If None, all features are considered.
2229
2230        name_slot : str
2231            Column in metadata to use as sample names.
2232
2233        inc_metadata : bool
2234            If True return tuple (data, metadata)
2235
2236        Returns
2237        -------
2238        pandas.DataFrame
2239            Subset of the normalized data based on the specified names and features.
2240        """
2241
2242        data = self.normalized_data.copy()
2243        metadata = self.input_metadata
2244
2245        if name_slot in self.input_metadata.columns:
2246            data.columns = self.input_metadata[name_slot]
2247        else:
2248            raise ValueError("'name_slot' not occured in data!'")
2249
2250        if isinstance(features, str):
2251            features = [features]
2252        elif features is None:
2253            features = []
2254
2255        if isinstance(names, str):
2256            names = [names]
2257        elif names is None:
2258            names = []
2259
2260        features = [x.upper() for x in features]
2261        names = [x.upper() for x in names]
2262
2263        columns_names = [x.upper() for x in data.columns]
2264        features_names = [x.upper() for x in data.index]
2265
2266        columns_bool = [True if x in names else False for x in columns_names]
2267        features_bool = [True if x in features else False for x in features_names]
2268
2269        if True not in columns_bool and True not in features_bool:
2270            print("Missing 'names' and/or 'features'. Returning full dataset instead.")
2271
2272        if True in columns_bool:
2273            data = data.loc[:, columns_bool]
2274            metadata = metadata.loc[columns_bool, :]
2275
2276        if True in features_bool:
2277            data = data.loc[features_bool, :]
2278
2279        not_in_features = [y for y in features if y not in features_names]
2280
2281        if len(not_in_features) > 0:
2282            print("\nThe following features were not found in data:")
2283            print("\n".join(not_in_features))
2284
2285        not_in_names = [y for y in names if y not in columns_names]
2286
2287        if len(not_in_names) > 0:
2288            print("\nThe following names were not found in data:")
2289            print("\n".join(not_in_names))
2290
2291        if inc_metadata:
2292            return data, metadata
2293        else:
2294            return data

2310    def gene_calculation(self):

def gene_threshold(self, min_n: int | None, max_n: int | None): 
2393    def gene_threshold(self, min_n: int | None, max_n: int | None):
2394        """
2395        Filter cells by gene-detection thresholds (min and/or max).
2396
2397        Parameters
2398        ----------
2399        min_n : int or None
2400            Minimum number of detected genes required to keep a cell.
2401
2402        max_n : int or None
2403            Maximum number of detected genes allowed to keep a cell.
2404
2405        Update
2406        -------
2407        Filters `self.input_data`, `self.normalized_data`, `self.input_metadata`
2408        (and calls `average()` if `self.agg_normalized_data` exists).
2409
2410        Side Effects
2411        ------------
2412        Raises ValueError if both bounds are None or if filtering removes all cells.
2413        """
2414
2415        if min_n is not None and max_n is not None:
2416            mask = (self.gene_calc > min_n) & (self.gene_calc < max_n)
2417        elif min_n is None and max_n is not None:
2418            mask = self.gene_calc < max_n
2419        elif min_n is not None and max_n is None:
2420            mask = self.gene_calc > min_n
2421        else:
2422            raise ValueError("Lack of both min_n and max_n values")
2423
2424        if self.input_data is not None:
2425
2426            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2427                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2428
2429            self.input_data = self.input_data.loc[:, mask.values]
2430
2431        if self.normalized_data is not None:
2432
2433            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2434                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2435
2436            self.normalized_data = self.normalized_data.loc[:, mask.values]
2437
2438        if self.input_metadata is not None:
2439
2440            if len([y for y in mask if y is False]) == 0:
2441                raise ValueError("Nothing to reduce")
2442
2443            self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.loc[mask.values, :].reset_index(
2444                drop=True
2445            )
2446
2447            self.input_metadata = self.input_metadata.drop(
2448                columns=["drop"], errors="ignore"
2449            )
2450
2451        if self.agg_normalized_data is not None:
2452            self.average()
2453
2454        self.gene_calculation()
2455        self.cells_calculation()

def load_sparse_from_projects(self, normalized_data: bool = False): 
2650    def load_sparse_from_projects(self, normalized_data: bool = False):
2651        """
2652        Load sparse 10x-style datasets from stored project paths, concatenate them,
2653        and populate `input_data` / `normalized_data` and `input_metadata`.
2654
2655        Parameters
2656        ----------
2657        normalized_data : bool, default False
2658            If True, store concatenated tables in `self.normalized_data`.
2659            If False, store them in `self.input_data` and normalization
2660            is needed using normalize_data() method.
2661
2662        Side Effects
2663        ------------
2664        - Reads each project using `load_sparse(...)` (expects matrix.mtx, genes.tsv, barcodes.tsv).
2665        - Concatenates all projects column-wise and sets `self.input_metadata`.
2666        - Replaces NaNs with zeros and updates `self.gene_calc`.
2667        """
2668
2669        obj = self.objects
2670
2671        full_data = pd.DataFrame()
2672        full_metadata = pd.DataFrame()
2673
2674        for ke in obj.keys():
2675            print(ke)
2676
2677            dt, met = load_sparse(path=obj[ke], name=ke)
2678
2679            full_data = pd.concat([full_data, dt], axis=1)
2680            full_metadata = pd.concat([full_metadata, met], axis=0)
2681
2682        full_data[np.isnan(full_data)] = 0
2683
2684        if normalized_data:
2685            self.normalized_data = full_data
2686            self.input_metadata = full_metadata
2687        else:
2688
2689            self.input_data = full_data
2690            self.input_metadata = full_metadata
2691
2692        self.gene_calculation()
2693        self.cells_calculation()

def rename_names(self, mapping: dict, slot: str = 'cell_names'): 
2695    def rename_names(self, mapping: dict, slot: str = "cell_names"):
2696        """
2697        Rename entries in `self.input_metadata[slot]` according to a provided mapping.
2698
2699        Parameters
2700        ----------
2701        mapping : dict
2702            Dictionary with keys 'old_name' and 'new_name', each mapping to a list
2703            of equal length describing replacements.
2704
2705        slot : str, default 'cell_names'
2706            Metadata column to operate on.
2707
2708        Update
2709        -------
2710        Updates `self.input_metadata[slot]` in-place with renamed values.
2711
2712        Raises
2713        ------
2714        ValueError
2715            If mapping keys are incorrect, lengths differ, or some 'old_name' values
2716            are not present in the metadata column.
2717        """
2718
2719        if set(["old_name", "new_name"]) != set(mapping.keys()):
2720            raise ValueError(
2721                "Mapping dictionary must contain keys 'old_name' and 'new_name', "
2722                "each with a list of names to change."
2723            )
2724
2725        if len(mapping["old_name"]) != len(mapping["new_name"]):
2726            raise ValueError(
2727                "Mapping dictionary lists 'old_name' and 'new_name' "
2728                "must have the same length!"
2729            )
2730
2731        names_vector = list(self.input_metadata[slot])
2732
2733        if not all(elem in names_vector for elem in list(mapping["old_name"])):
2734            raise ValueError(
2735                f"Some entries from 'old_name' do not exist in the names of slot {slot}."
2736            )
2737
2738        replace_dict = dict(zip(mapping["old_name"], mapping["new_name"]))
2739
2740        names_vector_ret = [replace_dict.get(item, item) for item in names_vector]
2741
2742        self.input_metadata[slot] = names_vector_ret

2769        if len(mapping["old_name"]) != len(mapping["new_name"]):
2770            raise ValueError(
2771                "Mapping dictionary lists 'old_name' and 'new_name' "
2772                "must have the same length!"
2773            )
2774
2775        names_vector = list(self.subclusters_.subclusters)
2776
2777        if not all(elem in names_vector for elem in list(mapping["old_name"])):
2778            raise ValueError(
2779                "Some entries from 'old_name' do not exist in the subcluster names."
2780            )
2781
2782        replace_dict = dict(zip(mapping["old_name"], mapping["new_name"]))
2783
2784        names_vector_ret = [replace_dict.get(item, item) for item in names_vector]
2785
2786        self.subclusters_.subclusters = names_vector_ret

def normalize_counts(self, normalize_factor: int = 100000, log_transform: bool = True): 
2844    def normalize_counts(
2845        self, normalize_factor: int = 100000, log_transform: bool = True
2846    ):
2847        """
2848        Normalize raw counts to counts-per-(normalize_factor)
2849        (e.g., CPM, TPM - depending on normalize_factor).
2850
2851        Parameters
2852        ----------
2853        normalize_factor : int, default 100000
2854            Scaling factor used after dividing by column sums.
2855
2856        log_transform : bool, default True
2857            If True, apply log2(x+1) transformation to normalized values.
2858
2859        Update
2860        -------
2861            Sets `self.normalized_data` to normalized values (fills NaNs with 0).
2862
2863        Raises
2864        ------
2865        ValueError
2866            If `self.input_data` is missing (cannot normalize).
2867        """
2868        if self.input_data is None:
2869            raise ValueError("Input data is missing, cannot normalize.")
2870
2871        sum_col = self.input_data.sum()
2872        self.normalized_data = self.input_data.div(sum_col).fillna(0) * normalize_factor
2873
2874        if log_transform:
2875            # log2(x + 1) to avoid -inf for zeros
2876            self.normalized_data = np.log2(self.normalized_data + 1)

def statistic( self, cells=None, sets=None, with_sets_names: bool = False, min_exp: float = 0.01, min_pct: float = 0.1, n_proc: int = 10): 
2878    def statistic(
2879        self,
2880        cells=None,
2881        sets=None,
2882        with_sets_names: bool = False,
2883        min_exp: float = 0.01,
2884        min_pct: float = 0.1,
2885        n_proc: int = 10,
2886    ):
2887        """
2888        Compute per-feature statistics (Mann–Whitney U) comparing target vs rest.
2889
2890        This is a wrapper similar to `calc_DEG` tailored to use `self.normalized_data`
2891        and `self.input_metadata`. It returns per-feature statistics including p-values,
2892        adjusted p-values, means, variances, effect-size measures and fold-changes.
2893
2894        Parameters
2895        ----------
2896        cells : list, 'All', dict, or None
2897            Defines the target cells or groups for comparison (several modes supported).
2898
2899        sets : 'All', dict, or None
2900            Alternative grouping mode (operate on `self.input_metadata['sets']`).
2901
2902        min_exp : float, default 0.01
2903            Minimum expression threshold used when filtering features.
2904
2905        min_pct : float, default 0.1
2906            Minimum proportion of expressing cells in the target group required to test a feature.
2907
2908        n_proc : int, default 10
2909            Number of parallel jobs to use.
2910
2911        Returns
2912        -------
2913        pandas.DataFrame or dict
2914            Results DataFrame (or dict containing valid/control cells + DataFrame),
2915            similar to `calc_DEG` interface.
2916
2917        Raises
2918        ------
2919        ValueError
2920            If neither `cells` nor `sets` is provided, or input metadata mismatch occurs.
2921
2922        Notes
2923        -----
2924        Multiple modes supported: single-list entities, 'All', pairwise dicts, etc.
2925        """
2926
2927        offset = 1e-100
2928
2929        def stat_calc(choose, feature_name):
2930            target_values = choose.loc[choose["DEG"] == "target", feature_name]
2931            rest_values = choose.loc[choose["DEG"] == "rest", feature_name]
2932
2933            pct_valid = (target_values > 0).sum() / len(target_values)
2934            pct_rest = (rest_values > 0).sum() / len(rest_values)
2935
2936            avg_valid = np.mean(target_values)
2937            avg_ctrl = np.mean(rest_values)
2938            sd_valid = np.std(target_values, ddof=1)
2939            sd_ctrl = np.std(rest_values, ddof=1)
2940            esm = (avg_valid - avg_ctrl) / np.sqrt(((sd_valid**2 + sd_ctrl**2) / 2))
2941
2942            if np.sum(target_values) == np.sum(rest_values):
2943                p_val = 1.0
2944            else:
2945                _, p_val = stats.mannwhitneyu(
2946                    target_values, rest_values, alternative="two-sided"
2947                )
2948
2949            return {
2950                "feature": feature_name,
2951                "p_val": p_val,
2952                "pct_valid": pct_valid,
2953                "pct_ctrl": pct_rest,
2954                "avg_valid": avg_valid,
2955                "avg_ctrl": avg_ctrl,
2956                "sd_valid": sd_valid,
2957                "sd_ctrl": sd_ctrl,
2958                "esm": esm,
2959            }
2960
2961        def prepare_and_run_stat(choose, valid_group, min_exp, min_pct, n_proc):
2962
2963            def safe_min_half(series):
2964                filtered = series[(series > ((2**-1074) * 2)) & (series.notna())]
2965                return filtered.min() / 2 if not filtered.empty else 0
2966
2967            tmp_dat = choose[choose["DEG"] == "target"]
2968            tmp_dat = tmp_dat.drop("DEG", axis=1)
2969
2970            counts = (tmp_dat > min_exp).sum(axis=0)
2971
2972            total_count = tmp_dat.shape[0]
2973
2974            info = pd.DataFrame(
2975                {"feature": list(tmp_dat.columns), "pct": list(counts / total_count)}
2976            )
2977
2978            del tmp_dat
2979
2980            drop_col = info["feature"][info["pct"] <= min_pct]
2981
2982            if len(drop_col) + 1 == len(choose.columns):
2983                drop_col = info["feature"][info["pct"] == 0]
2984
2985            del info
2986
2987            choose = choose.drop(list(drop_col), axis=1)
2988
2989            results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_proc)(
2990                delayed(stat_calc)(choose, feature)
2991                for feature in tqdm(choose.columns[choose.columns != "DEG"])
2992            )
2993
2994            df = pd.DataFrame(results)
2995            df = df[(df["avg_valid"] > 0) | (df["avg_ctrl"] > 0)]
2996
2997            df["valid_group"] = str(valid_group)
2998            df.sort_values(by="p_val", inplace=True)
2999
3000            num_tests = len(df)
3001            df["adj_pval"] = np.minimum(
3002                1, (df["p_val"] * num_tests) / np.arange(1, num_tests + 1)
3003            )
3004
3005            valid_factor = safe_min_half(df["avg_valid"])
3006            ctrl_factor = safe_min_half(df["avg_ctrl"])
3007
3008            cv_factor = min(valid_factor, ctrl_factor)
3009
3010            if cv_factor == 0:
3011                cv_factor = max(valid_factor, ctrl_factor)
3012
3013            if not np.isfinite(cv_factor) or cv_factor == 0:
3014                cv_factor += offset
3015
3016            valid = df["avg_valid"].where(
3017                df["avg_valid"] != 0, df["avg_valid"] + cv_factor
3018            )
3019            ctrl = df["avg_ctrl"].where(df["avg_ctrl"] != 0, df["avg_ctrl"] + cv_factor)
3020
3021            df["FC"] = valid / ctrl
3022
3023            df["log(FC)"] = np.log2(df["FC"])
3024            df["norm_diff"] = df["avg_valid"] - df["avg_ctrl"]
3025
3026            return df
3027
3028        choose = self.normalized_data.copy().T
3029
3030        final_results = []
3031
3032        if isinstance(cells, list) and sets is None:
3033            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing selected cells to the whole set...")
3034            choose.index = (
3035                self.input_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3036            )
3037
3038            if "#" not in cells[0]:
3039                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3040
3041                print(
3042                    "Not include the set info (name # set) in the 'cells' list. "
3043                    "Only the names will be compared, without considering the set information."
3044                )
3045
3046            labels = ["target" if idx in cells else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3047            valid = list(
3048                set(choose.index[[i for i, x in enumerate(labels) if x == "target"]])
3049            )
3050
3051            choose["DEG"] = labels
3052            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3053
3054            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3055                choose.reset_index(drop=True),
3056                valid_group=valid,
3057                min_exp=min_exp,
3058                min_pct=min_pct,
3059                n_proc=n_proc,
3060            )
3061            return {"valid_cells": valid, "control_cells": "rest", "DEG": result_df}
3062
3063        elif cells == "All" and sets is None:
3064            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing each type of cell to others...")
3065
3066            if with_sets_names:
3067                choose.index = (
3068                    self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3069                    + " # "
3070                    + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3071                )
3072            else:
3073                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3074
3075            unique_labels = set(choose.index)
3076
3077            for label in tqdm(unique_labels):
3078                print(f"\nCalculating statistics for {label}")
3079                labels = ["target" if idx == label else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3080                choose["DEG"] = labels
3081                choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3082                result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3083                    choose.copy(),
3084                    valid_group=label,
3085                    min_exp=min_exp,
3086                    min_pct=min_pct,
3087                    n_proc=n_proc,
3088                )
3089                final_results.append(result_df)
3090
3091            return pd.concat(final_results, ignore_index=True)
3092
3093        elif cells is None and sets == "All":
3094            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing each set/group to others...")
3095            choose.index = self.input_metadata["sets"]
3096            unique_sets = set(choose.index)
3097
3098            for label in tqdm(unique_sets):
3099                print(f"\nCalculating statistics for {label}")
3100                labels = ["target" if idx == label else "rest" for idx in choose.index]
3101
3102                choose["DEG"] = labels
3103                choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3104                result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3105                    choose.copy(),
3106                    valid_group=label,
3107                    min_exp=min_exp,
3108                    min_pct=min_pct,
3109                    n_proc=n_proc,
3110                )
3111                final_results.append(result_df)
3112
3113            return pd.concat(final_results, ignore_index=True)
3114
3115        elif cells is None and isinstance(sets, dict):
3116            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing groups...")
3117
3118            choose.index = self.input_metadata["sets"]
3119
3120            group_list = list(sets.keys())
3121            if len(group_list) != 2:
3122                print("Only pairwise group comparison is supported.")
3123                return None
3124
3125            labels = [
3126                (
3127                    "target"
3128                    if idx in sets[group_list[0]]
3129                    else "rest" if idx in sets[group_list[1]] else "drop"
3130                )
3131                for idx in choose.index
3132            ]
3133            choose["DEG"] = labels
3134            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3135
3136            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(
3137                choose.reset_index(drop=True),
3138                valid_group=group_list[0],
3139                min_exp=min_exp,
3140                min_pct=min_pct,
3141                n_proc=n_proc,
3142            )
3143            return result_df
3144
3145        elif isinstance(cells, dict) and sets is None:
3146            print("\nAnalysis started...\nComparing groups...")
3147            choose.index = (
3148                self.input_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + self.input_metadata["sets"]
3149            )
3150
3151            if "#" not in cells[list(cells.keys())[0]][0]:
3152                choose.index = self.input_metadata["cell_names"]
3153
3154                print(
3155                    "Not include the set info (name # set) in the 'cells' dict. "
3156                    "Only the names will be compared, without considering the set information."
3157                )
3158
3159            group_list = list(cells.keys())
3160            if len(group_list) != 2:
3161                print("Only pairwise group comparison is supported.")
3162                return None
3163
3164            labels = [
3165                (
3166                    "target"
3167                    if idx in cells[group_list[0]]
3168                    else "rest" if idx in cells[group_list[1]] else "drop"
3169                )
3170                for idx in choose.index
3171            ]
3172
3173            choose["DEG"] = labels
3174            choose = choose[choose["DEG"] != "drop"]
3175
3176            result_df = prepare_and_run_stat(

3186        else:

3189            )

def clustering_features( self, features_list: list | None, name_slot: str = 'cell_names', p_val: float = 0.05, top_n: int = 25, adj_mean: bool = True, beta: float = 0.2):

3234        self,

3241    ):
3242        """
3243        Prepare clustering input by selecting marker features and optionally smoothing cell values
3244        toward group means.
3245
3246        Parameters
3247        ----------
3248        features_list : list or None
3249            If provided, use this list of features. If None, features are selected
3250            from `self.var_data` (adj_pval <= p_val, positive logFC) picking `top_n` per group.
3251
3252        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'

3270        ready for PCA/UMAP/clustering.

3294        )

3299
3300        self.clustering_data = data
3301

def average(self): 
3304    def average(self):
3305        """
3306        Aggregate normalized data by (cell_name, set) pairs computing the mean per group.
3307
3308        The method constructs new column names as "cell_name # set", averages columns
3309        sharing identical labels, and populates `self.agg_normalized_data` and `self.agg_metadata`.
3310
3311        Update
3312        ------
3313        Sets `self.agg_normalized_data` (features x aggregated samples) and
3314        `self.agg_metadata` (DataFrame with 'cell_names' and 'sets').
3315        """
3316
3317        wide_data = self.normalized_data
3318
3319        wide_metadata = self.input_metadata
3320
3321        new_names = wide_metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + wide_metadata["sets"]
3322
3323        wide_data.columns = list(new_names)
3324
3325        aggregated_df = wide_data.T.groupby(level=0).mean().T
3326
3327        sets = [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in aggregated_df.columns]
3328        names = [re.sub(" #.*", "", x) for x in aggregated_df.columns]
3329
3330        aggregated_df.columns = names
3331        aggregated_metadata = pd.DataFrame({"cell_names": names, "sets": sets})
3332
3333        self.agg_metadata = aggregated_metadata
3334        self.agg_normalized_data = aggregated_df

Aggregate normalized data by (cell_name, set) pairs computing the mean per group.

The method constructs new column names as "cell_name # set", averages columns sharing identical labels, and populates self.agg_normalized_data and self.agg_metadata.

Update

Sets self.agg_normalized_data (features x aggregated samples) and self.agg_metadata (DataFrame with 'cell_names' and 'sets').

def estimating_similarity(self, method='pearson', p_val: float = 0.05, top_n: int = 25): 
3336    def estimating_similarity(
3337        self, method="pearson", p_val: float = 0.05, top_n: int = 25
3338    ):
3339        """
3340        Estimate pairwise similarity and Euclidean distance between aggregated samples.
3341
3342        Parameters
3343        ----------
3344        method : str, default 'pearson'
3345            Correlation method to use (passed to pandas.DataFrame.corr()).
3346
3347        p_val : float, default 0.05
3348            Adjusted p-value cutoff used to select marker features from `self.var_data`.
3349
3350        top_n : int, default 25
3351            Number of top features per valid group to include.
3352
3353        Update
3354        -------
3355        Computes a combined table with per-pair correlation and euclidean distance
3356        and stores it in `self.similarity`.
3357        """
3358
3359        if self.var_data is None:
3360            raise ValueError(
3361                "Lack of 'self.var_data'. Use self.calculate_difference_markers() method first."
3362            )
3363
3364        self.average()
3365        metadata = self.agg_metadata
3366        data = self.agg_normalized_data
3367
3368        df_tmp = self.var_data[self.var_data["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
3369        df_tmp = df_tmp[df_tmp["log(FC)"] > 0]
3370        df_tmp = (
3371            df_tmp.sort_values(
3372                ["valid_group", "esm", "log(FC)"], ascending=[True, False, False]
3373            )
3374            .groupby("valid_group")
3375            .head(top_n)
3376        )
3377
3378        data = data.loc[list(set(df_tmp["feature"]))]
3379
3380        if len(set(metadata["sets"])) > 1:
3381            data.columns = data.columns + " # " + [x for x in metadata["sets"]]
3382        else:
3383            data = data.copy()
3384
3385        scaler = StandardScaler()
3386
3387        scaled_data = scaler.fit_transform(data)
3388
3389        scaled_df = pd.DataFrame(scaled_data, columns=data.columns)
3390
3391        cor = scaled_df.corr(method=method)
3392        cor_df = cor.stack().reset_index()
3393        cor_df.columns = ["cell1", "cell2", "correlation"]
3394
3395        distances = pdist(scaled_df.T, metric="euclidean")
3396        dist_mat = pd.DataFrame(
3397            squareform(distances), index=scaled_df.columns, columns=scaled_df.columns
3398        )
3399        dist_df = dist_mat.stack().reset_index()
3400        dist_df.columns = ["cell1", "cell2", "euclidean_dist"]
3401
3402        full = pd.merge(cor_df, dist_df, on=["cell1", "cell2"])
3403
3404        full = full[full["cell1"] != full["cell2"]]
3405        full = full.reset_index(drop=True)
3406
3407        self.similarity = full

Estimate pairwise similarity and Euclidean distance between aggregated samples.

Parameters

method : str, default 'pearson' Correlation method to use (passed to pandas.DataFrame.corr()).

p_val : float, default 0.05 Adjusted p-value cutoff used to select marker features from self.var_data.

top_n : int, default 25 Number of top features per valid group to include.

Update

Computes a combined table with per-pair correlation and euclidean distance and stores it in self.similarity.
