def spatial_similarity( self, set_info: bool = True, bandwidth=1, n_neighbors=5, min_dist=0.1, legend_split=2, point_size=200, spread=1.0, set_op_mix_ratio=1.0, local_connectivity=1, repulsion_strength=1.0, negative_sample_rate=5, threshold=0.1, size_sort: bool = True, width=12, height=10): 
3520    def spatial_similarity(
3521        self,
3522        set_info: bool = True,
3523        bandwidth=1,
3524        n_neighbors=5,
3525        min_dist=0.1,
3526        legend_split=2,
3527        point_size=200,
3528        spread=1.0,
3529        set_op_mix_ratio=1.0,
3530        local_connectivity=1,
3531        repulsion_strength=1.0,
3532        negative_sample_rate=5,
3533        threshold=0.1,
3534        size_sort: bool = True,
3535        width=12,
3536        height=10,
3537    ):
3538        """
3539        Create a spatial UMAP-like visualization of similarity relationships between samples.
3540
3541        Parameters
3542        ----------
3543        set_info : bool, default True
3544            If True, retain set information in labels.
3545
3546        bandwidth : float, default 1
3547            Bandwidth used by MeanShift for clustering polygons.
3548
3549        point_size : float, default 200
3550            Size of scatter points.
3551
3552        legend_split : int, default 2
3553            Number of columns in legend.
3554
3555        n_neighbors, min_dist, spread, set_op_mix_ratio, local_connectivity, repulsion_strength, negative_sample_rate : parameters passed to UMAP.
3556
3557        threshold : float, default 0.1
3558            Minimum text distance for label adjustment to avoid overlap.
3559
3560        size_sort : bool, default=True
3561            If True, cluster names are sorted in descending order by cluster size.
3562             If False, cluster names follow the order of their first appearance in `names_slot`.
3563
3564        width : int, default 12
3565            Figure width.
3566
3567        height : int, default 10
3568            Figure height.
3569
3570        Returns
3571        -------
3572        matplotlib.figure.Figure
3573
3574        Raises
3575        ------
3576        ValueError
3577            If `self.similarity` is None.
3578
3579        Notes
3580        -----
3581        Builds a precomputed distance matrix combining correlation and euclidean distance,
3582        runs UMAP with metric='precomputed', then overlays cluster hulls (MeanShift + convex hull)
3583        and arrows to indicate nearest neighbors (minimal combined distance).
3584        """
3585
3586        if self.similarity is None:
3587            raise ValueError(
3588                "Similarity data is missing. Please calculate similarity using self.estimating_similarity."
3589            )
3590
3591        similarity_data = self.similarity
3592
3593        sim = similarity_data["correlation"]
3594        sim_scaled = (sim - sim.min()) / (sim.max() - sim.min())
3595        eu_dist = similarity_data["euclidean_dist"]
3596        eu_dist_scaled = (eu_dist - eu_dist.min()) / (eu_dist.max() - eu_dist.min())
3597
3598        similarity_data["combo_dist"] = (1 - sim_scaled) * eu_dist_scaled
3599
3600        # for nn target
3601        arrow_df = similarity_data.copy()
3602        arrow_df = similarity_data.loc[
3603            similarity_data.groupby("cell1")["combo_dist"].idxmin()
3604        ]
3605
3606        cells = sorted(set(similarity_data["cell1"]) | set(similarity_data["cell2"]))
3607        combo_matrix = pd.DataFrame(0, index=cells, columns=cells, dtype=float)
3608
3609        for _, row in similarity_data.iterrows():
3610            combo_matrix.loc[row["cell1"], row["cell2"]] = row["combo_dist"]
3611            combo_matrix.loc[row["cell2"], row["cell1"]] = row["combo_dist"]
3612
3613        tmp_data = self.input_metadata.copy()
3614
3615        tmp_data["tmp_nam"] = list(tmp_data["cell_names"] + " # " + tmp_data["sets"])
3616
3617        tmp_data["count"] = tmp_data["tmp_nam"].map(tmp_data["tmp_nam"].value_counts())
3618
3619        tmp_data = pd.DataFrame(tmp_data[["count", "tmp_nam"]].copy()).drop_duplicates()
3620
3621        queue = pd.unique(tmp_data["tmp_nam"])
3622
3623        tmp_data["tmp_nam"] = pd.Categorical(
3624            tmp_data["tmp_nam"], categories=queue, ordered=True
3625        )
3626
3627        if size_sort:
3628            tmp_data = tmp_data.sort_values("count", ascending=False).reset_index(
3629                drop=True
3630            )
3631            tmp_data["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(tmp_data["count"])[0]
3632
3633        else:
3634
3635            tmp_data = tmp_data.sort_values("tmp_nam").reset_index(drop=True)
3636            tmp_data["id_vec"] = pd.factorize(tmp_data["tmp_nam"])[0]
3637
3638        umap_model = umap.UMAP(
3639            n_components=2,
3640            metric="precomputed",
3641            n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
3642            min_dist=min_dist,
3643            spread=spread,
3644            set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
3645            local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
3646            repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
3647            negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
3648            transform_seed=42,
3649            init="spectral",
3650            random_state=42,
3651            verbose=True,
3652        )
3653
3654        coords = pd.DataFrame(umap_model.fit_transform(combo_matrix.values))
3655        coords.index = list(combo_matrix.index)
3656        coords = np.array(coords.loc[tmp_data["tmp_nam"].values, :])
3657
3658        cell_names = list(tmp_data["tmp_nam"].values)
3659        num_cells = len(cell_names)
3660        palette = sns.color_palette("tab20c", num_cells)
3661
3662        if "#" in cell_names[0]:
3663            avsets = set(
3664                [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell1"]]
3665                + [re.sub(".*# ", "", x) for x in similarity_data["cell2"]]
3666            )
3667            num_sets = len(avsets)
3668            color_indices = [i * len(palette) // num_sets for i in range(num_sets)]
3669            color_mapping_sets = {
3670                set_name: palette[i] for i, set_name in zip(color_indices, avsets)
3671            }
3672            color_mapping = {
3673                name: color_mapping_sets[re.sub(".*# ", "", name)]
3674                for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)
3675            }
3676        else:
3677            color_mapping = {name: palette[i] for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)}
3678
3679        meanshift = MeanShift(bandwidth=bandwidth)
3680        labels = meanshift.fit_predict(coords)
3681
3682        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(width, height))
3683        ax = plt.gca()
3684
3685        unique_labels = set(labels)
3686        cluster_palette = sns.color_palette("hls", len(unique_labels))
3687
3688        for label in unique_labels:
3689            if label == -1:
3690                continue
3691            cluster_coords = coords[labels == label]
3692            if len(cluster_coords) < 3:
3693                continue
3694
3695            hull = ConvexHull(cluster_coords)
3696            hull_points = cluster_coords[hull.vertices]
3697
3698            centroid = np.mean(hull_points, axis=0)
3699            expanded = hull_points + 0.05 * (hull_points - centroid)
3700
3701            poly = Polygon(
3702                expanded,
3703                closed=True,
3704                facecolor=cluster_palette[label],
3705                edgecolor="none",
3706                alpha=0.2,
3707                zorder=1,
3708            )
3709            ax.add_patch(poly)
3710
3711        texts = []
3712        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(coords):
3713            plt.scatter(
3714                x,
3715                y,
3716                s=point_size,
3717                color=color_mapping[cell_names[i]],
3718                edgecolors="black",
3719                linewidths=0.5,
3720                zorder=2,
3721            )
3722            texts.append(
3723                ax.text(
3724                    x, y, str(i), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8, color="black"
3725                )
3726            )
3727
3728        def dist(p1, p2):
3729            return np.sqrt((p1[0] - p2[0]) ** 2 + (p1[1] - p2[1]) ** 2)
3730
3731        texts_to_adjust = []
3732        for i, t1 in enumerate(texts):
3733            for j, t2 in enumerate(texts):
3734                if i >= j:
3735                    continue
3736                d = dist(
3737                    (t1.get_position()[0], t1.get_position()[1]),
3738                    (t2.get_position()[0], t2.get_position()[1]),
3739                )
3740                if d < threshold:
3741                    if t1 not in texts_to_adjust:
3742                        texts_to_adjust.append(t1)
3743                    if t2 not in texts_to_adjust:
3744                        texts_to_adjust.append(t2)
3745
3746        adjust_text(
3747            texts_to_adjust,
3748            expand_text=(1.0, 1.0),
3749            force_text=0.9,
3750            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", lw=0.1),
3751            ax=ax,
3752        )
3753
3754        for _, row in arrow_df.iterrows():
3755            try:
3756                idx1 = cell_names.index(row["cell1"])
3757                idx2 = cell_names.index(row["cell2"])
3758            except ValueError:
3759                continue
3760            x1, y1 = coords[idx1]
3761            x2, y2 = coords[idx2]
3762            arrow = FancyArrowPatch(
3763                (x1, y1),
3764                (x2, y2),
3765                arrowstyle="->",
3766                color="gray",
3767                linewidth=1.5,
3768                alpha=0.5,
3769                mutation_scale=12,
3770                zorder=0,
3771            )
3772            ax.add_patch(arrow)
3773
3774        set_names = set([re.sub(r".*# ", "", x) for x in cell_names])
3775
3776        sets = []
3777        for ic in set_names:
3778            sets.append([x for x in cell_names if ic in x][0])
3779
3780        legend_elements = [
3781            Patch(
3782                facecolor=color_mapping[name],
3783                edgecolor="black",
3784                label=f"{i} – {re.sub(' #.*', '', name)}",
3785            )
3786            for i, name in enumerate(cell_names)
3787        ]
3788
3789        if set_info is True and len(sets) > 1:
3790
3791            for ds in sets:
3792                proxy_marker = Line2D(
3793                    [0],
3794                    [0],
3795                    marker="o",
3796                    color="w",
3797                    markersize=12,
3798                    markerfacecolor=color_mapping[ds],
3799                    markeredgecolor="black",
3800                    linestyle="None",
3801                    label=f"Data: {re.sub(r'.*# ', '', ds)}",
3802                )
3803                legend_elements.append(proxy_marker)
3804
3805        plt.legend(
3806            handles=legend_elements,
3807            title="",
3808            bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1),
3809            loc="upper left",
3810            ncol=legend_split,
3811        )
3812
3813        plt.xlabel("UMAP 1")
3814        plt.ylabel("UMAP 2")
3815        plt.grid(False)
3816        plt.show()
3817
3818        return fig

3850    def define_subclusters(
3851        self,
3852        umap_num: int = 2,

3854        min_samples: int = 10,
3855        n_neighbors: int = 5,
3856        min_dist: float = 0.1,
3857        spread: float = 1.0,

3861        negative_sample_rate: int = 5,
3862        width=8,
3863        height=6,
3864    ):
3865        """
3866        Compute UMAP and DBSCAN clustering within a previously prepared subcluster dataset.
3867
3868        Parameters
3869        ----------
3870        umap_num : int, default 2
3871            Number of UMAP dimensions to compute.
3872
3873        eps : float, default 0.5
3874            DBSCAN eps parameter.
3875
3876        min_samples : int, default 10
3877            DBSCAN min_samples parameter.
3878
3879        n_neighbors, min_dist, spread, set_op_mix_ratio, local_connectivity, repulsion_strength, negative_sample_rate, width, height :
3880            Additional parameters passed to UMAP / plotting / MeanShift as appropriate.
3881
3882        Update
3883        -------
3884        Stores cluster labels in `self.subclusters_.subclusters`.
3885
3886        Raises
3887        ------
3888        RuntimeError
3889            If `self.subclusters_` has not been prepared.
3890        """
3891
3892        if self.subclusters_ is None:
3893            raise RuntimeError(
3894                "Nothing to return. 'self.subcluster_prepare' was not conducted!"
3895            )
3896
3897        self.subclusters_.perform_UMAP(
3898            factorize=False,
3899            umap_num=umap_num,
3900            pc_num=0,
3901            harmonized=False,
3902            n_neighbors=n_neighbors,
3903            min_dist=min_dist,
3904            spread=spread,
3905            set_op_mix_ratio=set_op_mix_ratio,
3906            local_connectivity=local_connectivity,
3907            repulsion_strength=repulsion_strength,
3908            negative_sample_rate=negative_sample_rate,
3909            width=width,
3910            height=height,
3911        )
3912
3913        fig = self.subclusters_.find_clusters_UMAP(

3916            min_samples=min_samples,
3917            width=width,

4189    def accept_subclusters(self):
4190        """
4191        Commit subcluster labels into the main `input_metadata` by renaming cell names.
4192
4193        The method replaces occurrences of the parent cluster name in `self.input_metadata['cell_names']`
4194        with the expanded names that include subcluster suffixes (via `add_subnames`),
4195        then clears `self.subclusters_`.
4196
4197        Update
4198        ------
4199        Modifies `self.input_metadata['cell_names']`.
4200
4201        Resets `self.subclusters_` to None.
4202
4203        Raises
4204        ------
4205        RuntimeError
4206            If `self.subclusters_` is not defined or subclusters were not computed.
4207        """
4208
4209        if self.subclusters_ is None or self.subclusters_.subclusters is None:
4210            raise RuntimeError(
4211                "Nothing to return. 'self.subcluster_prepare' -> 'self.define_subclusters' pip was not conducted!"
4212            )
4213
4214        new_meta = add_subnames(
4215            list(self.input_metadata["cell_names"]),
4216            parent_name=self.subclusters_.current_cluster,
4217            new_clusters=self.subclusters_.subclusters,
4218        )
4219
4220        self.input_metadata["cell_names"] = new_meta
4221
4222        if "clustering_metadata" in self.__dict__.keys():
4223            self.clustering_metadata["cell_names"] = new_meta
4224
4225        self.subclusters_ = None

4359    def data_composition(
4360        self,
4361        features_count: list | None,
4362        name_slot: str = "cell_names",
4363        set_sep: bool = True,
4364    ):
4365        """
4366        Compute composition of cell types in data set.
4367
4368        This function counts the occurrences of specific cells (e.g., cell types, subtypes)
4369        within metadata entries, calculates their relative percentages, and stores
4370        the results in `self.composition_data`.
4371
4372        Parameters
4373        ----------
4374        features_count : list or None
4375            List of features (part or full names) to be counted.
4376            If None, all unique elements from the specified `name_slot` metadata field are used.
4377
4378        name_slot : str, default 'cell_names'
4379            Metadata field containing sample identifiers or labels.
4380
4381        set_sep : bool, default True
4382            If True and multiple sets are present in metadata, compute composition
4383            separately for each set.
4384
4385        Update
4386        -------
4387        Stores results in `self.composition_data` as a pandas DataFrame with:
4388        - 'name': feature name
4389        - 'n': number of occurrences
4390        - 'pct': percentage of occurrences
4391        - 'set' (if applicable): dataset identifier
4392        """
4393
4394        validated_list = list(self.input_metadata[name_slot])
4395        sets = list(self.input_metadata["sets"])
4396
4397        if features_count is None:
4398            features_count = list(set(self.input_metadata[name_slot]))
4399
4400        if set_sep and len(set(sets)) > 1:
4401
4402            final_res = pd.DataFrame()
4403
4404            for s in set(sets):
4405                print(s)
4406
4407                mask = [True if s == x else False for x in sets]
4408
4409                tmp_val_list = np.array(validated_list)
4410
4411                tmp_val_list = list(tmp_val_list[mask])
4412
4413                res_dict = {"name": [], "n": [], "set": []}
4414
4415                for f in tqdm(features_count):
4416                    res_dict["n"].append(
4417                        sum(1 for element in tmp_val_list if f in element)
4418                    )
4419                    res_dict["name"].append(f)
4420                    res_dict["set"].append(s)
4421                    res = pd.DataFrame(res_dict)
4422                    res["pct"] = res["n"] / sum(res["n"]) * 100
4423                    res["pct"] = res["pct"].round(2)
4424
4425                final_res = pd.concat([final_res, res])
4426
4427            res = final_res.sort_values(["set", "pct"], ascending=[True, False])
4428
4429        else:
4430
4431            res_dict = {"name": [], "n": []}
4432
4433            for f in tqdm(features_count):
4434                res_dict["n"].append(
4435                    sum(1 for element in validated_list if f in element)
4436                )
4437                res_dict["name"].append(f)
4438
4439            res = pd.DataFrame(res_dict)
4440            res["pct"] = res["n"] / sum(res["n"]) * 100
4441            res["pct"] = res["pct"].round(2)
4442
4443            res = res.sort_values("pct", ascending=False)
4444
4445        self.composition_data = res

Compute composition of cell types in data set.

This function counts the occurrences of specific cells (e.g., cell types, subtypes) within metadata entries, calculates their relative percentages, and stores the results in self.composition_data.

Parameters

set_sep : bool, default True If True and multiple sets are present in metadata, compute composition separately for each set.

  • 'n': number of occurrences

def cell_regression( self, cell_x: str, cell_y: str, set_x: str | None = None, set_y: str | None = None, min_log=0.5, n_max=20, min_exp=0.1, min_pct=0.5, n_proc=10, min_esm=0.5, p_val=0.05, adj=True, image_width=12, image_high=7): 
4830    def cell_regression(
4831        self,
4832        cell_x: str,
4833        cell_y: str,
4834        set_x: str | None = None,
4835        set_y: str | None = None,
4836        min_log=0.5,
4837        n_max=20,
4838        min_exp=0.1,
4839        min_pct=0.5,
4840        n_proc=10,
4841        min_esm=0.5,
4842        p_val=0.05,
4843        adj=True,
4844        image_width=12,
4845        image_high=7,
4846    ):
4847        """
4848        Perform linear regression between two selected cell populations and identify
4849        significant and top-ranked differentially expressed genes.
4850
4851        The function compares the expression profiles of two selected cells or cell
4852        populations using linear regression. Each gene is represented as a point in
4853        the regression plot, with expression in `cell_x` on the X-axis and expression
4854        in `cell_y` on the Y-axis.
4855
4856        Differential expression statistics are calculated using `calc_DEG`. Genes are
4857        first filtered according to the minimum absolute log fold change, minimum
4858        absolute effect size (ESM), and statistical significance. Among the
4859        significant genes, up to `n_max` genes are selected within each `valid_group`,
4860        prioritizing genes with the largest standardized absolute regression residuals
4861        and absolute ESM values.
4862
4863        The regression plot uses three point categories:
4864        - gray: genes that are not statistically significant,
4865        - green: statistically significant genes that pass the DEG thresholds,
4866        - blue: top `n_max` genes selected within each `valid_group`.
4867
4868        The selected top genes are additionally annotated with their gene names.
4869        The plot also displays the fitted linear regression line, R-squared,
4870        p-value, and regression equation.
4871
4872        Parameters
4873        ----------
4874        cell_x : str
4875            Name of the first cell or cell population used as the X-axis.
4876
4877        cell_y : str
4878            Name of the second cell or cell population used as the Y-axis.
4879
4880        set_x : str or None
4881            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_x`.
4882            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4883            the cell is selected only by its name.
4884
4885        set_y : str or None
4886            Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to `cell_y`.
4887            Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None,
4888            the cell is selected only by its name.
4889
4890        min_log : float, default=0.5
4891            Minimum absolute log fold change required for a gene to be considered
4892            for significant DEG selection.
4893
4894        n_max : int, default=20
4895            Maximum number of top genes selected from each `valid_group`.
4896            Genes are ranked primarily by standardized absolute regression residual
4897            and secondarily by absolute Effect Size - Cohen's d.
4898
4899        min_exp : float, default=0.1
4900            Minimum expression threshold passed to `calc_DEG`.
4901
4902        min_pct : float, default=0.5
4903            Minimum fraction of cells in which a gene must be expressed, passed to
4904            `calc_DEG`.
4905
4906        n_proc : int, default=10
4907            Number of parallel processes used by `calc_DEG`.
4908
4909        min_esm : float, default=0.5
4910            Minimum absolute ESM (effect size measure) required for DEG selection.
4911
4912        p_val : float, default=0.05
4913            Maximum allowed p-value for statistical significance. If `adj=True`,
4914            this threshold is applied to the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`);
4915            otherwise, it is applied to the raw p-value (`p_val`).
4916
4917        adj : bool, default=True
4918            Whether to use the adjusted p-value (`adj_pval`) instead of the raw
4919            p-value (`p_val`) for statistical significance filtering.
4920
4921        image_width : int or float, default=12
4922            Width of the regression plot in inches.
4923
4924        image_high : int or float, default=7
4925            Height of the regression plot in inches.
4926
4927
4928
4929        Returns
4930        -------
4931        deg_stats : pandas.DataFrame
4932            DataFrame containing the DEG statistics after filtering by absolute
4933            log fold change, absolute ESM, and statistical significance.
4934
4935        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
4936            Matplotlib figure containing the regression plot, including expression
4937            points, regression line, regression statistics, and annotations for
4938            the selected top genes.
4939
4940        Raises
4941        ------
4942        ValueError
4943            If `cell_x` or `cell_y` is not found in the dataset.
4944
4945        ValueError
4946            If multiple columns correspond to the same cell name and the required
4947            dataset identifiers (`set_x` and/or `set_y`) were not provided.
4948
4949        Notes
4950        -----
4951        * The function calls `self.average()` before performing the analysis.
4952        * Linear regression is calculated using `scipy.stats.linregress`.
4953        * Regression residuals are calculated as the difference between the observed
4954        Y value and the value predicted by the fitted regression model.
4955        * Standardized residuals are used to prioritize genes that deviate most
4956        strongly from the expected linear relationship.
4957        * Significant genes are filtered using absolute log fold change, absolute
4958        ESM, and either raw or adjusted p-value.
4959        * Top genes are selected separately within each `valid_group`.
4960        * The top genes are annotated on the regression plot.
4961        * The returned `deg_stats` contains the significant genes before the final
4962        `n_max` per-group selection.
4963
4964
4965        Examples
4966        --------
4967        > > > deg_stats, fig = obj.cell_regression(
4968        > > > ...     cell_x="NeuronA",
4969        > > > ...     cell_y="NeuronB",
4970        > > > ...     min_log_min=0.5,
4971        > > > ...     min_esm=0.5,
4972        > > > ...     p_val=0.05,
4973        > > > ...     n_max=20
4974        > > > ... )
4975        > > >
4976        """

4978        self.average()
4979

4982        data2 = self.normalized_data
4983        metadata2 = self.input_metadata
4984
4985        if set_x is not None and set_y is not None:
4986            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
4987            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata2["sets"]
4988            cell_x = cell_x + " # " + set_x
4989            cell_y = cell_y + " # " + set_y
4990
4991            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
4992                data2,
4993                metadata_list=None,
4994                entities={
4995                    "cell_x": cell_x + " # " + set_x,
4996                    "cell_y": cell_y + " # " + set_y,
4997                },
4998                sets=None,
4999                min_exp=min_exp,
5000                min_pct=min_pct,
5001                n_proc=n_proc,
5002            )
5003
5004        else:
5005            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5006            data2.columns = metadata2["cell_names"]
5007
5008            deg_stats = calc_DEG(
5009                data2,
5010                metadata_list=None,
5011                entities={"cell_x": cell_x, "cell_y": cell_y},
5012                sets=None,
5013                min_exp=min_exp,
5014                min_pct=min_pct,

5018        # points
5019        x = data[cell_x]
5020        y = data[cell_y]
5021
5022        # regression
5023        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, std_err = stats.linregress(x, y)
5024
5025        # prediction
5026        y_pred = slope * x + intercept
5027
5028        # residuals
5029        residual = y - y_pred
5030
5031        # residuals for DEG
5032        deg_stats["residual"] = deg_stats["feature"].map(residual)
5033        deg_stats["residual_abs"] = deg_stats["residual"].abs()
5034        deg_stats["residual_std"] = deg_stats["residual"] / residual.std()
5035        deg_stats["residual_std_abs"] = deg_stats["residual_std"].abs()
5036        deg_stats["esm_abs"] = deg_stats["esm"].abs()
5037
5038        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["log(FC)"].abs() >= min_log]
5039
5040        deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["esm_abs"] >= min_esm]
5041
5042        if adj:
5043
5044            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["adj_pval"] <= p_val]
5045        else:
5046            deg_stats = deg_stats[deg_stats["p_val"] <= p_val]
5047
5048        deg_stats_n = (
5049            deg_stats.sort_values(
5050                ["residual_std_abs", "esm_abs"], ascending=[False, False]
5051            )
5052            .groupby("valid_group")
5053            .head(n_max)
5054        )
5055
5056        if not cell_x in data.columns:
5057            raise ValueError("'cell_x' value not in cell names!")
5058
5059        if not cell_y in data.columns:
5060            raise ValueError("'cell_y' value not in cell names!")
5061
5062        if list(data.columns).count(cell_x) > 1:
5063            raise ValueError(
5064                f"'{cell_x}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5065                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5066            )
5067
5068        if list(data.columns).count(cell_y) > 1:
5069            raise ValueError(
5070                f"'{cell_y}' occurs more than once. If you want to select a specific cell, "
5071                f"please also provide the corresponding 'set_x' and 'set_y' values."
5072            )
5073
5074        data["color"] = "gray"
5075
5076        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats["feature"])), "color"] = "green"
5077
5078        data.loc[data.index.isin(set(deg_stats_n["feature"])), "color"] = "blue"
5079
5080        color_order = {"gray": 0, "green": 1, "blue": 2}
5081
5082        data["color_order"] = data["color"].map(color_order)
5083
5084        data = data.sort_values("color_order")
5085
5086        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5087
5088        # dots
5089        sns.scatterplot(
5090            x=cell_x,
5091            y=cell_y,
5092            data=data,
5093            hue="color",
5094            palette={"blue": "blue", "green": "green", "gray": "gray"},
5095            legend=False,
5096            ax=ax,
5097        )
5098
5099        # regression
5100        sns.regplot(x=cell_x, y=cell_y, data=data, scatter=False, color="red", ax=ax)
5101
5102        legend_elements = [
5103            Line2D(
5104                [0],
5105                [0],
5106                marker="o",
5107                color="w",
5108                markerfacecolor="gray",
5109                markersize=7,
5110                label="Not significant",
5111            ),
5112            Line2D(
5113                [0],
5114                [0],
5115                marker="o",
5116                color="w",
5117                markerfacecolor="blue",
5118                markersize=7,
5119                label="Top significant",
5120            ),
5121            Line2D(
5122                [0],
5123                [0],
5124                marker="o",
5125                color="w",
5126                markerfacecolor="green",
5127                markersize=7,
5128                label="Significant",
5129            ),
5130            Line2D([0], [0], color="red", linewidth=2, label="Linear regression"),
5131        ]
5132
5133        ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="best", frameon=False)
5134
5135        slope, intercept, r_value, p_value, _ = stats.linregress(
5136            data[cell_x], data[cell_y]
5137        )
5138
5139        equation = "y = {:.2f}x + {:.2f}".format(slope, intercept)
5140
5141        ax.annotate(
5142            "R-squared = {:.2f}\nP-value = {:.2f}\n{}".format(
5143                r_value**2, p_value, equation
5144            ),
5145            xy=(0.05, 0.90),
5146            xycoords="axes fraction",
5147            fontsize=12,
5148        )
5149
5150        ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
5151        ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
5152
5153        # oznaczanie genów
5154        def annotate_outliers(x, y, features):
5155            texts = []
5156
5157            for i, (xi, yi) in enumerate(zip(x, y)):
5158                if data.index[i] in features:
5159                    text = ax.text(xi, yi, data.index[i])
5160                    texts.append(text)
5161
5162            return texts
5163
5164        features = list(set(deg_stats_n["feature"]))
5165
5166        texts = annotate_outliers(data[cell_x], data[cell_y], features)
5167
5168        adjust_text(texts, arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color="gray", alpha=0.5))
5169
5170        return deg_stats, fig

Perform linear regression between two selected cell populations and identify significant and top-ranked differentially expressed genes.

The function compares the expression profiles of two selected cells or cell populations using linear regression. Each gene is represented as a point in the regression plot, with expression in cell_x on the X-axis and expression in cell_y on the Y-axis.

Differential expression statistics are calculated using calc_DEG. Genes are first filtered according to the minimum absolute log fold change, minimum absolute effect size (ESM), and statistical significance. Among the significant genes, up to n_max genes are selected within each valid_group, prioritizing genes with the largest standardized absolute regression residuals and absolute ESM values.

The regression plot uses three point categories:

  • gray: genes that are not statistically significant,
  • green: statistically significant genes that pass the DEG thresholds,
  • blue: top n_max genes selected within each valid_group.

The selected top genes are additionally annotated with their gene names. The plot also displays the fitted linear regression line, R-squared, p-value, and regression equation.

Parameters

cell_x : str Name of the first cell or cell population used as the X-axis.

cell_y : str Name of the second cell or cell population used as the Y-axis.

set_x : str or None Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to cell_x. Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None, the cell is selected only by its name.

set_y : str or None Dataset or experimental set identifier corresponding to cell_y. Required when multiple datasets contain the same cell name. If None, the cell is selected only by its name.

min_log : float, default=0.5 Minimum absolute log fold change required for a gene to be considered for significant DEG selection.

n_max : int, default=20 Maximum number of top genes selected from each valid_group. Genes are ranked primarily by standardized absolute regression residual and secondarily by absolute Effect Size - Cohen's d.

min_exp : float, default=0.1 Minimum expression threshold passed to calc_DEG.

min_pct : float, default=0.5 Minimum fraction of cells in which a gene must be expressed, passed to calc_DEG.

n_proc : int, default=10 Number of parallel processes used by calc_DEG.

min_esm : float, default=0.5 Minimum absolute ESM (effect size measure) required for DEG selection.

p_val : float, default=0.05 Maximum allowed p-value for statistical significance. If adj=True, this threshold is applied to the adjusted p-value (adj_pval); otherwise, it is applied to the raw p-value (p_val).

adj : bool, default=True Whether to use the adjusted p-value (adj_pval) instead of the raw p-value (p_val) for statistical significance filtering.

image_width : int or float, default=12 Width of the regression plot in inches.

image_high : int or float, default=7 Height of the regression plot in inches.

Returns

deg_stats : pandas.DataFrame DataFrame containing the DEG statistics after filtering by absolute log fold change, absolute ESM, and statistical significance.

fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure Matplotlib figure containing the regression plot, including expression points, regression line, regression statistics, and annotations for the selected top genes.

Raises

ValueError If cell_x or cell_y is not found in the dataset.

ValueError If multiple columns correspond to the same cell name and the required dataset identifiers (set_x and/or set_y) were not provided.

Notes

  • The function calls self.average() before performing the analysis.
  • Linear regression is calculated using scipy.stats.linregress.
  • Regression residuals are calculated as the difference between the observed Y value and the value predicted by the fitted regression model.
  • Standardized residuals are used to prioritize genes that deviate most strongly from the expected linear relationship.
  • Significant genes are filtered using absolute log fold change, absolute ESM, and either raw or adjusted p-value.
  • Top genes are selected separately within each valid_group.
  • The top genes are annotated on the regression plot.
  • The returned deg_stats contains the significant genes before the final n_max per-group selection.

Examples

deg_stats, fig = obj.cell_regression( ... cell_x="NeuronA", ... cell_y="NeuronB", ... min_log_min=0.5, ... min_esm=0.5, ... p_val=0.05, ... n_max=20 ... )

def cell_genes_distribution( self, cells_names: list | None, cells_sets: list | None = None, image_width=10, image_high=7): 
5172    def cell_genes_distribution(

Compare the distributions of the number of detected genes per cell across selected cell populations.

For each selected cell population, the function calculates the number of detected genes in each cell, defined as the number of genes with an expression value greater than zero. The resulting distributions are visualized as overlapping histograms, allowing the gene detection levels of different cell populations to be compared.

This analysis can be used as a quality-control step before comparing gene expression profiles or performing differential expression analysis. Similar distributions of detected genes per cell indicate comparable levels of gene detection across the selected populations, whereas substantial differences may indicate differences in sequencing depth, RNA content, or other technical factors.

Parameters

cells_names : list List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.

cells_sets : list or None Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding element-wise to cells_names. This is required when the same cell population name occurs in multiple datasets and a specific dataset needs to be selected.

image_width : int or float, default=10 Width of the histogram figure in inches.

image_high : int or float, default=7 Height of the histogram figure in inches.

Returns

fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure Matplotlib figure containing overlapping histograms showing the distribution of the number of detected genes per cell for each selected cell population.

Raises

ValueError If cells_names is None or empty.

Notes

  • A gene is considered detected when its expression value is greater than zero.
  • The number of detected genes is calculated independently for every cell.
  • Each selected cell population is represented by a separate histogram.
  • When cells_sets is provided and has the same length as cells_names, cell populations are selected using both their population name and dataset identifier.
  • The function operates on self.normalized_data.
  • The resulting distributions can be used to assess whether selected cell populations have comparable gene-detection levels before downstream comparisons.

5288        values are included in the calculation.

5290        The resulting mean and median expression values are visualized as a grouped

5293        expression level and distribution between selected cell populations.

5296        ----------
5297        cells_names : list
5298            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5299
5300        cells_sets : list or None
5301            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5302            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5303            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5304            name and dataset identifier.
5305
5306        non_include_zeros : bool, default=True
5307            Whether to exclude zero-expression values before calculating the mean and
5308            median. If True, only non-zero expression values are used. If False, all
5309            expression values, including zeros, are used.
5310
5311        image_width : int or float, default=7
5312            Width of the figure in inches.
5313
5314        image_high : int or float, default=10
5315            Height of the figure in inches.

5317        Returns

5321            expression for each selected cell population.

5324        ------

5331        * The mean and median are calculated independently for each selected cell

5333        * When `non_include_zeros=True`, zero-expression values are excluded before

5338        * The resulting statistics describe the overall distribution of expression

5341        """
5342
5343        metadata = self.input_metadata
5344        data = self.normalized_data
5345
5346        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5347            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5348
5349        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5350            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5351            full_cells = []
5352            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5353                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])

5360

Compare the mean and median gene expression across selected cell populations.

For each selected cell population, the function calculates the mean and median expression values across all genes and cells. By default, zero-expression values are excluded from the calculation, allowing the comparison to focus on genes with detected expression. When non_include_zeros is set to False, zero values are included in the calculation.

The resulting mean and median expression values are visualized as a grouped bar plot, with separate bars representing the mean and median for each cell population. This visualization can be used to assess differences in the overall expression level and distribution between selected cell populations.

Parameters

cells_names : list List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.

cells_sets : list or None Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding element-wise to cells_names. When provided and its length matches cells_names, cell populations are selected using both their population name and dataset identifier.

non_include_zeros : bool, default=True Whether to exclude zero-expression values before calculating the mean and median. If True, only non-zero expression values are used. If False, all expression values, including zeros, are used.

image_width : int or float, default=7 Width of the figure in inches.

image_high : int or float, default=10 Height of the figure in inches.

Returns

fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure Matplotlib figure containing grouped bar plots showing the mean and median expression for each selected cell population.

Raises

ValueError If cells_names is None or empty.

Notes

  • Expression values are obtained from self.normalized_data.
  • The mean and median are calculated independently for each selected cell population.
  • When non_include_zeros=True, zero-expression values are excluded before calculating both statistics.
  • When non_include_zeros=False, zero-expression values contribute to both the mean and median.
  • The analysis uses all genes and cells belonging to each selected population.
  • The resulting statistics describe the overall distribution of expression values and can be used to compare the expression levels of different cell populations.
def cell_dispersion( self, cells_names: list | None, cells_sets: list | None, image_width=7, image_high=10): 
5398    def cell_dispersion(
5399        self,
5400        cells_names: list | None,
5401        cells_sets: list | None,
5402        image_width=7,
5403        image_high=10,
5404    ):
5405        """
5406        Assess the within-cluster dispersion of cell gene expression profiles.
5407
5408        For each selected cell population, the function calculates the centroid of
5409        the population as the mean expression profile across all cells in the cluster.
5410        The Euclidean distance between each individual cell and its corresponding
5411        cluster centroid is then calculated to quantify how much the cell's expression
5412        profile deviates from the average profile of the cluster.
5413
5414        The resulting distributions of distances are visualized using violin plots,
5415        with each violin representing one selected cell population. The distribution
5416        shows the degree of transcriptional heterogeneity within each cluster:
5417        smaller distances indicate cells with more similar expression profiles,
5418        whereas larger distances indicate greater within-cluster variability.
5419
5420        This analysis can be used to assess the internal consistency and transcriptional
5421        heterogeneity of cell populations before comparing their expression profiles
5422        between clusters.
5423
5424        Parameters
5425        ----------
5426        self : object
5427            self object containing the input metadata and normalized expression
5428            data.
5429
5430        cells_names : list
5431            List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.
5432
5433        cells_sets : list or None
5434            Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding
5435            element-wise to `cells_names`. When provided and its length matches
5436            `cells_names`, cell populations are selected using both their population
5437            name and dataset identifier.
5438
5439        image_width : int or float, default=7
5440            Width of the figure in inches.
5441
5442        image_high : int or float, default=10
5443            Height of the figure in inches.
5444
5445        Returns
5446        -------
5447        fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure
5448            Matplotlib figure containing violin plots showing the distribution of
5449            Euclidean distances between individual cells and their respective cluster
5450            centroids.
5451
5452        Raises
5453        ------
5454        ValueError
5455            If `cells_names` is None or empty.
5456
5457        Notes
5458        -----
5459        * Expression values are obtained from `self.normalized_data`.
5460        * A cluster centroid is calculated as the mean expression profile across all
5461        cells belonging to that cluster.
5462        * The distance of each cell from the centroid is calculated using Euclidean
5463        distance across all genes.
5464        * Each cell contributes one distance value to the distribution of its cluster.
5465        * Smaller distances indicate lower within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5466        * Larger distances indicate greater within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
5467        * The violin plot includes a box plot showing the median and interquartile
5468        range of the distance distribution.
5469        * Differences in dispersion between clusters can be used to assess their
5470        relative transcriptional homogeneity before downstream comparisons.
5471        """
5472
5473        metadata = self.input_metadata
5474        data = self.normalized_data
5475
5476        if cells_names is None or len(cells_names) == 0:
5477            raise ValueError("No cells selected!")
5478
5479        if cells_sets is not None and len(cells_sets) == len(cells_names):
5480            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"] + " # " + metadata["sets"]
5481            full_cells = []
5482            for n in range(len(cells_names)):
5483                full_cells.append(cells_names[n] + " # " + cells_sets[n])
5484
5485            data = data.loc[:, full_cells]
5486
5487        else:
5488            data.columns = metadata["cell_names"]
5489            data = data.loc[:, cells_names]
5490
5491        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(image_width, image_high))
5492
5493        dispersion_long = []
5494
5495        for cluster in data.columns.unique():
5496
5497            cells = data.loc[:, data.columns == cluster]
5498
5499            centroid = cells.mean(axis=1)
5500
5501            distances = np.sqrt(((cells.sub(centroid, axis=0)) ** 2).sum(axis=0))
5502
5503            for cell, distance in distances.items():
5504                dispersion_long.append(
5505                    {"cluster": cluster, "cell": cell, "distance_to_centroid": distance}
5506                )
5507
5508        dispersion_long = pd.DataFrame(dispersion_long)
5509
5510        sns.violinplot(
5511            data=dispersion_long, x="cluster", y="distance_to_centroid", inner="box"
5512        )
5513
5514        plt.ylabel("Distance from cluster centroid")
5515        plt.xlabel("Cluster")
5516        plt.xticks(rotation=45)
5517        plt.tight_layout()
5518
5519        return fig

Assess the within-cluster dispersion of cell gene expression profiles.

For each selected cell population, the function calculates the centroid of the population as the mean expression profile across all cells in the cluster. The Euclidean distance between each individual cell and its corresponding cluster centroid is then calculated to quantify how much the cell's expression profile deviates from the average profile of the cluster.

The resulting distributions of distances are visualized using violin plots, with each violin representing one selected cell population. The distribution shows the degree of transcriptional heterogeneity within each cluster: smaller distances indicate cells with more similar expression profiles, whereas larger distances indicate greater within-cluster variability.

This analysis can be used to assess the internal consistency and transcriptional heterogeneity of cell populations before comparing their expression profiles between clusters.

Parameters

self : object self object containing the input metadata and normalized expression data.

cells_names : list List of cell population or cluster names to be included in the analysis.

cells_sets : list or None Optional list of dataset or experimental set identifiers corresponding element-wise to cells_names. When provided and its length matches cells_names, cell populations are selected using both their population name and dataset identifier.

image_width : int or float, default=7 Width of the figure in inches.

image_high : int or float, default=10 Height of the figure in inches.

Returns

fig : matplotlib.figure.Figure Matplotlib figure containing violin plots showing the distribution of Euclidean distances between individual cells and their respective cluster centroids.

Raises

ValueError If cells_names is None or empty.

Notes

  • Expression values are obtained from self.normalized_data.
  • A cluster centroid is calculated as the mean expression profile across all cells belonging to that cluster.
  • The distance of each cell from the centroid is calculated using Euclidean distance across all genes.
  • Each cell contributes one distance value to the distribution of its cluster.
  • Smaller distances indicate lower within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
  • Larger distances indicate greater within-cluster transcriptional dispersion.
  • The violin plot includes a box plot showing the median and interquartile range of the distance distribution.
  • Differences in dispersion between clusters can be used to assess their relative transcriptional homogeneity before downstream comparisons.
